532720|2026-06.headline: Mahindra Finance Q1 FY27: standalone PAT up 70% YoY, ROA 2.4%, GS3 at 3.45%, credit cost 1.5%, AUM growth 13%.
532720|2026-06.overview: Management reported a strong Q1 FY27 with standalone profit up 70% YoY and consolidated PAT up 75% YoY to INR 927 crores. Asset quality improved to an eight-year low on GS3 (3.45%) and GS2+GS3 (8.3%), with credit cost at 1.5% and ROA at 2.4%. Wheels business grew about 20% and non-wheels grew 79%, while AUM grew 13% overall. Management kept an extra liquidity buffer of about INR 5,000-5,500 crores and two management overlays as protection against El Nino, monsoon and geopolitical risks, which weighed on loan yield and gross spread.

financial_highlights.change: from 1.94% in Q4 FY26 (June-to-June basis as stated)

financial_highlights.value: close to INR 15,000 crores in Q1

financial_highlights.change: from 2.8% QoQ; down about 10 bps YoY

financial_highlights.value: growth 83% YoY (MIBL PAT up 38% QoQ as stated)

segments.name: Wheels (PV, tractor, CV, 3-wheeler)
segments.commentary: Wheels grew about 20% as stated in the call and about 11-12% AUM compounding per management's framing. Share gains in PV, 3-wheeler and tractor; CV share lost in HCV and fleet, gained in SCV and LCV.

segments.name: Non-wheels (SME, mortgage, PL, others)
segments.commentary: Non-wheels grew 79% per management; SME grew 30%, others (PL, implements) grew 77%, and non-wheels AUM is compounding at 28-30%. Mortgage growth above 100% from a small base.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: Reported PAT of INR 30 crores for the quarter. Affordable housing is the core; prime housing started in a calibrated manner.

segments.name: Insurance broking (MIBL)
segments.commentary: PAT growth of 83% YoY. Expanding beyond motor into reinsurance and commercial lines.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term NIM target: above 7.1%.
Credit cost band of 1.3% to 1.7% through the cycle; management expects the lower end if execution holds, but no full-year call.
AUM CAGR of 16-18% over FY26-FY31, with wheels at about 12% and non-wheels at 30%+.
No yearly ROA guidance; path remains 2% toward 2.2% and eventually 2.5%.
Cost of funds expected to stay within roughly 10 bps plus or minus of the current level.
No new capital needed for at least the next 6-8 quarters; leverage could rise to 6x-plus debt to equity.
capex_capacity: Udaan digital stack covers 100% of wheels disbursements; LOS on Salesforce and LMS on FinnOne.
Manpower has stayed roughly flat over the last 2-3 years while productivity improved.
Samur.AI agentic CPC coverage rose from 20% to 45%; AI vernacular bots coverage rose to 20% of collections.
Digital and AI-led acquisition shows about 25% lower cost of acquisition.
Liquidity buffer raised to about INR 5,500 crores (about INR 5,000 crores still held as of July).
demand_pricing: Wheels growth around 20% in Q1; market share gains in PV (entry-level post GST), tractor (share widening), and 3-wheelers. CV share lost in HCV and fleet segments.
Tractor Q1 was strong because delayed monsoon extended the pre-kharif buying cycle; management expects Q2 may be softer as a result.
Mahindra Group share of AUM at 46% across PV, CV, tractor and 3-wheelers; management says no discriminatory scorecards for group vs non-group.
Loan yields fell about 25 bps QoQ, mainly from denominator effect of the enlarged liquidity buffer per management.
Management says it is tightening entry bars for SME and logistics operators and increasing skin in the game in tractors.

qa_highlights.question: Where will the ROA close FY27 and how sustainable is asset quality given monsoon and El Nino risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give yearly ROA guidance. It cited an extreme monitoring framework by geography, collection squads, and tighter entry bars for vulnerable segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will the elevated liquidity buffer stay, and what is the cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 5,000 crores of extra buffer is held and will be unwound when conditions stabilise. Cost of funds rose about 10 bps QoQ, expected to stay within roughly 10 bps either way.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the housing subsidiary and the insurance commission regulation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Board decision on housing structure is due by Q2 FY27. Insurance income is from basic credit and protection products, so management sees limited exposure to the expected IRDAI commission rules.

qa_highlights.question: What is the credit cost outlook and how much can AI reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1.3-1.7% through the cycle; at 1.5% now it expects the lower end if execution holds. AI is not expected to shift the band materially.

qa_highlights.question: How will AUM growth reach 16-18% CAGR and does it need acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 16-18% CAGR (not a 18-20% exit rate), with wheels at about 12% and non-wheels at 30%+, and no new capital needed for 6-8 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vehicle unit growth lag the industry in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PV unit share was lost by exiting low-IRR premium segments, while entry-level PV and SCV/LCV share was gained. Tractor units grew well above industry.

risks_watch: Monsoon deficit in Rajasthan, MP and Gujarat; tractor and agri-linked borrowers are most exposed.
Q2 collections and tractor demand, which may soften after the pulled-forward Q1 buying cycle.
Liquidity buffer unwind timing and its effect on loan yield and gross spread.
Pending IRDAI commission rules on insurance fee income.
CV market share loss in HCV and fleet segments; SCV and LCV growth still to show in the numbers.
Housing subsidiary merger or structure decision due by Q2 FY27.
532720|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's numbers and asset quality, but cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined full-year guidance and stressed overlays, monsoon risk and the need to avoid complacency.
key_quotes: I would stand by my earlier guidance of 1.3% to 1.7% overall credit cost.
We don't want to be the last creditor in the list. We'll show up first.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Medium-term NIM target is above 7.1% and credit cost could fall toward 1.3%, but loan yields fell about 25 bps QoQ from the enlarged INR 5,000-5,500 crore liquidity buffer and cost of funds rose about 10 bps QoQ, with unwinding timing undecided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM grew 13% YoY and disbursements were close to INR 15,000 crore in Q1, with non-wheels up 79% and the medium-term AUM CAGR of 16-18% (wheels ~12%, non-wheels 30%+) reiterated, though Q2 tractor demand may soften.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management sees no capital need for at least 6-8 quarters with Tier 1 at 16.5% and leverage allowed to rise to 6x-plus debt to equity, so no new capital raise; capex is not discussed as a capacity build, and the business is digital/AI-led with flat manpower.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it expects the lower end of the 1.3-1.7% credit cost band if execution holds, from 1.5% now, and ROA is on a path from 2.4% toward 2.2% and 2.5%, but no formal upgrade was given.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost at 1.5% sits inside the 1.3-1.7% band, but monsoon deficit in Rajasthan, MP and Gujarat and possible Q2 tractor softness after pulled-forward Q1 buying could push it up; management declined full-year ROA guidance.

rows.label: Opex to average assets at 2.5-2.7% via digital/AI
rows.why: Traditional opex fell to 2.65% from 2.8% QoQ, with manpower flat for 2-3 years, Samur.AI agentic CPC coverage up from 20% to 45%, and digital acquisition cost about 25% lower; management calls 2.5-2.7% a business model requirement.

rows.label: Housing subsidiary structure decision
rows.why: Board decision on housing structure is due by Q2 FY27; the subsidiary reported PAT of INR 30 crore in Q1.

rows.label: IRDAI commission rules on insurance income
rows.why: Rules are pending, but management says insurance income comes from basic credit and protection products, so exposure is limited; MIBL PAT grew 83% YoY.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 profit (standalone PAT up 70%), GS3 at an eight-year low of 3.45%, and the 16-18% AUM CAGR, but cautious on the outlook, declining full-year ROA guidance and stressing monsoon, El Nino and tractor-demand risks; analysts probed ROA trajectory, asset quality under monsoo

532720|2026-09.headline: M&M Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 55% YoY to INR 882 crore, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% and credit cost at 1.6%.
532720|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as steady across growth, margin and risk, with disbursements up 22% YoY and AUM up 15% YoY. Asset quality improved, with GS2+GS3 at 8.1% (near all-time lows) and inter-quarter volatility reduced; credit cost was 1.6% against a 1.3-1.7% guided range. ROA was about 2.2% in the quarter (H1 about 2.3%), dented by excess liquidity buffers and high trade advances, while cost of funds is expected to rise after one 25 bps repo hike with more hikes priced in. Management said it sees no change to its FY31 targets of 16-18% AUM growth, 1.3-1.7% credit cost and 2.2-2.5% ROA.

financial_highlights.value: Growth of 68% YoY (H1 figure as stated)
22% growth; AI-orchestrated disbursements INR 1,663 crore (as stated)

financial_highlights.change: Near all-time low; GS3 down 3 bps and GS2 down 7 bps QoQ (last year's Q1-Q2 comparison as stated)
+5 bps QoQ vs +23 bps last year
Created in Q3-Q4 for El Nino and West Asia risks

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: AUM growth of 28% YoY as stated on the growth-by-category page.

segments.name: Used vehicles
segments.commentary: AUM growth of 15% YoY.

segments.name: CV/CE
segments.commentary: AUM growth of 16% YoY.

segments.name: Tractors
segments.commentary: AUM growth of 13% YoY; tractor is cross-cycle attractive but drought districts are a watch item.

segments.name: Three-wheelers
segments.commentary: AUM growth of 32% YoY.

segments.name: SME
segments.commentary: AUM growth of 13% YoY.

segments.name: Other businesses (mortgage, others)
segments.commentary: Growth of 71% YoY; 'others' bucket rose to 8.2% of AUM from 5.3% in June, largely trade advances plus personal loans and early prime housing.

guidance_outlook: Long-term AUM growth target maintained at 16-18%; management declined to give quarterly or yearly guidance.
Credit cost guided within 1.3-1.7%; no near-term challenge seen and no additional overlay planned at present.
Cost of funds expected to trend upward: a 25 bps hike affects about 10 bps of existing stock within a quarter via floating resets, and refinancing adds further cost.

NIM expected to be challenging; management said it is at the lower end of the 7%+ range needed for 2.2-2.5% ROA. Loan income expected to recover as trade advances and excess liquidity convert into earning assets.
Mahindra Rural Housing Finance merger: appointed date 1 April 2027, effective date targeted June-July 2027, pending NCLT and some regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: Liquidity buffer roughly doubled YoY in rupee terms; management said it could be reduced somewhat if the environment eases.
Mortgage plan: MRHFL has 400 branches and MMFSL 1,400; the HFC is being folded into the parent, with plans for affordable housing, LAP and some prime housing (prime housing started in August).
Headcount rising after two static years to support wheels, SME and mortgage growth; off-roll to on-roll migration program in place.
AI toolkits: 75% of back office covered by enabled workflows; 12 regional AI vernacular bots in call centres. Roughly 10% of disbursements are AI-led, per the question from an analyst.
demand_pricing: Navratri first 10 days: underlying commerce and unit disbursements down YoY, with tractors seeing a somewhat sharper decline; last year's base was inflated by pre-GST-cut demand.
VAHAN registration data showed rural and semi-urban vehicle growth marginally above urban and metro through September.
Pricing: competition is intense in salaried segments (not served). Self-employed agri segments have less competition, leaving room to price incremental wheels loans higher; no broad repricing yet.
Trade advances deliberately raised above normal levels ahead of festive season growth.

Insurance: a draft consultation paper may cut fee income from motor insurance (MIBL) and corporate agency; fee income had risen from 1% to 1.6% of assets, partly from insurance. Quantification deferred until the final regulation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost-of-funds trajectory for FY27 given the rate hike and liquidity holdings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects cost of funds to rise after one 25 bps hike and more priced in; a 25 bps move resets about 10 bps of floating stock within a quarter. Refinancing is at higher rates. Some liquidity buffer flexibility exists but not large.

qa_highlights.question: Credit cost trajectory after a flat H1 with no seasonality: could it drop below 1.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 1.3-1.7%, citing existing stock keeping H2 GS3 stable and rural cash flows improving in Q3-Q4. The INR 852 crore overlay is adequate and no further buffer is planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Is the trade advance increase in others (8.2% of AUM) driving growth visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, trade advances were deployed at a clear level above normal to support Q3 festive growth. Personal loans to existing customers are also building; prime housing started in August and will be disclosed separately later.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on tractor collections in drought-affected states such as Maharashtra?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to call: tractor half-yearly instalments fall due at end of rabi/kharif and collections are not yet at that point. Teams are assessing stress case by case; management does not plan to change its tractor stance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the housing finance merger and mortgage push change returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Mortgage is an early drag on ROA but seen as strategic; management noted the HFC-NBFC cost-of-funds arbitrage is narrowing and cited the merger rationale of simplifying duplicated functions.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM fall below 7% in coming quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM expansion will be hard; loan income should recover as trade advances and excess liquidity convert, and fee income has some headroom. Half-year loan income reflects the run-rate better than Q2 alone.

risks_watch: Drought in 3 states and 282 drought-prone districts could raise tractor stress, especially after the half-yearly collection cycle.
Further repo hikes and refinancing at higher rates may compress NIM before loan repricing (fixed-rate vehicle book).
The draft insurance consultation paper could reduce fee income from MIBL and corporate agency.
Navratri demand softness versus a high base; H2 disbursement growth is uncertain against last year's strong H2.
Liquidity buffer and trade advances are drags on ROA until they convert into earning assets.
532720|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and operating metrics, but cautious on near-term cost of funds, NIM, festive demand and insurance regulation. Management was evasive on disclosing book maturity and segment-level details, and declined quarterly or yearly guidance.
key_quotes: And I'm happy to report that the overall lending AUM, which is at INR 1,56,000 crores now you have a 20% coming in from the non-wheels and 80% from the wheels.
So, we are a franchise that wants to grow in the high teens as we say.
The PAT growth is not, is not sustainable at the 70% levels.
We will not chase any growth at the cost of either price or risk.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says NIM will be challenging and sits at the lower end of the 7%+ range needed for 2.2-2.5% ROA, while cost of funds rises after a 25 bps repo hike (about 10 bps of floating stock resets within a quarter) and 45-48% of borrowings are floating; loan income recovery from trade advances and excess liquidity is the only offset.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No discrete plant or capacity figures given; headcount is rising after two static years and MRHFL's 400 branches fold into MMFSL's 1,400, with prime housing started in August, but nothing is dated or quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM grew 15% YoY to about INR 1,56,000 crore and disbursements rose 22% YoY in Q2, with PV AUM +28%, 3W +32% and non-wheels +52%, and the 16-18% medium-to-long-term AUM target was held, though H2 festive demand is softer after Navratri.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed and there is no utilisation figure; the business is asset-light, so a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give quarterly or yearly guidance, held the FY31 targets unchanged, and flagged NIM and cost-of-funds headwinds, so an upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost of 1.6% sits within the 1.3-1.7% range, but drought stress in 3 states and 282 drought-prone districts could hit tractor collections after the half-yearly cycle, and the draft insurance rule could cut fee income.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Prime housing started in August with disclosure to come later, affordable housing and LAP are planned, and personal loans to existing customers are building, though no dates or sizes were given.

rows.label: Excess liquidity buffer may be reduced
rows.why: Liquidity buffer roughly doubled YoY and management said it could be reduced if the environment eases, which would convert idle funds into earning assets and lift ROA from 2.2%.

rows.label: MRHFL merger into MMFSL
rows.why: Merger is approved, with pending NCLT and some regulatory approvals, and MRHFL's PAT was INR 35 crore for the subsidiary.

rows.label: Draft insurance consultation paper
rows.why: A draft could cut fee income from motor insurance (MIBL) and corporate agency, with fee income having risen from 1% to 1.6% of assets, but quantification is deferred until the final rule.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality (GS2+GS3 8.1%, credit cost 1.6%) and cost-to-income under 37%, but cautious on cost of funds, NIM, festive demand and insurance regulation; analysts pushed on credit cost below 1.5%, NIM below 7%, tractor stress and trade advances in others.

532725|2026-03.headline: Solar Industries Q4 FY26 revenue hit record INR3,053 crore (+41% YoY) with EBITDA INR870 crore at ~28.5% margin; FY27 revenue target INR14,000 crore.
532725|2026-03.overview: Solar Industries reported record quarterly and annual sales of INR3,053 crore and INR9,838 crore, with Q4 EBITDA up 59% YoY to INR870 crore and PAT up 61% to INR556 crore. Defence revenue nearly doubled, reaching INR1,008 crore in Q4 (+134% YoY) and INR2,634 crore for FY26 (+94%). Management guided to INR14,000 crore revenue in FY27 while maintaining current EBITDA margins, backed by a INR21,300 crore order book. Working capital days rose above the 90-100 day range in Q4 on deliberate inventory build, which management expects to normalise over about two quarters.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2,167 crore in Q4 FY25 (+41%)
vs INR546 crore in Q4 FY25 (+59%)
vs INR346 crore in Q4 FY25 (+61%)
vs INR464 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR21,300 crore (c. INR18,000 crore defence, c. INR3,000 crore non-defence)

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,008 crore (+134% YoY) and FY26 INR2,634 crore (+94%). Management expects defence revenue to cross INR4,500 crore in FY27; the order book is about INR18,000 crore, mainly Pinaka-related.

segments.name: International / export
segments.commentary: Grew 32% YoY in FY26 to about INR3,800 crore. Share of basket was 33% in Q4 (from 36%) and 39% for FY26 (from 38%). Q4 international revenue was about INR1,000 crore, similar to the prior quarter. Management guides about 30% growth in FY27.

segments.name: Domestic mining (CIL, non-CIL, housing and infra)
segments.commentary: CIL share of basket fell to 9% (from 13%) for FY26. Non-CIL and institutional was 12% (from 15%) and housing and infra 12% (from 15%) for the year. Management says domestic mining demand was flat in FY26, with roughly 4% value growth, and expects a pick-up in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of INR14,000 crore while maintaining current EBITDA margins (around 27-28% for FY26).
Ex-defence revenue implied at about INR9,500 crore for FY27, with domestic and international growing about 30%: roughly 10-15% volume and 18-20% price.
Defence revenue expected to cross INR4,500 crore in FY27.
International growth expected at about 30% in FY27; long-run volume growth about 10% and value growth about 15%.
Planned FY27 capex of INR2,050 crore, after about INR2,700 crore invested over the last two years.
Dividend of INR11 per share proposed for FY26-27, up from INR10.
Working capital days expected to normalise over about the next two quarters once geopolitical uncertainty eases.
capex_capacity: FY27 planned capex of INR2,050 crore; management did not split it between defence and non-defence, saying the business is one and capex is prioritised by opportunity.
Recent expansion in Northern India through an acquisition; mega expansion in Western India just completed; new plants planned in East and South India, including Odisha and Telangana/Andhra Pradesh.

Africa: facilities in South Africa (hub), Zambia, Tanzania and Zimbabwe; Nigeria base with Ghana operational; Sierra Leone expected this year. Turkey base and Kazakhstan plant started. Small facilities in Thailand and Indonesia; Australia to start soon.
Medium-calibre ammunition facility commissioned and supplying samples for qualification.
155 mm: raw material intermediates already being supplied; coupling facility to complete the full round in the next couple of quarters, then 3-4 months before full-round supply begins.
demand_pricing: Domestic mining: FY26 OB removal was negative across Coal India, Singareni and private mines, yet domestic value grew about 4%; management expects FY27 pick-up as the shift to electric-based mining grows.
FY27 price contribution of 18-20% is expected from higher crude and gas prices feeding upstream and downstream products; volume growth expected at 10-15%.

Working capital build in Q4 was deliberate inventory stocking against geopolitical risk; management expects inventory gains in coming quarters and says rise-and-fall clauses cover only about 60% of commodity increases, with some contracts passing through after a quarter.
Ammonium nitrate price spike may cause a demand contraction for a couple of months; management does not expect an annual impact.
Management declined to give market share data for exports and dismissed concern over a possible Kalyani Group entry, saying it is not afraid of competition.

qa_highlights.question: Which new geographies are being targeted for international growth in FY27 (Zimbabwe and others)?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on Africa, with South Africa as hub and facilities in Zambia, Tanzania and Zimbabwe; Nigeria base with Ghana started; Sierra Leone expected this year. Turkey and Kazakhstan are also active, with Southeast Asia and Australia smaller.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Bhargavastra counter-drone system and 155 mm shell qualification?
qa_highlights.answer: Bhargavastra final-stage development; all trials expected in calendar 2026. 155 mm complete-round supply expected after the coupling facility is done in a couple of quarters plus 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Can exports grow 2-3x in the medium term, and what investment is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Export revenue has grown from about INR800 crore (2018-21 plateau) to about INR3,800 crore now. Management would not give a multiple, but expects about 30% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the implied domestic growth (about 35%) for FY27 mainly low-base recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 growth of 30%+ across domestic and international combines 10-15% volume and 18-20% price, driven by commodity prices; mining demand expected to recover after a flat FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins hold given cost inflation and rising defence mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price rises have been taken and rise-and-fall clauses exist, but a small margin impact is expected; higher defence and international mix should let margins be maintained at current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why were subsidiary earnings so low in FY26 (about INR50 crore), and what drove the working capital build?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence and international subsidiaries were subdued in H1 FY26 and improved from Q3, strong in Q4. Working capital days rose above the 90-100 range on inventory built to hedge geopolitical risk; normalisation expected in about two quarters.

risks_watch: Commodity price pass-through lag: rise-and-fall covers only about 60% of input increases, so Q1 FY27 margins could be squeezed before contract escalations catch up.
Working capital days elevated in Q4 on inventory build; watch normalisation over the next two quarters.
Defence execution: Bhargavastra and 155 mm timelines have slipped before, and the order book is concentrated in Pinaka-related orders.
West Asia freight and logistics headwinds; international revenue was flat sequentially at about INR1,000 crore.
Possible demand softness from high ammonium nitrate prices for a couple of months; possible competitive entry from Kalyani Group.
Subsidiary profit contribution was only about INR50 crore in FY26 despite the large revenue base; the improvement needs to continue.
532725|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, defence and FY27 targets, but guarded on specific product timelines and market share, which management said it avoids discussing. Management acknowledged a margin impact from commodity costs and an inventory-led working capital build.
key_quotes: Dear investors, our defense business has nearly doubled.
And we should cross defense revenue of INR4,500 crores in FY '27.
So this time, we are confident that we should be able to manage this situation with the help of improved defense as well as international business.
So we run business as a whole, and we don't wish on quarter-to-quarter basis.

rows.why: Management guides to maintaining current EBITDA margins of ~27-28% (FY26 27.95%, Q4 28.5%) despite commodity cost inflation, with a 18-20% price contribution and rising defence/international mix supporting the level; expansion beyond current levels is not guided, so this is margin maintenance rather than expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 155 mm coupling facility completes in about 2 quarters with full-round supply 3-4 months after that, Sierra Leone facility expected this year, and East/South India plants (Odisha, Telangana/AP) are planned; FY27 capex of INR2,050 crore is earmarked, though no split or specific plant dates were given for the 14,000 crore revenue target.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 10-15% volume growth in FY27 with defence revenue crossing INR4,500 crore (from INR2,634 crore, +71%) and international growing ~30% from ~INR3,800 crore, backed by an INR21,300 crore order book (~INR18,000 crore defence).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Planned FY27 capex of INR2,050 crore after about INR2,700 crore over the last two years, with East and South India plants still to be detailed, implies further project announcements; utilisation rose but no figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management set FY27 revenue at INR14,000 crore (~42% growth on INR9,838 crore) with no sign of a raise; the call gave no conservative-beat signal, and the 42% target already relies on 18-20% price.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rise-and-fall clauses cover only about 60% of commodity increases so Q1 FY27 margins could be squeezed, the 155 mm and Bhargavastra timelines have slipped before, and West Asia freight hit international revenue, which was flat at about INR1,000 crore in Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Medium-calibre ammunition is supplying samples for qualification, 155 mm full-round supply follows coupling completion in about 2 quarters plus 3-4 months, and Bhargavastra counter-drone trials are all expected in calendar 2026.

rows.label: Working capital days normalise from above 90-100
rows.why: Q4 inventory build was deliberate against geopolitical risk, and management expects inventory gains and normalisation within about two quarters.

rows.label: INR21,300 crore order book (c. INR18,000 crore defence)
rows.why: The order book equals about 2.2x FY26 revenue of INR9,838 crore and covers much of the INR14,000 crore FY27 target, with defence concentrated in Pinaka-related orders.

rows.label: Africa expansion: Sierra Leone, Ghana, Nigeria, Australia
rows.why: International revenue grew 32% to about INR3,800 crore in FY26 and management guides ~30% growth in FY27, with Sierra Leone expected this year and Australia starting soon.

tone.note: Management was confident on the INR14,000 crore FY27 target, defence above INR4,500 crore and maintaining margins, but guarded on product timelines and declined to give market share data; analysts probed the implied ~35% domestic growth and margin resilience to cost inflation.

532725|2026-06.headline: Solar Industries to acquire Omnia Holdings (South Africa) on an all-cash, 100% basis, funded by debt; ~$1.35bn deal value cited, FY28 leverage target below 2x EBITDA.
532725|2026-06.overview: This was a business update call on the proposed acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings Limited by Solar SA Investments (wholly owned step-down subsidiary), held as a transaction-only call, with no questions on core Solar operations taken. Management framed the deal as creating an integrated global explosives and blasting platform, adding mining (BME brand) and agriculture/agritech businesses, with benefits expected to be visible from FY28. Funding will be all-cash, through debt at Omnia level plus Solar-group debt and internal accruals, with no equity issuance planned. Management guided to combined FY28 revenue of about INR30,000-32,000 crore and EBITDA of INR6,800-7,000 crore, and said net debt/EBITDA will stay below 2x. Many figures are management estimates pending shareholder and regulatory approvals, and structuring is not finalised.

532726|2026-09.headline: Gallantt Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR111 crores (9.64% margin) from INR185 crores in Q1 on Gorakhpur shutdowns and power outage, with revenue flat at INR1,146 crores.
532726|2026-09.overview: Revenue held at INR1,146 crores, up 13% year on year and flat quarter on quarter, as realisations offset lower volumes. TMT sales fell to 1,65,000 tons from about 1,92,000 tons in Q1 because of a planned Gorakhpur shutdown, and an unplanned extension of a captive power plant outage raised power costs. EBITDA margin compressed to 9.64% from 16.19% in Q1, and PAT fell to INR61 crores. Management attributes the hit to one-time factors and expects recovery from the Gorakhpur capacity ramp-up, power plant restart and higher steel prices in Q3. Coal block allotment in Singrauli and a medium-term greenfield growth plan (to be presented in Q4 FY27) were the main strategic updates.

segments.name: Kutch (Gujarat)

532732|2026-09.headline: Kewal Kiran Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 5% YoY to INR373 crore, with EBITDA up 12% to INR80 crore; management now guides only to double-digit FY27 growth, not 15%.
532732|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 5% YoY to INR373 crore, EBITDA grew 12% to INR80 crore (21% margin) and PAT rose 15% to INR54 crore. Management attributed a 3-4% revenue hit in Q2 to Vapi/Daman floods, plus festive shift of Diwali/Puja into Q3. Vision 2028 store targets were revised (total EBOs to 800 from 900, Lawman cut to 125 from 175, Kraus raised to 75 from 50, K-Lounge phased out), while revenue and profit targets were kept. Killer half-year SSG was reported at negative 10%, and management reduced its confidence in the 15% FY27 growth target.

financial_highlights.metric: Retail vs non-retail sales mix (Q2 FY27)

financial_highlights.change: In line with last year per management

segments.name: Killer
segments.commentary: Now operates 477 exclusive brand outlets; half-yearly EBO SSG was negative 10%. Store size is shifting to 800-1,000 sq ft, and store count is unchanged in the Vision 2028 revision.

segments.name: Kraus
segments.commentary: Grew over 25% YoY in Q2 on expansion and SSG. EBITDA margin said to be in line with KKCL. Store target raised from 50 to 75; early exports to Middle East and online traction, with MBO format just started.

segments.name: Lawman
segments.commentary: Re-strategised as a D2C-led, more retail- and online-focused brand. Store target cut from 175 to 125, with focus on larger, higher-quality stores.

segments.name: Integriti
segments.commentary: Delivered double-digit growth in H1 FY27 after its revamp; management said it had expected a larger outcome.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth: management says it is committed to double-digit revenue growth by year-end but is 'not too sure' of 15%; the earlier view was about 15% organic plus about 5% inorganic.
Retail SSG for nine months expected to be roughly flat, after H1 retail SSG of about negative 10%; the full-year SSG figure was not given.
Vision 2028 revenue and profitability targets retained; EBO target 800 by FY28 (Killer unchanged, Lawman 125, Kraus 75; K-Lounge excluded).
EBITDA margin: no incremental margin expected from store rationalisation; margins described as above industry average.

Price increases taken in the current two quarters; inflation pressure expected in Q3 and Q4, to be passed through by reducing discounts or raising MRP.
capex_capacity: Vapi and Daman factories were disrupted by floods for about 7-10 days, which hit production; management also cited oil and gas price impacts on production.
Store format shift: from 600-800 sq ft to 1,000-1,200+ sq ft stores, aimed at more category depth (kids wear, blazers, winter wear) and throughput per store.
Incremental store-size investment is mainly rental; most stores are franchisee-operated.
Goregaon and Gautam Chemical Compound properties: 'as is where is', no new investment; FSI approval pending. Market value not disclosed.

Core competitors for Killer named as Levi's, Lee, Wrangler, Mufti, Pepe and Spykar; management says pricing is in line with these brands.
Apparel quantity and realisation both rose YoY per management; total unit volume fell due to accessories and personal care mix.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Vapi flood on Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put the Q2 revenue impact at 3-4%.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 be 15% growth or early double-digit?

qa_highlights.answer: Stores were cut to 800 with larger formats; Lawman was cut to 125 and Kraus raised to 75; K-Lounge is being phased out over time, with single-brand formats and Junior Killer as a sub-part of Killer.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said no major incremental EBITDA margin is expected, as the increase is mainly rent and a share of revenue goes to franchisees; throughput per store should be better.

Working capital at about 130 days with higher inventory into Q3; watch receivables and inventory build for discount pressure.
Monsoon and flood disruption to manufacturing; supply chain resilience at Vapi and Daman.

532734|2026-03.headline: GPIL FY26 consolidated EBITDA flat at INR 1,253 crore, but Q4 EBITDA rose 91% QoQ to INR 439 crore; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 24-25%.
532734|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue and PAT were broadly stable, with consolidated PAT at INR 802 crore and EBITDA margin at 23%. Q4 FY26 revenue grew 41% QoQ and PAT reached INR 280 crore, driven by higher pellet volumes, a one-time carry-over pellet inventory gain (about INR 20 crore) and March mining uplift after environmental clearance for Ari Dongri. Consolidated PAT was below standalone because Ardent Steel was de-recognised as an associate after the stake sale. Management guided FY27 revenue above INR 6,000 crore and EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels, while flagging price softness of about 10% in late April and early May.

segments.name: Iron ore mining (Ari Dongri / Boria Tibu)
segments.commentary: FY26 mining achieved 92% of target; FY26 mining was about 2.7-2.8 million tons versus 2.35-2.4 million tons in FY25. FY27 usable ore guidance is 3.4 million tons (4-4.25 million tons mined, including about 0.5 million tons from Boria Tibu).

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: FY26 pellet output reached 95% of target. Pellet capacity rose from 2.7 to 4.7 million tons after the 2 million ton gas-based grate-kiln plant commissioned in December 2025; FY27 pellet guidance is 4 million tons, with about 3 million tons for merchant sales.

segments.name: Sponge iron
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26. Capacity is being expanded from 0.59 to 0.65 million tons under a CTO received from CECB.

segments.name: Structural rolled products / RR Ispat
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26 and rose sharply from Q4 after mill modifications finished at end-Q3; order book is about six months. Total FY27 rolled output is guided at about 3.7-3.75 lakh tons.

segments.name: Ferroalloys
segments.commentary: Production exceeded 100% of plan in FY26; no further figures given on the call.

segments.name: Galvanised / fabricated products and billets
segments.commentary: Billets reached 96% of target in FY26; sales volumes for galvanised fabricated products increased over the year.

segments.name: BESS (20 GWh project)
segments.commentary: Commissioning targeted March 2027, with long-term supply tie-ups with EVE Power (628 Ah LFP cells) and Shanghai Shenyi Roche. Phase-1 ramp is 5-6 GWh in FY28 (30-40%), about 12-14 GWh in FY29 and 17-18 GWh from FY30. Management guided a 7-8% margin, but said current margins are about 12-13%.

segments.name: CRM complex (0.7 million tons)
segments.commentary: Targeted commissioning March 2027; FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation, or 3-3.5 lakh tons. Management expects about 90% from FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue to cross INR 6,000 crore, driven by the new pellet plant running at 80-90% of capacity.
FY27 EBITDA margin of 24-25% at current market levels; management said it expects to maintain about 25%.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant (6 million tons) to be commissioned by Q3 FY27; full-scale mining of 6 million tons in FY28, with about 4.5 million tons of usable ore.
Capex guidance: about INR 1,500-2,000 crore in FY27, and about INR 3,000 crore each in FY28 and FY29, mainly for the steel plant.

Vision 2031 (per the presentation): steel, BESS (Phase-1) and CRM revenue are included. Management said PAT of about INR 3,000 crore implies a margin of about 10%, reflecting lower-margin BESS and CRM. Phase-2 BESS is excluded.

Steel plant: INR 7,000 crore 1 million ton integrated plant (blast furnace route, 50% pellet and 50% sinter feed); construction is expected to start in October 2026 and management expects EBITDA above 20% at full run-rate.
capex_capacity: Ari Dongri mines: EC and CTO received in February 2026 to expand from 2.35 to 6 million tons; phased ramp under way, full scale from FY28.
Pellet plant: 2 million ton natural gas-based plant commissioned in December 2025, running at about 70% in its first quarter; total capacity 4.7 million tons.
Captive solar: from 165 MW to 540 MW; 25 MW commissioned on 21 May 2026, with 100 MW more due by July 2026.
Waste heat recovery power capacity to reach 49 MW after a 7 MW addition; HB wire capacity to rise from 0.1 to 0.115 million tons.
EV fleet: 10 EV dumpers, 24 EV loaders and 15 EV excavators added in FY26. Plans for about 300-350 EV trucks, costing about INR 350 crore including charging infrastructure.
demand_pricing: Benchmark 62% Fe iron ore traded at $95-110/t recently; management expects prices above $100/t for the full year.
Pellet prices softened about 10% from late April/early May 2026 across the supply chain, citing war, summer heat and a weak steel finished-product market.
Domestic pellet price is about INR 9,500-10,000/t ex-plant; management said export pricing is now only about $10 apart from domestic and it may start exporting.
Q4 pellet realisations were held back because the EC delay forced production of 63% commercial-grade pellets instead of high-grade pellets, which earn a premium above INR 1,000/t.

Coal: Q1 FY27 average cost is about INR 12,000-13,000/t. Imported coal is up 15-20% from Q2 because of freight and currency; the company is about 100% on imported coal and may switch to domestic coal.
Mining-to-pellet conversion cost is about INR 2,000/t. Mining landed cost is about INR 3,000-3,200/t in FY27; transport cost is about INR 900/t, potentially rising to INR 1,150-1,200/t.

qa_highlights.question: Why has FY27 mining guidance (3.4 million tons) fallen versus the earlier 4.5-5 million tons?
qa_highlights.answer: 3.4 million tons is net usable ore after beneficiation. Mining will be about 4-4.25 million tons, including about 0.5 million tons from Boria Tibu, with about 0.8-1 million tons of ore bought from the market until post-monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 EBITDA jump?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry-over pellet inventory of about 89,000 tons sold in Q4, the new pellet plant ramp to 70% and about 2-2.5 lakh extra tons of mining in March after EC approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS margin and the lithium cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was planned at 7-8% but is now 12-13%. Cell pricing with EVE is index-linked, so cost changes pass through to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance for 24-25% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflects current market levels and the early stage of the year; pellet margins should widen from Q3 as high-grade mix rises after monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Why did steel plant capex rise to INR 7,000 crore from the earlier INR 4,000 crore estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management apologised for an earlier estimation error. The increase reflects a coke oven plant (now needed after import curbs) and a value-added structural mill; EBITDA above 20% is expected at full capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CRM and FY28 utilisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The first line is expected by end-Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. FY28 guidance is 50% utilisation (3-3.5 lakh tons), with about 90% from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company export pellets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports may start soon if the domestic market stays weak; freight to China is about INR 3,000/t, and domestic prices are about INR 9,500-10,000/t ex-plant.

Pellet and CRM margins on lower-margin BESS and CRM revenue expansion: management guided about 10% PAT margin in 2031.

So, we were not able to produce the same volumes of high-grade pellets where we draw premium for more than INR 1,000.
We were wrong on the cost estimation. The current CAPEX given as INR 7,000 crores is very much on the practical side.

Iron ore mining volume fell because dumping space was constrained by pending tree-cutting approval on additional land, forcing market ore purchases for pellets. One of the new 2 mtpa pellet plants was shut from around mid-June/July on gas price and iron ore economics, with Q2 pellet output guided to roughly 500 kt. Management shelved the 1 mtpa integrated steel project over water allocation delays and moved the 0.7 mtpa CRM complex to Maharashtra, with commissioning now targeted December 2027.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume guidance is said to be on track, with Q1 at 16-29% of full-year guidance. Management said FY27 pellet output will be slightly lower, and a revised figure will come later.

Q2 FY27 pellet production is expected at about 500 kt if the plant stays shut for the whole quarter. Q3 is expected at full pellet capacity, with merchant ore purchases at 25-30%, falling below 10% in Q4 and to zero (fully captive) in FY28.

Mining ramp-up is expected from Q3 FY27 once government land approval comes through (targeted end-September), reaching full capacity by end Q4 FY27 or early Q1 FY28. Beneficiation plant commissioning is expected by Q3 FY27.

Margin improvement is expected from Q4 FY27 once the beneficiation plant enables higher captive pellet use. Management said CRM incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from the earlier 7-8%.
Vision 2030 target (4x revenue, 3x EBITDA and PAT) was restated without the steel plant. Management said the steel plant is on hold and no timeline is set.
capex_capacity: CRM complex (0.7 mtpa, relocated to Maharashtra near Sambhajinagar): capex raised to INR1,100 crore from earlier INR900-950 crore, including working capital margin money; INR80 crore spent so far; land about INR50 crore for 35 acres; construction from October 2026; commissioning December 2027; funded by INR550 crore debt and internal accruals. Land allotment approval is expected by end-August 2026.
BESS (20 GW... as stated in transcript, battery storage project in Maharashtra): about INR500 crore spent; remaining INR700-800 crore to be spent over FY27 and FY28; commissioning targeted Q1 FY28.
Mining and other capex: about INR2,000 crore for the remaining FY27 and the whole of FY28. No FY29 projection has been given.
Ari Dongri beneficiation plant: INR218 crore spent till June 2026; ramp-up from Q3 FY27 and full-scale operation from FY28.

Captive solar: 25 MW commissioned in May 2026; 100 MW under construction, targeted September 2026; 150 MW project in abeyance. Solar storage of 45 MW targeted for Q3 FY27 (management corrected 'Q3 27' to 'Q3 26' and then said Q3 FY27 was intended). Captive solar would reach 290 MW.
Boria Tibbu mine (0.7 mtpa now) expansion to 4 mtpa targeted for FY31, with a 4 mtpa beneficiation plant yielding 1.5-2 mt concentrate (about 40% yield). TOFR filing pending.
demand_pricing: Iron ore prices (global) expected to hover around USD90-100/t; management said it does not expect prices to fall below USD90 soon. Domestic ex-mine iron ore about INR5,500/t.

Pellet exports: two vessels exported in June-July at about INR9,000/t ex-plant, roughly at par with domestic. Exports have now stopped due to the plant shutdown.
Industry pellet utilisation is about 65%, held back by lower exports, limited high-grade supply and margin pressure. Indian pellet production was about 120 mt in FY26, up from 109 mt in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Milestones needed before the board revives the 1 mtpa integrated steel plant, and should it now be treated as optional growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Water allocation is the gating item: an LOI was received but the confirmation letter has stalled, delaying the ~9.4 MCM allocation by 6-8 months. Management said to treat the steel plant as an option for medium-term growth, and that Vision 2030 was restated without it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the mining production shortfall continue into Q2 and Q3, and when does merchant ore purchasing fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Government land approval for dumping (tree cutting) is expected by end-September, with Q2 mining at the same level as Q1. Mining ramps from Q3 and reaches full capacity by end-Q4 or early Q1 FY28. Merchant ore purchases stay at 25-30% in Q3, fall below 10% in Q4, and reach 100% captive in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the pellet plant shut, and is the gas issue expected to normalise after Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Gas is fully supplied, but the PNGRB guideline has pushed gas purchase value up about 40-45%. Combined with market ore purchases, this made the plant commercially unviable, so one 2 mtpa plant was shut. No clarity on normalisation was given; GAIL has no guidelines, and August is expected to remain a shutdown month.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for iron ore and pellet prices, and what is the sensitivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Global iron ore is expected to hover at USD90-100/t, with management not expecting a fall below USD90 soon. Pellet prices were about INR10,000/t after a roughly 10% recovery from the early-July low of about INR8,700/t. Each INR100/t fall in pellet price cuts annual EBITDA by about INR40 crore on 4 mt.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA benefit per tonne do beneficiation, EV fleet and mining cost cuts deliver from FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining cost is INR3,000-3,500/t now, with a target below INR2,700/t from FY28. Each INR100/t saving on about 5-6 mt of ore is worth about INR45-50 crore EBITDA. Pellet output is expected to reach about 4.5 mt in FY28, and selling surplus ore is not planned in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised CRM capex, and what incentives and margins are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: CRM capex rose to about INR1,100 crore from INR900-950 crore, which includes working capital margin money. The land is about INR50 crore for 35 acres. Management said incentives can add 2-3% to CRM margins, taking them to 10-11% from 7-8%. Commissioning is December 2027.

Capex visibility: no FY29 projection given, and the BESS (commissioning Q1 FY28) and CRM (December 2027) timelines have slipped in the past. The BESS commercial ramp depends on tender wins.

532735|2026-03.headline: R Systems Q1 CY26 (Jan–Mar 2026) revenue rose 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 20.1%, helped by rupee depreciation.
532735|2026-03.overview: Revenue grew 3.5% QoQ and 29.9% YoY to INR 574.8 crore ($62.8 million), with Novigo consolidated for a full quarter and rupee depreciation supporting the numbers. Management said organic revenue was flat QoQ, citing fewer days and Q4 fixed-price true-ups, and that Novigo's restated revenue is about $21–22 million a year after accounting alignment versus the roughly $32 million quoted at acquisition. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 115.7 crore (20.1% margin), which management said is about 19% excluding the currency benefit. Utilisation was deliberately reduced to about 80.5% (from a peak of about 84%) to build AI and data bench and COE capacity. Trailing-12-month ACV wins rose to $82.5 million from $76.5 million last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI in SDLC threaten growth, and how will frontier-model firms entering IT services affect R Systems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI in SDLC expands the addressable market for a projects-based business with over 90% discretionary revenue; deal sizes per unit of work fall, but TAM expansion more than compensates. It views the frontier-lab services move as validation that AI is a people problem, and will assess competition as it develops.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Q1 growth mainly from full-quarter Novigo consolidation, and is organic growth returning from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Novigo's accounting was aligned to R Systems policies, moving some licence revenue from gross to net and changing fixed-price accounting. Restated Novigo revenue is about $21–22 million a year versus about $32 million at acquisition. Organic growth was flat QoQ, attributed to fewer days and Q4 true-ups, and management said it sees no challenge to positive outlook for Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Blackstone and Anthropic consulting venture: threat to mid-market players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it sees the venture as early-stage and as validation of its playbooks; Blackstone portfolio access gives a faster path to some companies, but deals are still won on merit against competition.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SG&A fall, and what is the normal run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop from INR 114.3 crore to INR 91.4 crore reflected reversal of a conservative AR provision after collections and year-end provision true-up, not lower investment. Normal run rate is about USD 11 million a quarter versus USD 10 million in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is organic growth and the FY outlook, and how is Novigo contributing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth was flat in Q1, but it does not give forward guidance; it pointed to new wins and expects EBITDA margins to be sustained. Novigo cross-selling is active across close to a dozen deals.

qa_highlights.question: How are GCCs and token costs affecting the business?
qa_highlights.answer: R Systems has helped about 8–9 mid-market clients set up GCCs since launching the service about six quarters ago, which it sees as a growth lever. Token costs for client output are mostly borne by clients, and Optima AI FinOps tooling is used to meter them.

532749|2026-06.headline: Allcargo Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.2% YoY to INR546 crores and PAT turned to a INR14 crore profit from a Q1 FY26 loss.

Consultative Logistics revenue grew 6.1% YoY on a stable 7.5 million sq ft of warehouse space under management. Management reiterated a 3-year plan targeting Express EBITDA margin of 10% and a company-level EBITDA margin of about 13% this year.

532749|2026-09.headline: Allcargo Q2 FY27 revenue rose 3.4% YoY to INR555 crore while EBITDA grew 24.2% to INR77 crore, margin 13.9%.

Revenue from operations was INR555 crore (up 3.4% YoY, up 1.6% QoQ), with gross margin at 31.4% and EBITDA margin at 13.9%. Management attributed margin expansion mainly to service-led price realisation and tight cost control, and reiterated its FY28 revenue guidance. Express volumes were described as stabilised after a decline, with higher realisation per ton.

532755|2026-03.headline: Tech Mahindra Q4 FY26 revenue rose 2.4% cc YoY to USD 1,625M, with EBIT margin at 13.8% and FY27 targets of 15% EBIT reiterated.
532755|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was USD 1,625M, up 0.9% QoQ and 4.9% YoY reported (2.4% YoY constant currency), with operating margin up 70 bps QoQ to 13.8%. Full-year FY26 revenue was USD 6,385M (+0.6% cc) and operating margin expanded 290 bps to 12.6%. Deal wins for the year reached USD 3.79B (+42% YoY) and the company reiterated FY27 targets of above-peer-average organic cc growth and a 15% EBIT margin. The analyst day framed AI as a modernization opportunity and highlighted Orion, Helix and a new pricing model, but did not report a standalone AI revenue figure.

segments.commentary: FY26 growth 7.3% YoY, the fastest vertical for the year; Q4 up 6.2% YoY. Driven by logistics and e-commerce tailwinds.

qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said the portfolio is diversifying into aerospace and defence, BFSI and retail CPG, and that pipeline BFSI and manufacturing deals should add meaningfully as they ramp up.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Tuck-in acquisitions and back-end integration

532755|2026-06.headline: Tech Mahindra Q1 FY27 revenue rose 6.1% YoY to US$1.66bn with operating margin at 14.4%, and deal wins hit US$1.078bn.
532755|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 2.2% QoQ and 6.1% YoY in reported USD (6.6% YoY constant currency), with every vertical growing YoY. EBIT margin rose 60 bps QoQ and 330 bps YoY to 14.4%, led by volume growth and Project Fortius savings, partly offset by Comviva seasonality and business mix. Management said Q1 was stronger than expected, helped by early delivery on a European automotive programme that it expects to reverse in Q2. Management reiterated its FY27 ambition of growth above the peer average and an operating margin of 15%, with Q4 margin expected above 15%.

financial_highlights.change: +16.2% YoY in USD; PAT margin +80 bps YoY

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Grew 1.3% YoY; held back by Comviva Q1 seasonality and a cloud pass-through that a client pulled back after a takeover. Management expects the pass-through impact to fade in Q2, and one large deal has not yet ramped.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 8.1% YoY and 2.7% QoQ. Acquisition of Avant Techno Solutions (Canada, payments modernisation and wealth platforms) was announced in the quarter.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew 17.2% YoY and 9% QoQ, helped by aerospace and early delivery on a large European automotive programme. Management called the auto delivery acceleration a timing benefit, not a one-off, with a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure expected next quarter.

segments.name: Retail, Travel & Logistics
segments.commentary: Grew 8.6% YoY; management described the macro as mixed.

segments.name: Healthcare (HLS)
segments.commentary: Grew 7.2% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, supported by providers and life sciences; the largest deal wins this quarter came from manufacturing and HLS.

segments.name: Technology, Media & Entertainment
segments.commentary: Declined 1.7% QoQ on continued volatility in client spend. YoY growth was not stated in the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: growth above the peer average (management said it is already ahead in Q1) and an operating margin of 15%; management said Q4 margin must be above 15%.
Q2 growth expected to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months; the European auto acceleration will create about a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure in Q2.
Wage increases to take effect from Q2 in a phased manner.
Management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number, citing volatility; it said it expects to exceed peer-average growth, by an amount it did not quantify.

Margin levers: Project Fortius (fixed-price productivity, T&M utilisation) and SG&A savings from portfolio company consolidation. Management also flagged wage bill increases and AI-driven productivity pressure as headwinds.
capex_capacity: Communications experience centre in Pune opened in April 2026, with more than 10 executive sessions held in its first two months.
Management said it is investing in centres of excellence in Hyderabad (learning, engineering, retail CPG) and will calibrate investment to growth opportunities.
Investing in talent, IP and software licences; deals are screened to be margin-accretive over the long term.
Headcount in IT services fell 7% YoY because of AI-led productivity gains in fixed-price work. Management expects hiring to resume in the rest of FY27, mixing fresh and experienced talent.
demand_pricing: Deal wins of US$1,078 million, with the largest coming from manufacturing and HLS. Management said the pipeline looks strong but that large deals are binary and hard to forecast beyond a quarter or two.

Demand strengthening in ServiceNow, SAP, Salesforce, and data and AI (Databricks, Snowflake, GenAI). Weakness seen in manual testing, traditional big data, standalone e-commerce, legacy CRM and legacy infrastructure admin.

Management walked away from deals with 70%-80% productivity benefits over 5-7 year contracts and from fixed price guarantees on infrastructure, citing memory and chip price inflation of about 20% YoY.
Auto sector: some customers are cutting costs with AI. Auto finance was resilient. Aerospace demand is rising, especially in IT and engineering.

BPS: AI operations made up most of the BPS deal TCV this quarter, including a large AI-led engagement with a high-tech client. Some clients are questioning in-house versus outsourcing decisions on multi-year deals, but management said it is not seeing outsized delays or cancellations.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth momentum carry into Q2 without the Comviva seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 to be supported by ramp-up of large deals won over the past 12 months, offset by a European auto slowdown; it expects to meet or exceed the peer-average growth for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion lever remains, and what is the exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an exit target, but said Q4 margin must be above 15%. Levers are gross margin from Project Fortius plus SG&A gains from portfolio company consolidation. Q1 had seasonal visa and travel costs and Comviva seasonality as negatives.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO and free cash flow improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of Q1 was helped by accelerated customer payments and FX on receivables, which will normalise. Management said working capital remains a priority with a long-term improvement trend, though quarterly seasonality will persist.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Comms ramp impact is in Q1, and what is the full-year growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: One of the two large Comms deals has not ramped at all yet, so impact comes in later quarters. Management said it would not give a specific full-year growth number, given the volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Was the strong quarter a plan or a surprise, and is demand improving or is share being taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the quarter was stronger than expected, helped by the European auto acceleration. It described a shift in demand toward modernisation and platform work, with the core stable and no 'SaaS eclipse' seen; it remains cautiously optimistic.

qa_highlights.question: Given the pricing comparisons with peers, can 15% margins go higher, and what competitor irrationality exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15% is the target for FY27, with a path beyond FY27 to be set. Examples of irrational pricing included 70%-80% productivity assumptions in 5-7 year deals and holding infrastructure prices amid about 20% YoY inflation.

risks_watch: Q2 revenue drag of about 1%-1.3% from the European auto programme acceleration not repeating, plus slower Comms ramp until the large deal goes live.
Wage increase effective Q2 and AI-led productivity pressure on margins, against the 15% FY27 target.
Large-deal conversion is binary; management cannot forecast beyond one or two quarters.
Cash flow and DSO benefits partly from timing (accelerated payments and FX), which management said will normalise.
Auto sector cost pressure and EV programme softness, and client questions about in-house versus outsourced delivery on multi-year deals.
532755|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on execution and margins, but cautious on the forward view: management declined to give a specific FY27 growth number, citing macro volatility. It was more open about pricing discipline and about the Q2 headwinds from the European auto acceleration and the Comms cloud pass-through.
key_quotes: We had said that in the third year of our transformation, we would pivot strongly to growth, and as the numbers today show, we have done just that.
So it has to be upwards of 15% for the fourth quarter, and we'll see how each quarter progresses from here and now.
So I would feel that the demand situation is not catastrophic.
But candidly, it's not very different from what I used to see, in my 25-plus years in this industry.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Reported revenue +6.1% YoY and 6.6% cc, with US$1,078m TCV (+33.3% YoY) and large deals ramping, though Q2 faces a 1%-1.3% revenue drag from the European auto pull-forward reversing and Comms pass-through fading.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation described only as healthy with no figure given, and investment is framed as talent, IP and software licences rather than capex; no new capex plans or land approvals disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it is already ahead of peers in Q1 and will meet or exceed peer-average growth for FY27, but declined to quantify, citing volatility and binary large-deal timing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 was flattered by early European auto delivery that management expects to reverse, creating a 1%-1.3% revenue pressure in Q2, plus Comviva seasonality and a Comms cloud pass-through hit, and DSO/FCF gains partly timing-driven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or model launches discussed; only the Avant Techno Solutions acquisition in BFSI was announced.

rows.label: Record TCV of US$1,078m with ramp-ups from past 12 months' large deals
rows.why: TCV up 33.3% YoY to US$1,078m and management says Q2 growth is supported by ramp of large deals won over the past 12 months, though one Comms large deal has not ramped at all yet.

rows.label: Walk-away discipline on low-productivity fixed-price and infrastructure deals
rows.why: Management walked away from deals assuming 70%-80% productivity benefits over 5-7 years and from fixed-price infrastructure amid about 20% YoY memory and chip inflation, supporting margin-accretive mix.

rows.label: Wage increases phased in from Q2
rows.why: Wage increases take effect from Q2 in a phased manner, a margin headwind against the 15% FY27 target, with AI-led productivity pressure also flagged.

tone.note: Management was confident on execution, margins (Q4 above 15%) and pricing discipline, but cautious on the forward view, declining a specific FY27 growth number and flagging the Q2 European auto reversal and Comms ramp delay; analysts pushed on sustainability of the margin, DSO/FCF gains and the peer

532755|2026-09.headline: Tech Mahindra Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.8% YoY to US$1,693M and EBIT margin hit 14.8%, with US$1,023M deal wins.
532755|2026-09.overview: Revenue grew 2.4% QoQ and 7.2% YoY in constant currency, with organic growth of 7% YoY in CC, led by Communications ramp-up on the Orange large deal. EBIT margin of 14.8% expanded 40 bps QoQ and 260 bps YoY, and management reiterated a full-year FY27 EBIT margin target of 15%. Free cash flow was US$135M, held back by rebadged-deal ramp-ups that management expects to normalise next quarter. Management emphasised AI (Helix, Zero-Gravity Telco Architecture) and a shift in the three-year plan toward growth, with the next plan to be announced later.

financial_highlights.change: US$ PAT +23.2% YoY; PAT margin +130 bps YoY
Impacted by rebadged deal ramp-up; FCF-to-PAT guidance 90-100% reiterated
MTM movement US$13.83M: US$8.7M in P&L, US$5M in reserves

segments.name: Communications
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9.5% YoY and 6% QoQ, driven by Orange large-deal ramp-up and new strategic engagements; management says pipeline and visibility remain strong despite client concentration.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 4.6% YoY (5.4% CC) and 0.4% QoQ (1% QoQ CC); management said prior two quarters were above 8% and expects a return to that level next quarter, with leadership changes made.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY but declined 3.9% QoQ after accelerated execution of a large European automotive program in Q1; a further sequential headwind of about 0.5% is expected in Q3.

segments.name: Retail, Travel and Logistics
segments.commentary: Grew 9.2% YoY (about 9.5-9.6% per call) and 9.6% QoQ, supported by new deal scale-up and growth in existing accounts; fastest-growing vertical per management.

segments.name: Hi-Tech / TME / Healthcare
segments.commentary: Hi-Tech grew 6.7% YoY; Technology, Media and Entertainment grew 2.8% QoQ; Healthcare grew 6.2% YoY and 1.4% QoQ.

segments.name: Service lines
segments.commentary: Digital enterprise applications (ServiceNow, Salesforce, SAP, Oracle) grew about 13% YoY; ADMS grew 7.6% YoY; BPS grew 6.5% YoY; experience design and consulting were relatively weaker.

segments.name: Large accounts (>US$20M)
segments.commentary: Revenue from accounts above US$20M grew 3.1% QoQ and 11.7% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 EBIT margin target of 15% reiterated; management said the company is on track and within about 20 bps of its margin aspiration.
Free cash flow to PAT of 90-100% on a full-year basis reiterated.
Capital allocation policy of returning 85% and above of free cash flow to shareholders reaffirmed.
Q3 FY27 sequential headwind from European auto program expected at roughly 0.5%, to normalise thereafter.
Management expects normal seasonality in H2 FY27 with no unusual furloughs in Q3 or Q4.
AI revenue reporting to be introduced as part of H2 FY27 disclosures.
Next three-year plan to be announced later; management signalled growth will be the focus and no specific growth number was given.
capex_capacity: Board recommended a 1:1 bonus share issue; interim dividend of INR15 per share declared.
Launched Toronto Innovation Hub and Engineering Experience Center, building on Manufacturing, Communication and Retail CPG Experience Centers.
Launched Consumer Agentic Experience Studio (more than 20 customers hosted since launch) and Indus-Terra, a 30-billion-parameter model built with NVIDIA and AWS under IndiaAI Mission.
AI Velocity Cells program delivered 16 client-relevant capstones in seven weeks; portfolio includes more than 200 AI assets being rationalised.
IHub Quantum partnership: middleware for India's 20-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer, completion expected by December 2026.
demand_pricing: Deal wins of US$1,023M in the quarter were broad-based across Comms, BFSI, Manufacturing and Retail/Logistics/Transport; wins include a Canadian insurer (ApMS), a UK digital network mainframe-as-a-service deal, and a 5-year Australian telecom managed services deal.
Management said pricing pressure is driven more by competitive intensity than by budget diversion to AI; AI token costs are not a material part of client IT budgets.
Outcome-based and human-plus-agent pricing (including Vector Squad-based pricing for F&A) is gaining adoption across telco and financial services.
Management argued that AI model commoditisation resembles cloud, with clients using multiple models including open-source, which it sees as supporting services demand.
Management expects some productivity release from fixed-price contracts via AI toolchains, but sees growth opportunity in consulting, modernization, data and analytics.

qa_highlights.question: How are service-line offerings like TechM Orion driving share gains and where is momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital enterprise applications grew about 13% YoY and BPS 6.5% YoY; management sees AI toolchains per service line plus industry roadmaps driving above-industry growth. Consulting and experience design were relatively weaker.

qa_highlights.question: Is gross margin expansion nearing its peak given headcount increased this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the headcount rise to the Orange deal employee transfer and said gross margin opportunity is not fully tapped; AI toolchains should release headcount from fixed-price projects, and Rohit said gross margin gains will continue for the next three years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company trade margin for growth, aiming for near double-digit growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohit said the focus will pivot to profitable growth in year three of the roadmap and will not buy revenue; he declined to give a number for the next three-year plan.

qa_highlights.question: Can Communications and BFSI drive medium-term growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Comms pipeline is strong but concentrated; BFSI grew 5.4% CC, was above 8% in the prior two quarters, and management expects a return to that level next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are growth gains coming from large accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Accounts above US$20M grew 11.7% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, and management said these accounts still have significant headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI capex slowdown shift enterprise budgets toward services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI token spend is small for clients; hardware and cloud cost increases from the AI build-out could ease, freeing budget for services, but it is hard to quantify benefit given competitive pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Is the European auto revenue impact a reversal and how big is the Q3 effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit clarified it is a ramp-up from Q1 leading to QoQ declines in Q2 and Q3, not a reversal; Q3 impact is about 0.5% and then normalises.

risks_watch: Free cash flow was US$135M, held back by rebadged-deal ramp-up; management expects normalisation next quarter, and DSO rose four days QoQ to 88 days.
Effective tax rate of 29.9% included a one-time prior-period adjustment; underlying rate was 26.6%.
AI-driven deflation in effort-based fixed-price and managed services contracts could pressure revenue, and management acknowledged ADMS renewals carry productivity expectations that may mute growth.
Comms revenue is highly concentrated among a few clients, adding volatility.
European automotive weakness in Manufacturing, with a further sequential headwind in Q3.
AI revenue disclosure methodology is still being defined and will start in H2 FY27.
Growth in BFSI remains below the company's aspiration; leadership changes made.
532755|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and AI, with management repeatedly stating the quarter was strong and the margin target near. Cautious on specifics: declined to give a next three-year growth number, and was defensive on BFSI underperformance and on AI deflation questions.
key_quotes: We delivered a very strong quarter with broad -based growth across the business.
We do expect, as a result of the specific AI toolchain, we're building for each and every single service line, to be able to release head count across our fixed-price projects
We don't believe for a moment that the gross margin opportunities in the business have been fully tapped out
Our principle is simple. AI revenue must be evidenced by client -funded work and reconcilable to financial records.
