rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Reported revenue +6.8% YoY (7% organic CC) with US$1,023M deal wins and LTM deal wins +34.8% YoY to US$4,270M; BFSI expected to return to above 8% growth next quarter, offset by about 0.5% Q3 European auto headwind.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No new capacity or capex discussed; the call notes utilisation is high but gives no figure, and the business is largely asset-light services, so a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident and running ahead on margin, but no revenue guidance was given and the next three-year plan growth number was withheld.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q3 carries a further sequential ~0.5% European auto headwind, BFSI is below its aspiration, and AI deflation in fixed-price contracts is acknowledged, with FCF at US$135M held back by rebadged-deal ramp-ups.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Recent launches include Consumer Agentic Experience Studio, Indus-Terra 30B model, and Toronto Innovation Hub; AI revenue disclosure starts in H2 FY27, and the IHub Quantum middleware is due by December 2026.

rows.label: Deal wins momentum: US$1,023M in Q2, LTM US$4,270M (+34.8% YoY)
rows.why: Quarterly deal wins of US$1,023M and LTM up 34.8% support a revenue pipeline, with large accounts above US$20M growing 11.7% YoY and 3.1% QoQ.

rows.label: FCF normalisation after rebadged-deal ramp-up
rows.why: FCF was US$135M, held back by rebadged-deal ramp-ups that management expects to normalise next quarter, with FCF-to-PAT guidance of 90-100% reiterated for FY27.

rows.label: Outcome-based and human-plus-agent pricing adoption
rows.why: Outcome-based pricing is gaining adoption across telco and financial services, but management said pricing pressure is driven by competitive intensity and ADMS renewals carry productivity expectations.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins (15% FY27 target reiterated, 14.8% EBIT) and AI, but cautious on the next three-year growth number and defensive on BFSI underperformance and AI-driven deflation; analysts pushed on gross margin peak, trading margin for growth, and Comms concentration.

532762|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 total income rose 15% QoQ to INR1,021 crore, but FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 18.33%; management plans 9-10% price hikes to offset 11-14% cost inflation.
532762|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as the company's best ever revenue quarter, with total income of INR1,021 crore (up 15% QoQ, 5.58% YoY) and EBITDA of INR163.7 crore (16% margin). FY26 total income was flat at about INR3,395 crore, with EBITDA up about 4% to INR622 crore and PAT up 5.4% to INR425 crore. Other income was negative in Q4 on mark-to-market losses on surplus-cash investments, and March brought West Asia-driven steel and crude cost inflation. Management is taking staged price increases and has withheld annual guidance until the middle of Q2.

segments.name: Cranes, metal handling and construction equipment
segments.commentary: FY26 income over INR2,946 crore with an 18.6% margin and INR548 crore profit; management called FY26 a normalisation year after the pre-buying ahead of the emission transition in FY25.

segments.name: Agri division
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9% to around INR251 crore in FY26, with margins at about 1%.

segments.name: Others (miscellaneous exports)
segments.commentary: Separately reported line of about INR76.55 crore; management said it is mainly miscellaneous exports, including some construction equipment, and no volume figure is available.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: management expects growth of 15-20% or slightly more, helped by a low base in Q1 FY26; no full-year guidance given until the middle of Q2.
Pricing: 1-1.5% hike in January, about 4% from 1 May, and a further 5% from 1 June (total 9-10%); management sees total cost inflation of 11-14% and may take another 3-4% later in Q2.
Margins: target EBITDA ex-other income of 15-16%; management said expanding margins beyond about 17-18% including other income would hurt market share.
Other income expected to recover to INR20-35 crore in Q1 FY27 if markets hold or improve, after partial April recovery of March mark-to-market losses.
Defense: execution of about INR200-220 crore in FY27 (5-6% of revenue vs about 3% last year); about INR575 crore order book; rough terrain forklift/telehandler execution to start next quarter.

Long-term: INR6,000-6,200 crore revenue target by FY29 (worst case FY30) implies adding about INR700-800 crore a year; exports plus defense targeted at 10-15% of the segment, with about 11-13% expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation for cranes, metal handling and construction equipment is about 60%.

FY27 capex about INR200 crore: about INR130-135 crore for a land parcel contracted about 1-1.5 years ago, INR40-50 crore for a new defense and new-product plant within the existing complex, and INR20-25 crore maintenance.

Proposed new tower crane factory with capex upwards of INR400 crore; 12-18 months to build; decision to start this year is need-based, and management expects only about INR150 crore to be spent in FY27 if it starts.
Tower crane capacity is about 950-1,000 units a year versus about 680-690 units produced in FY26 (FY25 comparison not given).
demand_pricing: Tower crane order books are full; demand is strong into the start of Q1, with slowdown usually beginning mid-to-late June during monsoon.

Hydra-type cranes (about 60% of the market) shrank in FY26 on emission-norm skepticism and are recovering since January-February; management expects higher volumes in backhoe loaders and construction equipment.
Price realisation per unit rose on a mix shift to higher tonnage cranes; emission-transition costs added an estimated 5-7% to blended cost per unit.
About INR40-50 crore of Q4 revenue was lost to Middle East-bound export shipments stuck in India and March delivery deferrals.

Competition: Chinese players are absent from pick-and-carry cranes (below 30-35 tonnes) and compete in slew/heavy cranes (40-50+ tonnes), offering 1-2 year credit terms; competitor segment margins are about 8-9% versus about 18-19% for ACE.
Anti-dumping duties of 25-52% on Chinese cranes were recommended by DGTR in September 2025 but not notified by the Finance Ministry; the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Status of LD implementation and Chinese competition in pick-and-carry cranes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Chinese players do not make pick-and-carry cranes; they compete in heavy slew cranes (40-50+ tonnes). The anti-dumping order was not notified, and the 90-day window has lapsed.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-current investments large and what is their size?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus cash is invested in secured, listed bonds with 1-3 year tenures, classified as non-current under accounting rules but saleable; the amount is about INR700-750 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the INR76.55 crore 'others' revenue and the impairment line?
qa_highlights.answer: 'Others' is miscellaneous exports, reported separately by the auditors. Impairment is a prudent expected-credit-loss provision on slightly delayed receivables.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Mark-to-market losses on investments at March month-end; partly recovered in April. Management expects INR20-35 crore of other income in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes grow 10%+ in FY27 and what are price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 growth of 15-20% or more is possible on a low base; annual guidance is deferred to mid-Q2. Price hikes total 9-10% with another 3-4% possible, against 11-14% cost inflation (steel about 65% of cost, up 20-22% since January).

qa_highlights.question: What is the KATO JV revenue potential and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue of about INR300 crore in 3-4 years under current conditions, potentially INR700-800 crore if anti-dumping duties are imposed. Chinese imports are priced 25-30% below Indian-made costs, aided by credit terms.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and tower crane factory timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR200 crore; a INR400 crore tower crane factory is need-based, with a 12-18 month build.

risks_watch: Steel (about 65% of cost) up 20-22% since January; the price pass-through lags 2-3 months and may not fully recover 11-14% inflation.
Anti-dumping duty notification remains pending; the outcome determines JV scale and Chinese pricing pressure.
Other income is volatile due to mark-to-market exposure on treasury investments (INR700-750 crore).
Demand is capital-goods-linked; management flagged geopolitical risk, rupee depreciation, and a possible monsoon slowdown from mid-June.
Other expenses are largely fixed, so margins are sensitive to volume shortfalls; volumes fell about 18-20% in FY26 (about 13,300 to 10,800 units by the analyst's count).
ROCE fell from about 40% to 32% over two years; capex timing is tied to demand before the tower crane factory is approved.

qa_highlights.answer: Surplus liquidity from the FCNR(B) raise was carried for most of the quarter; lending yield fell 2 bps QoQ. Management expects NIM to improve in Q3 and Q4 as repo-linked loans reprice in November, and as credit costs stay low.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gold loan book growing faster than disbursements, and are gold slippages rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth includes inorganic DA and co-lending, while disbursement figures are organic only. Non-gold slippage rose to 1.55% from 1.52%. Management said some co-lending and DA partners collect before NPA, so the 1 DPD rule does not apply to many of them.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-FCNR(B), what was the lending yield and margin, and will the expansion continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an ex-FCNR NIM figure. It said lending yield fell 2 bps and that yield should rise with repo hikes, with a fairly decent NIM expansion expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL readiness and impact on PCR and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: A Big 4 firm has been appointed; the ECL model is expected to be live by March. Management said lead indicators are positive except SMA-1 and SMA-2, and sees credit-cost gains from SMA reduction after ECL.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA/ROE guidance be revised, and how will bancassurance fee loss be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to set a new ROE target until capital comes in; it expects ROE above 13.5%. On bancassurance, it cited the prior loss of about INR 100 crore of treasury gains and said it will wait for final norms and build offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Is gold loan CIBIL screening relaxed, and what is the risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Low CIBIL is not a bar for gold loans; management uses it to profile customers. The main risk is a fall in gold prices, and auction recovery was under 10% during the MFI stress, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How are the drought and agri books, and what is the mortgage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor and KCC books are about 4% each and collections remain robust, with no state above 20% of exposure. Management expects mortgage share to rise as gold is capped at 25% and overall growth is 18-20%.

risks_watch: Non-gold slippage edged up to 1.55%, and SMA-1 and SMA-2 are elevated; ECL transition and the related model risk are to be tested by March.
Gold loan book, co-lending and DA partner collection practices and gold price exposure.
Bancassurance commission drop under draft norms; management has not quantified the offset, and analysts estimated a 10-12 bps ROA hit.
Capital raise: terms and price are not yet disclosed; management said it will not raise below book value.
NIM recovery depends on repo pass-through and on deposit repricing lagging asset repricing.
532772|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and firm on asset quality, cost and profitability. Management was evasive on NIM ex-FCNR(B), product-wise repricing mix, and the size and price of the capital raise, citing ongoing negotiations.
key_quotes: So we got more than what we deserve in terms of foreclose -- what you call, prepayment penalty, etcetera, and lesser interest rate.
Below the book value, we will not raise capital. That much I can tell you.
So it's about -- it's from that perspective that you'd be looking at the CIBIL.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 20 new branches planned for the year, branch count up about 3 in Q2, and headcount guided to rise from 12,002 to 12,800-12,900 by year-end, but these are mostly existing-location adds with no plant-style capacity numbers.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Management said it is near closure on three components with a firm commitment expected before the next investor call, the bank has not raised equity since 2017, and it will not raise below book value; size and price undisclosed.

rows.label: ECL model go-live with Big 4 advisor

532777|2026-03.headline: Info Edge Q4 FY26 standalone billings rose 7% to Rs.1,057 crore and revenue 17% to Rs.805 crore, with 99acres billings flat at 2%.
532777|2026-03.overview: Standalone operating profit rose 39% YoY to Rs.323 crore at a 40% margin, helped by a one-time Rs.20.5 crore 99acres warranty provision write-back that lifted revenue. Recruitment billings grew 10% standalone (9% including Zwayam and DoSelect) amid a subdued hiring market, with GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4. 99acres billings grew only 2% after a sales reorganisation and tighter invoicing controls, while traffic share rose to 49% web and 52% in April. Management guided to double-digit Naukri topline growth as the threshold for holding margins, and said 99acres should turn cash-generative in FY27 if execution holds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hiring sentiment across GCCs, IT and non-IT, and what is driving 99acres margins and share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Hitesh Oberoi called the market lukewarm; larger GCCs have shrunk headcount while smaller ones hire. Share gains credited to execution, with 13-14 points added to traffic share in recent months; new-home responses up 33% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs.20 crore 99acres revenue write-back sustainable, and how did it affect billings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a one-time reversal of over-provisioned warranty on cost-per-lead products, which did not affect billings. Provision will move from 20% to 5% of leads going forward; the write-back was not expected to recur.

qa_highlights.question: Why did jobseeker services revenue grow so fast, and is there guidance for it?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from AI tools, a self-serve shift away from telecalling and a counter-cyclical lift as hiring slowed. Management was surprised by 30% growth after one quarter and said it was unsure whether it would sustain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for JobHai and its monetisation model?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is similar to Apna and WorkIndia but more freemium. It is monetising in Delhi NCR and will expand to Mumbai and Bangalore; management targets about 100% YoY growth for several years.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins and 99acres growth be framed for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Naukri margins hold at 10%+ topline growth; 99acres aim is 60% share, doubling billings in 3 years and reaching 25-30% EBITDA margin. Management said Q1 should recover but near-term markets may slow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the adoption and willingness to pay for AI-Rex, and how does 99acres gain share in new homes?
qa_highlights.answer: AI-Rex was made free to many recruiters after B2B sales friction; it has 30,000 mandates, with 1% take rate targeted. New-home share gains come from secondary-market traffic plus 99Shorts video content.

risks_watch: 99acres Q1 FY27 billings recovery after the 2% Q4 growth and the sales reorganisation; the one-time write-back will not repeat.
Recruitment growth held at 9-11% all year; watch whether Naukri can hold double-digit topline growth to protect the 57-58% margin.
GCC and IT hiring softness, with larger GCCs shrinking headcount and GCCs de-growing 1% in Q4.
Shiksha billings down 13% in Q4 on AI-driven search traffic loss; study-abroad softness in the US and Canada.

532777|2026-06.headline: Info Edge Q1 FY27: standalone billings up over 14% and recruitment billings up 17%, with underlying recruitment billings growth at about 15%.
532777|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs.824 crores and operating profit rose 33% to Rs.334 crores, with cash from operations up 25% to Rs.225 crores. Naukri recruitment billings grew 17%, which management says is about 15% after adjusting for renewal timing, with revenue up 13% and a 58% operating PBT margin. 99acres billings grew 17% and its operating PBT loss narrowed to about Rs.2 crores, near break-even. Shiksha billings fell 23% on AI-driven search traffic loss, and matchmaking grew billings 20% and was near break-even.

segments.name: Naukri Jobseeker (Naukri 360)

segments.name: 99acres

segments.commentary: Billings down 23% and revenue down 12% as reduced Google referral traffic hit client delivery; US and Canada study-abroad softer.

segments.commentary: Portfolio billings up 20%; Aisle +44%, Jeevansathi +14%; near break-even operating PBT; more than 45% profile share in Hindi-speaking markets.

segments.commentary: Revenue roughly doubled on a small base; about Rs.15 crores revenue last year, burn near Rs.50 crores a year.

Heavy AI investment will continue, so margins are not expected to expand from AI monetisation alone.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 13% revenue growth is from realisation versus customer count, and how much from AI products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about one-third of revenue growth came from renewals and volume, and about one-third from newer offerings such as AI-Rex and Talent Pulse. Premium CV views are growing over 25% from a small base.

qa_highlights.question: Is the normalised 15% recruitment billings growth adjusted for the favourable Q1 FY26 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said normalisation nets out early and deferred renewals each quarter, which captures the prior-year base effect. GCC billings grew 31% reported, with about 2.5% of one-off timing shift from Q4 FY26 deferrals.

qa_highlights.question: Are clients paying separately for AI-Rex, and is there cannibalisation?

qa_highlights.question: Will 99acres reach 30% margin faster after the Housing acquisition?

qa_highlights.question: What is the AI-Rex renewal cycle and how is value measured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it needs one renewal cycle to confirm success. Customers buy mandate bundles (10, 20 or 30 mandates), and internal dashboards track shortlisting, screening and delivery time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 99acres billing reconciled against JobSpeak index trends?

532777|2026-09.headline: Info Edge Q2 FY27: standalone billings up 13% YoY, revenue up 13% to Rs.842 crore, operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore; CEO Hitesh Oberoi steps down Dec 2.
532777|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone billings grew 13% and revenue 13% to Rs.842 crore, with operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore and operating PBT margin of 41% (up 541 bps). Management said renewal timing shifted billings between Q1 and Q2, so H1 (billings +14%, revenue +12%) is the better read, with underlying growth guided at about 14-15%. Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi announced he will step down as MD and CEO at close of business on December 2, with Sanjeev Bikhchandani becoming Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from December 3; Oberoi stays on the board subject to shareholder approval. Management said AI-first products now run at a Rs.240 crore annualised rate, and 99acres reached near-breakeven operating losses with positive cash generation.

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri)
segments.commentary: Q2 billings +13%, revenue +13%, operating profit +20% at 59% operating PBT margin; H1 billings +15%. Q2 IT/Tech/BPM billings +3%, GCCs +7%, other sectors +18%, consultants +7%. Naukri 360 billings +37%; Job Hai billings +86%; NaukriGulf +9% at about 36% margin.

segments.name: Real Estate (99acres)
segments.commentary: Billings +21% YoY in Q2 (up from 17% in Q1), revenue +17%. Operating loss cut 93% from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore; operating cash flow Rs.22 crore vs Rs.2 crore a year ago. Marketing spend down about 13% YoY while enquiries grew 33%.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Billings +23% in Q2 (Jeevansathi +18%, Aisle +40%). Segment near breakeven at operating PBT; Jeevansathi operating profit Rs.2 crore, Aisle operating loss Rs.3 crore. Segment cash generation Rs.3 crore vs cash loss Rs.2 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Education (Shiksha)
segments.commentary: Billings -27% and revenue -9% in Q2; near breakeven at operating PBT with cash loss of Rs.16 crore. 532784|2026-03.headline: Sobha FY26 real estate sales hit a record INR8,136 crore (+~30%), with Q4 EBITDA of INR194 crore and FY27 sales growth guided at a similar ~30%.
532784|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: real estate sales of INR8,136 crore at an average realisation of INR14,675 per sq ft (up 9.4% from INR13,412), and 3,188 homes (5.4 million sq ft) delivered, up about 19%. Q4 revenue recognition improved after occupancy certificates delayed in Q3 were received, with Q4 total income of INR2,030 crore, EBITDA of INR194 crore and PAT of INR92 crore. Net operating cash flow was INR1,637 crore for FY26 (up 39.4%) and the company moved to a net cash position of about INR800 crore. Management expects margins to improve through FY27, with projects nearing completion guided at 24-26% margins against a 30%+ EBITDA margin on the overall unrecognised revenue of INR18,647 crore. Some FY26 launches slipped, and the Rivana (Greater Noida) launch and the Crescent (Gurgaon) launch in April were the main new-launch data points.

segments.commentary: Record annual sales of about INR4,500 crore, with both new launches and sustenance sales contributing.

segments.name: NCR (Gurgaon, Greater Noida)
segments.commentary: Record annual sales of about INR2,450 crore, helped by the Greater Noida expansion; Bangalore and NCR together made up about 85% of sales.

segments.name: Kerala
segments.commentary: Steady at about INR800 crore of sales in FY26.

segments.commentary: About INR400 crore of sales in FY26.

segments.name: Non-real estate (manufacturing, contracting, retail)
segments.commentary: Management says these performed steadily; collections of INR732 crore in FY26 and INR183 crore in Q4, with an expectation of similar run rate and better profitability.

FY27 net operating cash flow target close to INR2,000 crore.

FY27 sales mix guided at roughly 45-50% from sustenance and 50-55% from new launches.
Business development spend of about INR1,100-1,200 crore expected in FY27, with pending land payments cleared in H1; targets a pipeline of at least 10 million sq ft a year.
Projected marginal cash flow of INR9,560 crore from completed and ongoing projects, and INR8,699 crore from forthcoming projects.
capex_capacity: Hoskote (Bangalore) residential project: about 5.3 million sq ft, GDV about INR7,000 crore; Phase 1 expected to launch in Q1 FY27 after RERA; at least half of Phase 1 to be released initially, with ~INR3,500 crore potentially launching depending on demand.

Rivana (Greater Noida): about 2.5 million sq ft, 1,384 units; Phase 1 of 684 units launched in late March 2026, with about 25% sold; execution started. Crescent (Gurgaon) Phase 1 launched in April 2026, about 50% sold, about INR1,100 crore.
Q2 FY27 launches planned in Calicut and Thrissur (Kerala); a Bangalore row-house project was cancelled and is being relaunched as apartments toward year-end.

Tentative Pune and Chennai launches toward year-end; Hyderabad second project awaiting approvals, targeted this year.
demand_pricing: Pricing described as stable for 3-4 quarters, with NCR and Bangalore both stabilising; management expects growth mainly from volume.
Management says leading indicators (inquiries, site visits) are stable and there is no big slowdown from AI concerns for the sub-INR3 crore ticket band, though demand is not at the 2021-23 peak.
Launch pricing for FY27 assumed at about INR15,000 per sq ft; FY27 GDV from the ~10 million sq ft launches estimated at about INR15,000 crore.

Management flagged commodity and material price increases from the geopolitical situation; the margin impact is not yet quantified and will be reviewed in 3-6 months. Escalation clauses have not yet been exceeded.

Kerala inquiries improved slightly, given that much of its demand comes from the Middle East.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins and EBITDA still below historical guidance, and when will they expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise as ongoing projects complete at end of Q2 and Q3 FY27, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be far better, in line with the projected EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Hoskote project size, GDV and approval status?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5.3 million sq ft of residential space with a GDV of about INR7,000 crore; RERA expected in Q1 FY27 and the launch is at an advanced stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Row House project converted to apartments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is a better use of the land, with higher ticket sizes, higher realisation and margins, and it will add to sales value.

qa_highlights.question: How are Rivana and Crescent performing and why was Rivana weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: Rivana sold about 25% of its launched inventory (~INR500 crore) and Crescent about 50% (~INR1,100 crore). Management attributed the gap to the timing of the Rivana launch in late March amid uncertainty, rather than to demand, and said sustenance sales are good.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 sales split between sustenance and new launches, and what is the GDV of the FY27 launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustenance is expected at 45-50% and new launches at 50-55%. About 10 million sq ft of launches is roughly INR15,000 crore GDV, and with about INR1,200-1,300 crore of unreleased inventory the total is about INR27,000-28,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost inflation is expected and can it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost inflation is event-led and its duration is unknown; the impact will be assessed over 3-6 months, and price increases depend on demand-supply, so it is in a wait-and-watch mode.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for rental and annuity income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees about 2-2.5 million sq ft of rental space on land already held in Hoskote and Gurgaon, with a decision on a separate rental vertical expected to be visible within a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Launch slippage: some FY26 launches were delayed, and FY27 relies on about 10 million sq ft of launches, including Hoskote (INR7,000 crore GDV) whose Phase 1 needs RERA in Q1.
Margin recovery depends on project completions in Q2-Q3 FY27 and on absorbing commodity and material cost increases from the geopolitical situation.
Rivana sustenance pace after its ~25% launch sell-through; Phase 2 timing depends on demand.
Bangalore FSI change remains unresolved in the courts; management has not given a timeline.
Business development: Hyderabad and Mumbai have few current land parcels, with only two small Mumbai deals (about INR2,000 crore GDV) targeted this year.
Demand sensitivity to AI-related IT/ITeS job concerns and the macro environment in Bangalore.

532784|2026-06.headline: Sobha Q1 FY27 record presales of INR3,656 crore (+76% YoY) and PAT of INR50.7 crore vs INR13.5 crore a year earlier.

Total income rose about 48% YoY to INR1,330 crore and real estate revenue rose about 60% to INR1,107 crore. Net cash stood at INR659 crore, with operational cash inflow of INR1,924 crore, though collections lagged presales because new-sale cash came late in the quarter and milestone billing slipped on labour shortages in April and May. 532790|2026-03.headline: Tanla's Q4 FY26 call: management says EBITDA margin (~16%) is range-bound, with GTM investment weighing; ₹12 crore FX loss flagged as non-cash.
532790|2026-03.overview: Management described the EBITDA margin (about 16%) as range-bound since FY22, attributing the pressure to deliberate GTM and innovation investment, while gross margin has improved slightly over the last couple of quarters. 532796|2026-09.headline: Lumax Auto Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% y-o-y to INR 1,556 crore, with PAT up 50% to INR 117 crore; FY27 growth guided to 20-25%.
532796|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,500 crore for the first time in a quarter, up 35% y-o-y and 14% q-o-q, with EBITDA of INR 228 crore (14.7% margin, broadly flat y-o-y). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR 2,919 crore (+34%), EBITDA INR 434 crore (+42%, margin 14.9%, up 90 bps) and PAT INR 215 crore (+64%). Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to 20-25% growth (near INR 6,000 crore), with H2 growth of 15-20%, and said the order book rose to INR 1,879 crore. Margin dilution in Q2 was attributed to input-cost pass-through lag of about one quarter.

segments.name: Advanced Plastics (incl. IAC)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue rose 45% y-o-y to INR 1,655 crore from INR 1,138 crore; IAC is about 60% of the division. Order book INR 834 crore. Contributes 44% of total order book.

segments.name: Mechatronics
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 45% y-o-y to INR 177 crore from INR 122 crore; order book INR 512 crore. Management says margins are in line with the overall company. Contributes 27% of order book.

segments.name: Structures & Control Systems
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 24% y-o-y to INR 476 crore from INR 380 crore; order book about INR 150 crore. Contributes 8% of order book.

segments.name: Aftermarket
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 9% y-o-y to INR 234 crore from INR 216 crore; Q2 growth was 11%. Non-lighting category weakened as input-cost increases were passed on.

segments.name: Alternate Fuels (Greenfuel)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 30% y-o-y to INR 220 crore from INR 170 crore; order book INR 379 crore. Contributes 20% of order book. Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 for M&M.

segments.name: Lumax Industries (LIL) wiring business
segments.commentary: Reported H1 revenue flat y-o-y because one product line moved to in-house supply by LIL; management says like-for-like growth is about 25-30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now guided at 20-25% y-o-y, implying roughly INR 6,000 crore; H2 FY27 growth expected at 15-20% y-o-y due to higher FY26 base.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance unchanged; management expects current margins to be sustained for the rest of the year.
FY28 absolute EBITDA target of about INR 1,000 crore reaffirmed.

North Star: 20% revenue CAGR FY25-FY31, with EBITDA margin moving toward 20% over 5-7 years; FY31 revenue aspiration about INR 11,000 crore. Organic CAGR of about 20% now seen as achievable if industry momentum holds.
Margin ambition of a further 100-200 bps over the next few years, toward 17-18%.

Capex guidance for FY27 around INR 300 crore, including greenfield expansions in Mechatronics, Advanced Plastics and Alternate Fuels; SOP expected in H2 FY27. Effective tax rate about 25%; minority interest about 11% of PAT.
capex_capacity: Capex capitalised in H1 FY27 was INR 60 crore; full-year capex guided at about INR 300 crore.

Board approved (24 Oct 2026) a new Mechatronics plant at Manesar, Haryana, with capex of about INR 150 crore funded by debt and internal accruals; commissioning in two phases from Q3 FY28, peak turnover about INR 500 crore.

Greenfuel Nashik facility began production in Q3 FY27 (ferrule-less tubes, fittings, receptacles) for M&M; Maruti Suzuki firm orders also won. Capacity expected to be significantly utilised by M&M and Maruti over about 2 years.
IAC Chakan Plant IV is in SOP phase; product launches expected around December 2026 to January 2027. Efficiency gains from centre-of-competence concept to be quantified after launch.
demand_pricing: Management cites industry Q2 FY27 production growth (SIAM): overall +19% y-o-y to 106 lakh units; PV +25% to about 17 lakh; 2W +17% to 81 lakh; 3W +25% to about 4.5 lakh; CV +34% to 3.5 lakh. Growth expected to moderate in H2.

Inflation: input costs (crude-linked polymers, electronic parts, freight, rupee) are rising. Most cost increases are passed to OEMs with about a one-quarter lag; management says pass-through is complete, with a 30-40 bps EBITDA margin dilution in Q2.
Order book of INR 1,879 crore: about 14% to execute in FY27, 59% in FY28, 27% in FY29; about 85% is new business. EV and CNG together are 29% (CNG 20%, pure EV about 9%); future technologies 22%.

Content per vehicle: about INR 70,000-75,000 per PV and INR 20,000-22,000 per 2W; about 50% of PV content is in IAC; Greenfuel about INR 5,000-8,000 per vehicle. Mechatronics is about 20% of PV content; expected to rise about 10% in 2-3 years.
Aftermarket growth target of 15-20% over a 3-5 year horizon, despite weak H1.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance being raised after 34% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management now expects FY27 revenue growth of 20-25% y-o-y (about INR 6,000 crore), versus the earlier implied 12-14%. H2 growth is expected at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins face pressure in Q3, and is the FY28 EBITDA target of INR 1,000 crore on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pass-through lags about one quarter, so margins dilute by a few bps. It remains confident of the FY28 INR 1,000 crore EBITDA target and of sustaining current margins in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% North Star revenue CAGR (FY25-FY31) still realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is now more confident of about 20% organic CAGR if industry growth holds. Inorganic growth could push it higher. The base year is FY25.

qa_highlights.question: Who develops the Body Control Module (BCM), and is it reported in standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: BCM is a build-to-print standalone revenue stream since SOP in July 2026, with a INR 250 crore order book. Technology comes from a large Japanese electronics component maker, not a JV; it is reported under Mechatronics across standalone and subsidiaries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV component strategy and the Aftermarket outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: EV focus is narrowed to 3-5 products, with active SOPs targeted for 2028-2030 and possible inorganic routes. Aftermarket grew 11% in Q2 and 9% in H1; the 15-20% target is over 3-5 years.

risks_watch: Input-cost inflation (crude-linked polymers, electronics, freight, rupee) and the one-quarter pass-through lag, which dilutes margin by 30-40 bps in Q2.
Festive-season demand sustainability and H2 moderation, with H2 growth guided at 15-20%.
Aftermarket weakness in non-lighting products, with H1 growth at 9%.
Mechatronics BCM ramp faces global competition and is in build-to-print phase; the Manesar plant is due Q3 FY28.
Dependence on JV partners for technology and IP (Mechatronics: about 75% of IP via JVs). One JV (with JOPP of Germany) was dissolved amicably in Q2.
Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East and energy price volatility, flagged by management as key uncertainties.
532796|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and guidance, with the FY27 outlook raised. Cautious on input costs and H2 moderation. Evasive on specifics for Chakan IV efficiency gains and the BCM counterparty name, which were not disclosed.
key_quotes: Q2 FY 27 revenue stood at INR 1,556 crore, up by 35% y-o-y and 14% quarter-on-quarter (q-o-q).
we can expect the full-year growth to be somewhere in the region of 20%-odd, if we compare from FY 26.
we are quite confident of delivering the absolute guidance of EBITDA for FY 28, which was always at about INR 1,000 crore EBITDA.
It is standalone revenue for Lumax Auto Technologies, and we are extremely proud of it.

rows.why: IAC Chakan Plant IV product launches are expected around December 2026 to January 2027, and Greenfuel Nashik is already producing ferrule-less tubes and fittings for M&M and Maruti.

rows.why: Order book rose 17% q-o-q to INR 1,879 crore from INR 1,600 crore, with about 14% executing in FY27, 59% in FY28 and 27% in FY29.

532799|2026-03.headline: Hubtown guides FY27 pre-sales of ~6,000 crore and collections of ~3,000 crore; 25 South/Downtown debt expected to fall at least 35% by end-FY27.
532799|2026-03.overview: Management hosted its Q4 and FY26 analyst meet, focusing on the promoter-entity mergers, project launches and debt reduction. In FY26 the company sold about 1 million sq ft, mainly in Mumbai, for roughly 4,400 crore of pre-sales and collected about 1,900 crore. About 11,300 crore of unrecognised revenue from booked sales sits in existing projects, with substantial recognition expected in FY27 on project completions. Two of the three promoter-entity mergers are NCLT-approved and the third awaits exchange approval. Refinancing of the roughly 15% legacy debt has slowed due to Middle East market conditions, and the proposed equity placement at 341 was cancelled in favour of a possible QIP.

financial_highlights.change: Management said both pre-sales and collections improved vs previous years; no exact percentage given

financial_highlights.value: approx. 1 million sq ft, primarily Mumbai

financial_highlights.metric: Unrecognised revenue from booked sales (existing projects)

financial_highlights.change: Construction finance for 25 West from ICICI at 12%

segments.name: 25 South / 25 Downtown (merging entities)
segments.commentary: 25 South is about 95% sold and expected to complete in FY27; 25 Downtown has sold almost 1.1 million sq ft of carpet area. Combined debt of these two is about 4,000 crore and management expects at least 35% reduction by end of this year.

segments.name: 25 West (Bandra)
segments.commentary: Fifth tower launched, selling about 1,40,000 sq ft; first tower completion expected next year. Construction finance from ICICI at about 12%.

segments.name: Rising City (Ghatkopar)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 (about 6.5 lakh sq ft): 5 of 6 towers have received OC; 6th tower OC expected in calendar 2026. Phase 2 (commercial offices) to be partly launched this year.

segments.name: Hubtown Seasons (Chembur)
segments.commentary: Phase 2 launch of about 500,000 sq ft expected this year, including a strata commercial building, one luxury and two mid-luxury buildings; phase 1 revenue expected in FY27.

segments.name: Mulund-Thane (Sunstream City)
segments.commentary: About 150 acres on seafront at Thane and Mulund, about 2.5 crore sq ft, not yet launched; environmental clearances being obtained and expected within months.

segments.name: Commercial (Gujarat and Pune)
segments.commentary: Four ongoing commercial projects in Pune, Ahmedabad, Mehsana and Baroda; three Gujarat projects expected to recognise substantial revenue this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance of around 6,000 crore and collections of around 3,000 crore.
Surplus collections to be used first to repay high-cost debt; at least 35% of combined 25 South and 25 Downtown debt expected to reduce by end of FY27.
25 South expected to complete this year; 25 West first tower next year; 6th Rising City tower OC within calendar 2026.
Launch pipeline this year: 25 Vistas (Thane), 25 Estates (Khalapur weekend homes), Seasons Chembur Phase 2, Rising City Phase 2 (partial), and a fifth tower at Mahalakshmi.
Management says returns to shareholders and stakeholders will start coming from FY27 onwards.
Mergers: 25 West and Ghatkopar holding entity merger expected this year; 25 South/Downtown awaiting exchange approval. Effective date of all mergers is 1 April 2025.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 350 acres and over 35 million sq ft; delivered 47+ projects, mainly in MMR.
Total ongoing and unlaunched pipeline stated as in excess of 1 lakh crore GDV; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore.
Launch-pending projects (excluding Sunstream) estimated at about 50,000 to 60,000 crore GDV, mostly on the floor per management.
Substantial increase in construction activity this year, which absorbed most of the cash outflow; approval and sales expenses also elevated.
Project funding taken for Seasons Chembur Phase 2 and 25 Estates to support launches; debt rose slightly this year as a result.
demand_pricing: Management says walk-in inquiries have not declined despite the slowdown; 25 Residences sold about 5,000 crore with zero advertising, per management.
Borivali product reportedly selling at 50,000 to 60,000 per sq ft; management expects prime-location products to hold demand.
Rising City Phase 2 commercial offices expected to do well given strong office market.
Management said price growth cannot be expected to be sharp, but prime-location product should avoid a cycle hit.

qa_highlights.question: Why does pro forma financing cost look high relative to combined debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest payable to DLF on Downtown's balance sheet was unprovided for 3-4 years due to disputes; it is now provisionally booked after settlement. Some further outflow until full repayment; Shapurji's share was small.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 15% cost of borrowing be refinanced lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing efforts continue but have slowed due to the last six months' market conditions and the Iran-US/Middle East situation; not expected in the immediate future.

qa_highlights.question: What is the year-end FY27 debt level for 25 South?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is combined across 25 South and 25 Downtown, not only 25 South; at least 35% of the total should go down by end of this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total GDV of the launch and pipeline projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Total including unlaunched and ongoing projects is over 1 lakh crore; 25 Downtown and Sunstream each about 40,000 to 50,000 crore; other launch projects about 50,000 to 60,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What happened to the equity placement at 341 per share?
qa_highlights.answer: It was cancelled because the market did not support the preference share issue; management is now looking at a QIP instead.

qa_highlights.question: Has the 6,000 crore asset-debt raise authorised last year been done?
qa_highlights.answer: No, not raised yet; the company is still trying.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Sunstream City plan and financing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 150 acres on the Thane/Mulund seafront; environmental clearances are the main hurdle and are expected within months; capital needs and financing will be planned after approvals.

risks_watch: Legacy debt at about 15% cost; refinancing stalled amid Middle East conflict and market conditions.
Unresolved exchange approval for the 25 South / 25 Downtown merger.
Sunstream City depends on environmental clearances for the seafront site; no launch timeline.
Equity raise: 341-price placement cancelled; QIP plan unconfirmed. The 6,000 crore asset-debt enabling resolution remains unused.
Collections guidance (3,000 crore) is well below pre-sales guidance (6,000 crore), so collection execution is key to deleveraging.
Management did not give a clear FY26 collections growth figure or FY27 operating cash flow number.

532799|2026-06.headline: Hubtown Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell 17% YoY to INR156 crore and PAT dropped 68% to INR27 crore under project completion accounting.
532799|2026-06.overview: Revenue and profit fell year on year because revenue is recognised only on occupation certificate and handover, and Q1 FY26 was a high base. Management stressed contracted pipeline (INR11,583 crore yet to flow through P&L), collections of INR320 crore and pre-sales of INR535 crore in the quarter. Merger of 25 Downtown, 25 West and 25 South entities remains subject to NCLT sanction, with the first two schemes approved by key authorities. Management guided pre-sales of about INR6,000 crore for FY27, weighted to Q3 and Q4, and collections of INR3,000 crore.

INR8,352 crore collected; INR3,252 crore recognised

segments.commentary: One tower handed over; second tower OC expected in FY27 and final tower by March 2027. Management described it as the top-selling residential project; Hubtown ranked number two top-selling developer in South Mumbai including merging entities.

segments.name: 25 Downtown / 25 West (merging entities)
segments.commentary: Under construction, not yet contributing to reported revenue. 25 West RCC targeted by end of 2026; Downtown Tower 5 launch planned around October-November 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for opening sales on floors 51 to 85 of 25 Downtown?
qa_highlights.answer: Vyomesh Shah said sales would commence from October onwards, opened strategically to capture higher prices on upper floors.

qa_highlights.question: Current cost of debt and refinancing plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of debt varies from 14% to 20% by site; refinancing being explored for about INR2,800 crore of higher-cost debt, with no term sheets finalised yet.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for equity fundraise?
qa_highlights.answer: Enabling resolutions in place for preferential issue and/or QIP including FCCB, but timing awaits better markets. A USD150 million (about INR1,400 crore) FCCB was discussed, preferably in a single tranche.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 collections target and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections target of INR3,000 crore; linked to construction progress under RERA, with Q2 to Q4 inflows from 25 South, 25 West, Ghatkopar and Chembur OC-related receipts.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter holding after mergers and pledge status?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding expected around 68%; two promoter pledges continuing, with management aiming to release them in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to address low ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited refinancing at lower rates, rising realisations and deliveries as drivers of ROE improvement; no specific ROE target given.

risks_watch: Revenue lumpiness from completion-method accounting; reported earnings may stay weak until OCs and handovers in Q3-Q4 FY27.

532805|2026-06.headline: Redington Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR34,966 crores and PAT 77% to INR486 crores, helped by PC price-led stock-and-sell.
532805|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR34,966 crores (+34% YoY), EBITDA INR751 crores (+67%) and PAT INR486 crores (+77%), with profit growth outpacing revenue. Excluding Arena, revenue grew 41% to INR33,794 crores and profit was INR517 crores, which management called the best ever. India grew 63% on top line and was the strongest geography, while Middle East & Africa grew 15% despite the West Asia crisis, with UAE and Saudi softening. Management attributed a large part of ESG growth to component-shortage-driven price increases and channel stocking, and flagged that large data-center deals will dilute margin percentage. Arena continued to lose money (INR64 crores total, INR31 crores Redington share).

financial_highlights.value: INR64 crores total; INR31 crores Redington share

financial_highlights.change: vs INR31 crores in Q1 FY26

Arena: hypercompetitive Turkey market with gross margin compression; revenue roughly halved.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stock-and-sell effect is largely in ESG PCs; channel holds about 2-3 months of inventory, and the build is across distributors and Tier 2 partners.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on large deals and India mobility growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR700 crores of the INR1,000 crore large deals came from India data centers; funnel is multiple times that. Premium smartphone share gains helped Mobility, but management is unsure if demand holds after price rises.

qa_highlights.question: Middle East demand in UAE and Saudi, and cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: UAE was down about 3-4% and Saudi slightly more; some freight and warehousing cost passed on, while about $3 million of extra cost sat in opex.

qa_highlights.question: Why Arena losses persist and what is the end goal?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue halved, margins compressed and opex inflated by 35-40%; management says structural options are being evaluated and losses may continue this year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose industry-wide, but better payable days, especially in Middle East from additional vendor credit, offset it; spikes occurred within the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance costs rise 74% QoQ, and what was the INR147 crore tax refund?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher revenue and inventory days raised interest, and market rates firmed though central bank rates were unchanged. The refund related to contested past-year demands that the company won.

532805|2026-09.headline: Redington Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR43,002 crores and PAT excluding exceptionals rose 50% to INR581 crores, with Arena still loss-making.
532805|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and PAT, with growth broad across India, GCC, Africa and the UAE, led by TSG (up 91%) on AI server and GPU migration. H1 FY27 consolidated revenue reached INR77,967 crores (up 41%) and PAT excluding exceptionals INR1,067 crores (up 61%). Arena remained the drag: revenue fell 37% YoY and Redington's share of loss was INR115 crores, including transition and impairment charges. Management flagged elevated receivable provisions, inventory above comfortable levels, rising debt, and possible softening in consumer demand after price increases.

segments.name: India distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution business grew 67% YoY in the quarter, the fastest of the regions cited.

segments.name: Rest of World ex-Arena
segments.commentary: Grew 38% YoY; GCC and Levant ex-UAE/KSA +121%, UAE +39%, Africa +35%, Middle East overall +41%.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 40% YoY and was 34% of consolidated revenue; SISA geography grew 70%; Rest of World Mobility grew 34% ex-Arena.

segments.name: Endpoint Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 38% YoY to 30% of revenue, driven mainly by higher ASPs plus a sequential rise in commercial PC volumes; highest quarterly revenue to date.

segments.name: Technology Solutions Group (TSG)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 91% YoY to 20% of mix; large deals above INR3,800 crores (about 9% of group revenue), mostly data centres and neo-cloud. Ex-large deals TSG grew about 33-35%.

segments.name: Software Solutions Group (SSG)
segments.commentary: Grew 39% YoY to 15% of revenue, with all SBUs growing, led by cybersecurity and cloud; SSG gross margin above 6%.

segments.name: Arena (Turkey)
segments.commentary: Revenue down 37% YoY; exited the VDF contract and high-interest Lira working capital business; new management in place; Q2 loss includes transition provisions and impairment.

guidance_outlook: Management sees H2 FY27 growth north of 25% at overall business level, with caveats on price-driven demand contraction and West Asia impact on UAE, KSA and GCC.
H2 seasonality is expected to be muted this year because price increases and shortages pulled consumption forward; H2 is normally bigger than H1.
Sustainable quarterly opex guided at INR950-1,000 crores.
TSG expected to be the strongest growth driver in H2, followed by SSG; ESG and MSG approached with more caution due to price-volume elasticity.
Neo-cloud opportunity in India estimated at INR150,000 crores over the next four years; data centre margins below the 4.5-5% run-rate, with ROCE targets maintained.
Management expects SSG and TSG gross margin to improve over 3-5 years through orchestration and services; debt-equity may rise, with equity raise possible if growth needs it.
capex_capacity: Funded capital investment for the data centre large deals is almost nil; only non-funded (bank guarantee) capacity is used, per the CFO India.
Funding strategy: additional debt is currently sufficient; dividend moderation or equity raise are options if the growth trend requires it.
Debt-equity is about 0.5-0.6x; management cited global distribution peers at 0.6-0.8x and said distribution is working-capital intensive, typically above 1:1.
Five AI learning centres rolled out in India over the last two quarters (CSR); AI COE launched in Singapore with a physical experience centre and a virtual COE in build.
demand_pricing: Smartphone and PC prices up roughly 30-50% YoY; enterprise AI PC adoption above 40% in commercial, consumer around 10%.
Consumer PC/smartphone units declining; Microsoft activation data down 20-30% for consumer, while commercial PC activation is 0-7% growth.
Enterprise is about two-thirds of Redington's PC business and consumer about one-third; Mobility is roughly equal consumer-type, so IT is about half-half.
Management views market share as flat to a slight gain, with no loss.
Channel inventory above comfortable levels as partners hold stock ahead of price increases; Middle East supply chains stressed (Strait of Hormuz closed, alternate routes adding turnaround time).
Gross margin ex-large deals about 5.13%; reported gross margin broadly similar QoQ.
AI exchange platform in early traction, engaging hundreds of partners; described as a long-term journey.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins trending down despite lower Mobility mix, and how sustainable is the TSG large-deal pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the TSG jump is a CPU-to-GPU migration with roughly 4x ASPs, not just pricing, and expects it to continue. CFO said margins ex-large deals were 5.13%, similar to last year, and that Arena's higher-margin local-currency business in prior-year quarters affects comparison.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Arena losses rise to about INR70 crores in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were three components: business loss, Lira transition provisions (rebates and discounts not aligned with vendor support), and a INR40 crore intangibles impairment. Business loss alone was much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What is sustainable opex and what provisions were taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex was elevated by receivable provisions, SSG investments, and Middle East war-related insurance costs. Sustainable run-rate is INR950-1,000 crores per quarter. Receivable provisions were about INR213 crores (INR67 crores SISA, INR135 crores Arena); inventory provisioning was not material.

qa_highlights.question: How will growth be funded and what are the levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is sufficient for now; levers include more debt, moderating dividends, or raising equity, which will be used if the growth trend requires it. Debt-equity of 0.5-0.6x was described as comfortable versus 0.6-0.8x for global peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 growth exceed 25%, and is there seasonality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no reason to pull back from north of 25% H2 growth, with caveats on price-led demand contraction and West Asia impact. Seasonality is expected to be muted because price increases pulled demand forward.

qa_highlights.question: Would a slowdown in AI capex affect the FY29/FY30 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said TSG and data-centre business would be affected by any AI capex pullback; SSG (cloud, security) and smartphones less so. PCs could see some impact, but the market is expected to rationalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the neo-cloud opportunity and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: India neo-cloud capacity is expected to go from 1.5 GW to 7 GW and then 12 GW; INR150,000 crore opportunity over four years. Margins are below the 4.5-5% run rate, but ROCE targets are maintained with less incremental opex.

qa_highlights.question: When will Arena turn around?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Arena has exited high-interest Lira working capital business and is near the end of that transition, but partner health and Turkish market issues make a turnaround timeline hard to estimate.

risks_watch: Arena (Turkey) receivables and liquidity, plus a new management team and further restructuring; Q2 loss of INR115 crores including INR40 crore impairment.
Price-led demand elasticity in consumer PCs and smartphones after 30-50% price increases; possible post-Diwali demand contraction.
Channel inventory above comfortable levels, with working-capital build and Q2 FCF of negative INR1,871 crores.
West Asia conflict impact on UAE, KSA and GCC, including logistics, collection cycles and insurance costs.
TSG large deals are lumpy in data centres; AI capex pullback risk for TSG and FY29/FY30 targets.
Rising debt and possible equity raise or dividend moderation as working capital grows.

Management repeatedly flagged unknowns and declined to estimate Arena's turnaround timing. The CEO took the call from hospital, which the CFO noted, so answers were brief.

rows.why: AI exchange platform is in early traction with hundreds of partners and the AI COE in Singapore is under construction, but no commercial product launch dates were given.

532808|2026-03.headline: Pearl Global FY26 consolidated revenue rose 11.5% to INR5,025 crore; adjusted EBITDA margin 9.3% (10.3% ex tariff and new-facility losses).
532808|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,314 crore (+6.9% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA (ex-ESOP) of INR135 crore at a 10.3% margin, the highest quarterly margin to date. FY26 PAT rose 17% to INR270 crore, helped by cost restructuring, while India volumes fell sharply in Q4 as US tariffs shifted orders to other countries. Management guided to a 10% group EBITDA margin for FY27 and a 12-14% revenue CAGR, with FY28 capacity of 125-130 million pieces. The company also raised its dividend to a record INR14.50 per share for FY26.

segments.name: India (standalone)
segments.commentary: Q4 India revenue fell about 23% as the US tariff pushed orders out of India; management says Q4 India EBITDA ex-tariff was 9.6% versus 10.2% a year earlier. Target is high single-digit EBITDA for FY27 and double-digit in Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Bangladesh
segments.commentary: Strong export growth to the US, UK, EU, Spain and Canada; capex of about 6 million pieces due H1 CY2027, with two new units (washing and stitching) ready in H2 this year.

segments.name: Vietnam
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation rose to 80%+ from 63%; management is buying land for a greenfield project and considering in-house capacity over partner factories.

segments.name: Indonesia
segments.commentary: Utilisation rose to 47% from 39% last year; the company will buy an extra 10% of PT Pinnacle Apparels for $1.4 million, taking its stake to 99.92%.

segments.name: Guatemala
segments.commentary: Losses continuing; strategy reworked and management expects breakeven in FY27. The Other segment (Indonesia, Dubai, US, Guatemala) drove the Q4 spike, not Guatemala alone.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group adjusted EBITDA margin guided at about 10%, then 10-12% in subsequent years, with the 10% considered largely operational.
Revenue CAGR of 12-14% targeted at group level; management says the INR6,000 crore FY28 target (set in 2023) is achievable even at about 9% growth.
FY28 target: 125-130 million pieces of established capacity and about 100 million pieces shipped, to reach INR6,000 crore.
FY27 capex of INR200-250 crore being outlined across geographies; INR250 crore already committed for completion by H1 FY27.
Expected realisation gain from the removal of tariff costs, though hard to quantify as costing is reset each season; current realisation about INR635-640 per garment, with a goal of INR600+.
Guatemala expected to reach breakeven in FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 101 million pieces per annum as of 31 March 2026, crossing 100 million ahead of an H1 FY27 target.
Bangladesh expansion adds about 6-7 million pieces in FY27; CWIP INR110 crore, expected to reach about INR150 crore after H1 FY27 capitalisation.
Vietnam land parcel identified; purchase consideration $2.5-3 million; greenfield plans to follow.
Management targets an additional 20-25 million pieces, combining capex and partner capacity, over the next two years; a laundry capex in Bangladesh will lift margins without adding top line.
Bihar plant is in ramp-up; the company adds capacity line by line, with partner factories used alongside in-house (target roughly 80-85% in-house).
demand_pricing: India order book is seeing good traction after the US tariff eased; EU and UK customers are interested in India under the FTAs, and some are seeking added capacity there.
US consumer demand has held up despite inflation; management says there is no sign yet of the weakness seen in 2022 at about $110 oil.
Raw material costs are typically passed through within 1-2 months of order booking, and fabric is bought once orders are placed.
Muji has crossed about $65 million in turnover and is in the top 6 clients; UNIQLO is not a current priority due to competitive overlap.
Discounts and burden-sharing to US clients during the tariff period weighed on India margins; part of the 10% US tariff is still being absorbed.
Design team grew from about 70-75 to just over 100 people.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India revenue fall about 23% in Q4 and what drove growth in the Other segment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India orders shifted out under the high US tariff, with existing orders shipped by December-January. Growth in overseas business came from volume and value-added products in Bangladesh, Vietnam and Indonesia; the Other segment includes Indonesia, Dubai, US and Guatemala, not Guatemala alone.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 10% margin be sustained in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10% is achievable for FY27, given the removal of reciprocal tariff costs and the Guatemala and Bihar ramp-up, with Q4 seasonally strongest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR6,000 crore FY28 target consistent with INR630 realisation and 100 million pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR6,000 crore target dates from 2023 and is expected to be exceeded; the company plans 12-14% group CAGR, with growth rotating across countries.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is needed beyond INR250 crore for 25-30 million pieces?
qa_highlights.answer: INR250 crore covers the committed program; FY27 capex could be INR200-250 crore, and the total may exceed that, combining in-house and partner capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tariff cost likely to be in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR36 crore tariff cost will fall significantly, possibly to INR5-8 crore, with some burden share continuing at about 10%.

qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani cited three drivers: TAM expansion as clients need AI scaffolding; share gains from challenger brands playing offense; and clients willing to move work away from in-house delivery with compelling commercial constructs.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q4 softer than expected, and what drove it?

qa_highlights.answer: Ritesh Idnani argued that clients buy one continuous motion across implement, run and transform rather than pillars; Firstsource's size and domain depth in regulated workflows let it assemble teams around the customer problem.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said efficiency saves from automation and offshoring fund new capabilities, and it remains confident of the FY27 margin guidance; FY26 margin expansion was about 74bps.

532810|2026-03.headline: PFC FY26 standalone PAT hit a record INR 20,051 crore (+16% YoY), but FY27 spread guided lower at 2.40-2.50% and loan growth at ~10%.
532810|2026-03.overview: PFC reported its highest-ever standalone net profit of INR 20,051 crore for FY26, up 16% YoY, helped by 13% NII growth and about INR 1,800 crore of provision reversals. Net NPA fell to 0.13% and net credit-impaired ratio to a new low of 0.15%, after resolution of Sinnar Thermal and TRN Energy. Disbursements were INR 1,65,414 crore and loan book grew about 7% to ~INR 5.8 lakh crore, with management blaming elevated prepayments in a falling-rate cycle. Management guided FY27 spread to 2.40-2.50% and loan growth to around 10%, and outlined the proposed PFC-REC merger targeted for 1 April 2027.

Management does not expect further RBI rate cuts in FY27 (repo held at 5.25%); expects prepayment pressure to moderate.

Peak power demand hit an all-time high of 256 GW in April 2026.

Sanctioned-but-undisbursed pool estimated at INR 2.5-3 lakh crore (approximate, per management).

Forex volatility (rupee depreciation vs USD and EUR, Middle East conflict, trade tariffs) raised FY26 funding costs; hedging covers 97% of USD 10.3 billion foreign currency borrowing, with management saying most mark-to-market losses are notional until maturity.
Borrowing mix: 80:20 domestic-foreign; 65% fixed-rate; 60% bonds, 20% bank term loans, 20% foreign currency (per management).
Repayments from borrowers in FY26 were about INR 1,28,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did disbursements and loan growth weaken despite stable disbursement volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said disbursements were broadly flat (INR 1,65,414 crore vs ~INR 1,68,000 crore) but DISCOMs shifted from short-tenor RBPF revolving loans (~6-month average) to 3-7 year loans, reducing rollover-driven disbursement counts; competition from banks also present.

qa_highlights.question: Why is only a fraction of sanctions disbursed and what is the timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 sanctions were ~INR 2.85 lakh crore with ~INR 80,000 crore disbursed; infrastructure disbursements are slow due to pre-commitment conditions, environmental and land approvals, and pick up near commissioning. Management said the balance is spilling over, not cancelled.

qa_highlights.question: How will the merger affect the government shareholding and borrowing limits?
qa_highlights.answer: Government shareholding would fall to about 41-42% post share swap; management said the government has committed to keep the merged entity a government company, with modalities yet to be decided. Single-borrower exposure limit to banks would fall from 25% to 20% for the merged entity, which management does not see as a challenge.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend and ROE outlook post-merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend is 30% of PFC's standalone profit, of which PFC receives REC dividend as income; post-merger dividend will be declared on combined profit under DIPAM's 30% policy, subject to RBI rules. No ROE guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How does PFC view the impact of a potential future rate hike?
qa_highlights.answer: About 65% of borrowings are fixed-rate and bond liabilities average 5-6 years, so repricing is gradual; lending rates are linked to the weighted cost of borrowing, so a rate rise would transmit slowly as older debt matures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the FY27 spread decline and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 2.40-2.50% versus 2.46% in FY26, citing competitive lending rates, prepayment pressure and forex-driven funding costs; the spread is calculated on weighted average cost including foreign borrowings.

Rupee volatility and Middle East conflict could raise hedging and translation costs on USD 10.3 billion foreign borrowing; ~97% hedged.

New ECL norms from April 2027 under RBI; management says current policy broadly in sync with RBI IRAC norms.

The company guided to 15-20% revenue growth and double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, with an order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, but gave no formal PAT guidance.

segments.name: CSMT Mumbai (order value INR2,076 crores ex-GST)
segments.commentary: Designs now approved and execution has picked up after a slow 1.5 years. FY27 execution target is about INR600 crores.

segments.name: Dahlias (private)
segments.commentary: FY27 execution target about INR400 crores.

segments.name: IJPM - India Jewellery Park (Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Design changes ongoing; ground work expected to start in the last month of Q1 FY27 after the Mumbai monsoon. FY27 target kept modest at about INR100 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20%, up from the 10-15% guidance given in prior years.
EBITDA margin expected to reach double digits in FY27 (currently 9.5% in FY26); management said margins will rise over the next two years as mechanisation takes effect.
FY27 order inflow target of about INR8,000 crores, including two L1 positions worth INR1,620.95 crores (RML Hospital Delhi and an Odisha government university project in Bhubaneswar).
FY27 capex about INR300 crores, down from an earlier guidance of about INR500 crores; FY26 capex was about INR274 crores.
Q1 FY27 expected to be very slow due to elections, labour exodus and Eid; ramp-up from Q2 and H2 significantly above H1.
Management said no guidance is prudent beyond FY27 given headwinds; a FY28 number was not given. Share buyback 'not in the offing'.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR274 crores; FY27 capex planned at about INR300 crores, with depreciation rising in line.

Mechanisation (tower cranes, passenger hoists costing INR50-70 lakh each, batching plants, concrete pumps) is the stated response to labour shortage. Management estimated the IRR uplift at 7-10% and payback at 4-5 years on equipment with a 4-year life; other assets have a 7-8 year life.
Q4 depreciation was about INR29 crores; management expects a similar run-rate going forward.
Management is evaluating precast and pre-engineered building technologies, but said these would take 2-3 years to be used on projects.

Management is walking away from some projects, including with existing clients, and is raising bid margins by a couple of percentage points or more.
Pipeline has been slowed by the war, with developers delaying launches. The company is bidding selectively with existing or well-funded clients.
Competitors named: L&T, B&F, Nagarjuna, Shapoorji Pallonji, Kalpataru and Tata Projects.

qa_highlights.question: Will execution ramp up in FY27-28, and what growth should be expected?

qa_highlights.question: Why are capex and depreciation rising while margins lag, and is this a new normal?

qa_highlights.question: How are cost inflation and fuel-price increases being protected against?

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin fall was due to inflation vs. disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gross margin decline mainly to under-absorbed IDC and overheads from lost execution days, plus staff cost increments taken in January; inflation was a smaller factor, largely covered by escalation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed-price share, and how is margin protected in the order book?

qa_highlights.question: Are IJPM and the two L1 projects likely to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: RML Hospital (Delhi) and an Odisha university project are old tenders with no LOA date. Either side can rebid or cancel if escalation has moved too far.

Q1 FY27 expected to be very weak, so FY27 growth depends on a strong H2.

Pipeline slowdown and possible cancellation or rebidding of the two L1 orders.

532811|2026-06.headline: Ahluwalia Q1 FY27 PAT fell 77.65% to INR11.42 crore on 4.29% EBITDA margin, as AIIMS Jammu bill cut and NCR labour cost spike hit margins; FY27 double-digit margin ruled out.
532811|2026-06.overview: Turnover rose 12.03% YoY to INR1,125.81 crore, but PAT fell to INR11.42 crore from INR51.11 crore, with EBITDA margin at 4.29% versus 8.59%. Management attributed the drop to a INR29 crore AIIMS Jammu bill reduction (2.6 percentage points), labour cost increases of roughly 35-40% in NCR (about 50% of the order book), higher staff costs, and SIR/election-related disruption in West Bengal and Assam. Net order book stands at INR20,663.52 crore, with only INR512.81 crore of inflow in FY27 to date. Management guided to 12-15% top-line growth but ruled out double-digit EBITDA margin for FY27, and did not give a firm date for margin recovery.

financial_highlights.value: Sharp increase YoY; mgmt expects similar ~INR15-16 crore per quarter
financial_highlights.change: due to mobilisation advance for Central Vista

segments.name: NCR projects (about 50% of order book)
segments.commentary: Labour minimum wages rose about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled categories in Haryana and UP, with projects running at 40-50% labour strength. Management estimated a company-level EBITDA hit of about 1.5% this quarter, up to 5% of turnover on some projects where material is client-issued.

segments.name: AIIMS Jammu
segments.commentary: Final bill reduced by INR29 crore after finalisation; the matter is going to arbitration. Impact is 2.6 percentage points on EBITDA. Management says the project is closed and no further hit is expected.

segments.name: Central Vista (Ministry of Housing/CPWD-type govt project)
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR700 crore billing in FY27 and about INR1,000 crore in FY28, with Nirman Bhawan demolition complete and Udyog Bhawan 90% demolished. Full project completes in FY29.

segments.name: CST (Mumbai railway station project)
segments.commentary: Q1 billing about INR70 crore; management targets about INR400-450 crore for FY27 (hoping to cross INR500 crore total) and about INR700 crore in FY28. Earlier target was about INR600 crore.

segments.commentary: Work on ground delayed by client design changes; expected to start in Q3 FY27. Targets INR100 crore billing in FY27 and about INR450 crore in FY28; 3.5-year completion.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 EBITDA margin so low, and was the labour cost rise known at the last call (about 15 days/45 days after quarter end)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the labour increase was not known at the last call, citing a sharp NCR minimum wage hike of about 35-40% for skilled and unskilled labour, with projects at 40-50% labour strength. Management disputed the suggestion it had withheld information and declined further debate, offering site visits instead.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins recover, and when will client compensation flow through; is double-digit margin possible in Q3 or FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Compensation timing cannot be dated, but some is expected over the next two quarters. Double-digit EBITDA margin is ruled out for FY27; management hopes to return to Q1 FY26 margins over the next three quarters. NGT impact on Q3 is unquantified. FY28 double-digit is an aspiration, hard to predict.

qa_highlights.question: Is top-line guidance changing (12-15% vs 15%)?

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost jump and recurrence; interest-bearing mobilisation advance?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost rose due to mobilisation advance taken for Central Vista; similar INR15-16 crore per quarter expected. Of INR924 crore mobilisation advance, 31% is interest-bearing at around 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Inflow guidance and bidding stance after Odisha university bid lapsed?
qa_highlights.answer: The Odisha university bid (about INR1,620 crore L1) lapsed after the company refused a bid validity extension on a fixed-price contract. RML (about INR500 crore) remains L1 but not converted. FY27 inflow now seen at INR4,000-5,000 crore versus INR8,000 crore earlier; bidding will be less aggressive.

qa_highlights.question: How much labour-cost impact is quantifiable, and how much of it is recoverable?
qa_highlights.answer: Company-level EBITDA hit about 1.5% this quarter; project-level impact 2% to about 5% of turnover where material is client-issued. Without escalation the hit is about 1%, as some contracts escalate after 6-12 months. Management cited incentives from developers for stage-wise completion as partial offset.
