532814|2026-03.headline: Indian Bank Q4 FY26: Q4 net profit Rs 3,103 crore (+1.3% QoQ), FY26 profit Rs 12,156 crore (+11.33%), gross NPA cut to 1.98%.
532814|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a decent year, beating guidance on most parameters except cost-to-income, with advances up 13.43% led by RAM (+15.18%) and corporate growth reviving to 9.19%. Gross NPA fell 111 bps to 1.98% and annualised Q4 slippage eased to 0.85%, while NIM for the year declined 17 bps to 3.24%. Management guided FY27 to tighter NIM (3.10%-3.25%), ROA (1.20%-1.30%) and growth (advances 11%-13%), citing rising cost of deposits and lower treasury income. ECL impact was not quantified; management said it would be absorbed over one to three quarters and that the final guidelines were received only the day before the call.

financial_highlights.change: down from 46.90% in December; above guidance

financial_highlights.value: Rs 31,000 crore (SMA-0 ~Rs 16,000 cr, SMA-1 ~Rs 9,000 cr, SMA-2 ~Rs 6,000 cr)
About Rs 310 crore (management cited Rs 400-500 crore MOC in Q4)

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 18.72% and MSME 16.39% within RAM (+15.18%); about 6 lakh loans and Rs 48,000 crore sanctioned to MSME. Personal loans only Rs 6,500 crore and MFI Rs 3,300 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.19% after about 3% last year; corporate sanctions about Rs 1.31 trillion. Exposure to NBFCs fell about Rs 8,000 crore, with about 99% rated AAA/AA/A.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Overseas book runs through GIFT City and Singapore branches (plus Sri Lanka), mainly syndicated loans and trade finance across sectors.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital business grew 63% to Rs 272,000 crore; mobile banking users 2.36 crore; 94% of transactions digital; 97% of retail and agri loans sanctioned digitally.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 9%-11%; advances growth 11%-13%; CASA around 40%; CD ratio around 80%.
FY27 NIM 3.10%-3.25% (cost of deposits to stay elevated as advances outpace deposits); ROA 1.20%-1.30%.
FY27 gross NPA 1.50%-1.60%; net NPA below 0.25%; credit cost below 1%; slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recoveries Rs 4,500-5,500 crore (vs guidance Rs 5,500-6,500 crore in FY26); written-off book recovery Rs 1,200-1,500 crore.
Treasury profit expected around Rs 1,000-1,200 crore for FY27; LCR to be kept around 115%-120%.
ECL impact to be absorbed over roughly one to three quarters; management said some spill-over into FY28 is likely. Numbers to be given later.
Management said it is comfortable with growth 1%-2% below industry, prioritising NIM and asset quality.
capex_capacity: Opened 102 branches so far; target about 300 branches over three years, described as on track.
IND Optima cash management launched with 150-plus corporate customers onboarded.
Digital pipeline: corporate CRM, corporate ecosystem engine, RFP creator, invoice processing, intelligent document reader, IND UPI app upgrade, and automated suspicious transaction reporting.
Digital and IT budget to be roughly equivalent to employee cost, per Ashutosh Choudhury.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: jewel loans (16%-17% of book, Rs 1.27 trillion) grew about 28% last year on gold price rises; management does not expect similar growth this year.
Around 50% of the loan book is linked to external benchmarks, leaving little repricing lever; MCLR-linked loans are the main remaining lever.
Retail term deposit rates will not be cut because bulk deposit rates are elevated; bulk and CD together are about 18%-19% of deposits, kept under 20%.
Pipeline Rs 51,000 crore, of which sanctioned but unavailed term loans about Rs 34,000-35,000 crore; focus on green energy, transmission, data centres and roads.
Textile remains stressed for about two years; management says little leather exposure.
Average SA balance (ex-BSBD) rose to Rs 46,000 from Rs 30,000; average current account balance rose to Rs 2.64 lakh from Rs 1.88 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the bank for the final ECL guidelines, and how large is the hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final guidelines came the day before and impact will be a little higher than draft estimates, adding the HTM book is now included. It declined to give a number yet, saying it would give concrete figures later, and expects the impact to be absorbed over one to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia war and tariffs raise slippages? What about SMA trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 slippage rose on about Rs 400-500 crore of March MOC, which recurs each March. SMA fell mainly because two government accounts left SMA-2; management also said some stress has been present since tariffs in August but is not visible in SMA.

qa_highlights.question: How will treasury income trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said treasury will be lower but not as severe as last year, since securities have not been sold at low yields. It expects Rs 1,000-1,200 crore of treasury profit for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank measuring the revenue benefit of digital investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits are real but not quantified; cited 94% digital transactions (branch visits cost at least 5x more), and said it will try to quantify going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What levers exist on the asset side if cost of deposits rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said few levers remain since about 50% of loans are external-benchmark linked; MCLR-linked loans may reprice up. It is focusing on mid-sized corporates of Rs 50-500 crore for better pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and why is it so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Average LCR was 127% (currently 123%-124%). Management said 115%-120% is a fair operating level and that excess SLR holdings support the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AFS reserve movement?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS reserve moved from about Rs 400 crore in December to minus Rs 200 crore in March, per management.

risks_watch: ECL transition: impact not quantified; some spill-over into FY28 expected; HTM book now included; management has not disclosed existing floating/standard provisions beyond about Rs 500 crore standard-asset provisions in Q4.
Cost of deposits rising with advances outpacing deposits; NIM guidance cut to 3.10%-3.25%.
Recoveries falling (Rs 7,600 crore to Rs 6,600 crore) and treasury income lower in FY27.
Cost-to-income ratio ended FY26 at 46.03%, above guidance; management said course correction is underway.
MSME stress if industry weakens; textile sector weak for about two years; monitor SMA-0 (up to about Rs 16,000 crore).
532814|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability, with a clear message that growth is secondary to NIM and asset quality. Cautious and somewhat evasive on ECL quantum and on the cost-of-deposit outlook, saying numbers will come later.
key_quotes: So, if I summarize the result, I think it has been a decent year, almost all parameters except cost-to- income ratio, we have done better than our guidance.
But, having said that, let me assure you, all of you, that impact is not going to be very huge.
We will give you concrete numbers so that variation is minimum.
So, my focus is, of course, growth, but NIM and asset quality should also remain intact.
So, in NPA, in fact, we are not holding any floating provision, NPA whatever we are making only a specific account-wise provision.

532814|2026-09.headline: Indian Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 14.71% to Rs 3,462 crore, helped by Rs 1,134 crore NSE MTM gain; guidance raised to 11-12% deposit and 13-14% advances growth.
532814|2026-09.overview: Indian Bank reported Q2 FY27 with total business up 14.22%, advances up 16.39% and deposits up 12.50% year on year. Profit was lifted by NSE-related gains (Rs 252 crore realised plus Rs 1,134 crore MTM), while operating profit excluding NSE grew about 18%. Management raised deposit and advances growth guidance, and flagged ECL provisioning (Rs 1,500 crore this quarter, Rs 2,500 crore cumulative) and a possible one-time HTM mark-to-market hit from 1 April. CASA ratio improved year on year to 39.36% but slipped sequentially on FCNR(B) inflows.

segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.06% YoY. About Rs 10,000 crore of MSME limits remains undrawn.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.92% YoY. Pipeline of Rs 63,000 crore: Rs 30,000 crore sanctioned but undisbursed, Rs 10,000 crore in-principle approved, around Rs 23,000 crore early stage. Growth target now 10-12%.

segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 17.74% YoY and constitute about 67% of the loan book.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Treasury income ex-NSE was Rs 290 crore in Q2 (Rs 293 crore a year ago) and Rs 794 crore in H1 (Rs 854 crore). Net MTM loss of about Rs 11 crore. Management expects muted treasury income going forward.

segments.name: International book
segments.commentary: Loans against FCNR(B) deposits of about USD 2 billion were extended at preferential rates, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value; this drove advances growth and is expected not to recur fully next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standard asset provisions rise from Rs 733 crore to Rs 1,882 crore, and what drove miscellaneous income to Rs 468 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: ECL provision of Rs 1,500 crore this quarter and Rs 1,000 crore last quarter, totalling Rs 2,500 crore, against an expected total impact of Rs 3,500 crore. Other income includes Rs 271 crore of interest on an income tax refund, which may not recur.

qa_highlights.question: Where will treasury income come from?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects muted treasury income and does not expect high profits; not budgeted for high treasury gains. Forex income guidelines from RBI are being assessed.

qa_highlights.question: Will deposit and credit growth continue, and what drives NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: 12% deposit growth expected to be maintained; advances growth of 14-15% expected next quarter. NIM to rise 6-7 bps (later framed as 5-6 bps) this quarter, with bulk deposits repricing later.

qa_highlights.question: How much FCNR(B) was raised and how much is lent against it?
qa_highlights.answer: USD 2.3 billion (about Rs 21,000 crore) raised; fully utilised, with no surplus liquidity. Loans against it of roughly USD 2 billion, with customers borrowing 90-96% of deposit value.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL recurring impact and is it passed on through pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Recurring impact of 10-15 bps maintained. Management does not expect clear pass-through to borrowers; models take 1.5-2 years to stabilise. LGD uses five years of history.

qa_highlights.question: What is the HTM mark-to-market exposure and could RBI provide an HTM reserve?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 3,500 crore covers only the credit book; HTM MTM would be additional, and the 10-year yield at 7.41% could cause a large impact across banks. Bank will first take it up with RBI.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of UCC guidelines on capital?
qa_highlights.answer: One-time CET1 and Tier 2 adjustment, with unutilised limits now included in credit RWA. CRAR at 16.21%, expected at 17-17.5% by March-end.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the borrowing increase and the LCR?

532815|2026-03.headline: SMS Pharma FY26 revenue rose 13% to INR887 crores and EBITDA margin reached 20%; FY27 guidance is 15% revenue growth.
532815|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR238 crores with EBITDA of INR40 crores (17% margin) and gross margin down about 2% QoQ on higher solvent costs. For FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR887 crores, EBITDA rose 23% to INR171 crores (20% margin), and PAT rose 47% to INR102 crores, including INR14 crores from associate VKT Pharma. Management framed FY26 as a foundation-building year, with benefits expected in FY27 and FY28 from backward integration, new products and capacity. FY27 guidance is 15% revenue growth and an EBITDA margin above 20%, with management citing Middle East logistics risk as the reason for prudence.

qa_highlights.answer: Ibuprofen backward integration takes capacity from 500 to 800 MT per month; a brownfield block of 4-5 new APIs is also being built. Both are due by March 2027, with incremental revenue from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margins are achievable in the next 2-3 years?

Gross margin was 35% and EBITDA rose 40% to INR68 crore at a 21% margin, with PAT up 57% to INR39.6 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 19% to INR523 crore and PAT grew 36% to INR59.8 crore. Management now expects to exceed both the 15% revenue growth and 20% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27.

532822|2026-03.headline: Vodafone Idea booked a Rs 55,622 Cr AGR-related exceptional gain, lifting Q4 FY26 net profit to Rs 51,970 Cr, while Q4 revenue grew 2.9% YoY to Rs 11,332 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Network opex fell sequentially despite site additions; is this sustainable?

532822|2026-06.headline: Vodafone Idea posted its first positive net subscriber addition since merger in Q1 FY27, with revenue up 6.0% YoY to Rs 11,689 Crore and Cash EBITDA up 13.5% to Rs 2,475 Crore.

Funding improved with Rs 1,183 Crore of warrant proceeds from the Aditya Birla Group, a first tranche of Rs 6,400 Crore in total, and rating upgrades to Crisil A-/Stable and ICRA A-(Stable).

532827|2026-03.headline: Page Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 14.1% to INR12,526 million on 10.8% volume growth; FY26 EBITDA margin 22%, guided to 19-21% for FY27.
532827|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 14.1% YoY to INR12,526 million, with volume up 10.8% to 54.5 million pieces and PAT up 9% to INR1,787 million. Management attributed the pickup to better consumer sentiment, a correction in distributor inventory that aligned secondary and primary sales, and product upgrades, with March the strongest month. EBITDA margin was 20.8% in the quarter and 22% for FY26, but management guided to a 19-21% range for FY27 citing marketing normalising to 5% of sales, input cost inflation and technology investments. Price increases were small: a 2% weighted average taken in January on product enhancements, with a further price increase planned in Q1 FY27 to cover input costs.

segments.commentary: Athleisure is reviving after distributor inventory correction; outerwear and value-added premium products are supporting premiumisation. Management did not give category-level growth numbers.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp volume acceleration to double digits, and what initiatives contributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited better consumer demand in Q4 and recovery in athleisure after distributor inventory correction. Primary and secondary sales are now closely aligned, and March was strong. Management said upstocking was not encouraged and festive timing played little role.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 19-21% EBITDA margin range still hold after input cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management reiterated 19-21% for FY27, citing marketing at 5%, gross margin levels and salary costs as the basis. FY26 margin was higher because marketing was below 5% and gross margin held up.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 margin 22% and why should it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY26 benefited from marketing below 5% of sales and sustained gross margin. Normal marketing at 5% plus input inflation will pressure EBITDA, though not to the 22% level.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 2% price increase cover raw material inflation, and will there be more price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: The January 2% increase was for product enhancements, not inflation. A Q1 FY27 price increase is planned to cover input costs, with the pass-through share still undecided. Management said it would absorb costs if volumes were at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Will price hikes hurt volume elasticity in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to price only to the extent volumes are unaffected and would rather absorb cost temporarily in margin than cut volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of market share in economic segment and the new product pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said product upgrades launched in Q3 and Q4 were well received. Groove 3 is being extended to about 500 EBOs, select MBOs and e-commerce, and the men's Bonded collection outdoor campaign launched around 20 May.

qa_highlights.question: Are digital-first brands taking share, and is distribution friction behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said e-commerce has grown for 3-4 years and Jockey ranks number one on major platforms in core categories. Auto replenishment has settled in for about 2.5 years, and a new distribution management system is being rolled out over the next year.

532827|2026-06.headline: Page Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 7.9% to INR14,204 mn and PAT fell about 4%, as ~3 days of billing slipped into Q2 on logistics disruption.
532827|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 7.9% YoY to INR14,204 mn and volume rose 5.7% to 61.9 mn pieces, but management said quarter-end logistics and manpower disruptions left about three days of billing undelivered. EBITDA fell 1.9% YoY to INR2,890 mn, with margin at 20.3% versus 22.4% a year earlier, as input costs (cotton, nylon, synthetics) spiked from March–May. PAT declined about 4% to INR1,928 mn. Management said most of the delayed billing and the May price increase (about 2.2% weighted average) should show up in Q2, and it reaffirmed double-digit annual volume growth and the 19–21% EBITDA margin range.

segments.name: Jockey innerwear and core range
segments.commentary: Volume growth of 5.7% was ahead of revenue growth of 7.9%-minus-mix, with lower-ASP accessories and socks gaining share due to scheme design. Schemes are now spread across quarters under the ARS model.

segments.name: Groove 3 (street fashion line)
segments.commentary: Launched in June 2026 across close to 500 exclusive brand stores; management said sell-through looks very good.

segments.name: Disney/Marvel character merchandise
segments.commentary: Go-to-market planned for end-June; a large portion of revenue expected in Q2.

segments.name: Speedo
segments.commentary: Multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1 from consolidation in swim offline; online is upwards of 35% of Speedo business. Combined Q4+Q1 view is about 950 stores.

guidance_outlook: Full-year volume growth target remains double-digit, phased across quarters; Q2–Q4 must show above-average volume growth to recover Q1 shortfall (analyst read-through of about 11–12% average).
Majority of the roughly three days of undelivered billing (seven days vs normal three to four) expected to be reported in Q2.
Full benefit of the mid-May price increase to flow through in Q2 under FIFO billing; difference between volume and value growth expected to widen from Q1 levels.
Annual EBITDA margin outlook retained at 19–21%.
Management intends to hold prices and drive volumes if margins stay within 19–21%; another price action possible if input costs re-escalate.
Marketing spend to remain at 4–5% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Management is augmenting in-house manufacturing capacity and investing above plan, alongside outsourced garment supply.
Odisha and K.R. Pet manufacturing facilities are scaling up progressively.
Distribution: 115,871 multi-brand outlets, 1,640 exclusive brand stores, 930 large format stores.
E-commerce: two fulfilment centres (one South, one North); management prefers outright model over marketplace.
Consumer data platform (CDP) expected to go live by end-August 2026, subject to DPDP Act compliance.
DMS rollout: all distributors targeted on DMS by end-2026 or Q1 FY28 at latest.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 5.7% was driven by healthy consumer demand across EBOs, e-commerce and wider retail.
Price increases: about 2.5% in January 2026 (product-quality related, not input-cost linked) and about 2.2% weighted average in mid-May 2026 (input-cost linked).
Input cost inflation in cotton, nylon, synthetic fabrics and packaging peaked in May; prices eased by late June but remain volatile.
Management said the May price increase only partially offsets the raw material escalation.
Pricing is uniform across channels with no flash sales or markdowns; quick commerce is on an outright model.
Secondary growth was better than primary in Q1 because of undelivered billing; tertiary and EBO performance was better than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume growth below the double-digit target flagged in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was affected by a planned scheme phasing change under ARS and about three days of undelivered billing; the full-year double-digit target is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will the price increase offset input costs and restore margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The May increase only partially covers input costs; the full benefit flows from Q2 and management said prices have eased below April–May levels, so it is a 'waiting game'.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days fall from 73 to 66?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not intend to reduce inventory further, that Q1 had some lost sales from non-availability, and that inventory is now at an optimum level.

qa_highlights.question: What were the logistics and manpower disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party logistics and labour concerns linked to fuel price rumours, fuel availability and a June SAR drive disrupted last-mile delivery to distributors at quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Speedo multi-brand outlets decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline swim consolidation as business moved online; Speedo multi-brand outlets fell to about 700 in Q1, and about 950 counting Q4 and Q1 combined.

qa_highlights.question: Why did A&P spend fall 5% in FY26 and is the company shifting to outright e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 included a disproportionate World Cup campaign; marketing will stay at 4–5% of revenue. E-commerce has tilted to outright because of quick commerce, and price governance is maintained through partnerships.

risks_watch: Recovery of about three days of undelivered billing and above-average Q2–Q4 volume growth needed for double-digit annual volume target.
Input cost volatility (cotton, nylon, petroleum-based synthetics) and possible re-escalation requiring another price action.

Karnataka minimum wage: garmenting wage hike applied from April; second announcement affecting third-party support staff was withheld in late July; impact on margins from a garment-level hike not quantified.
Logistics and third-party labour reliability at quarter end.
Speedo multi-brand outlet consolidation and channel shift online.
Shift of e-commerce towards outright model and its implications for pricing control.

532830|2026-09.headline: Astral Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% to INR 1,988 crore with EBITDA margin of 13.7%, while H1 plumbing volume grew 10.1%.
532830|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 1,988 crore, with EBITDA of INR 272 crore (13.7% margin). Plumbing delivered INR 1,398 crore (+25%) with 16.3% EBITDA margin, while adhesives India, adhesives UK and paints grew 25%, 30% and 44% respectively, but adhesives and paints margins were under pressure from high-cost inventory and lagged price pass-through. Management said October was the best month in company history and guided to a stronger H2 for plumbing, targeting roughly INR 1,050 crore plumbing EBITDA and about INR 1,250 crore group EBITDA for FY27.

guidance_outlook: Plumbing: double-digit volume growth guided; H2 expected to exceed H1 (10.1%). Full-year plumbing volume targeted at about 290,000-300,000 tonnes.
Plumbing EBITDA: full-year plumbing EBITDA of about INR 1,050 crore projected (H1 INR 426 crore, 40/60 split assumed as last year). Plumbing margin guidance of 16-18% reaffirmed; H1 was 17.4%.
Group EBITDA: about INR 1,250 crore projected for FY27, including about INR 200 crore plus from chemicals (DSS and others); FY28 EBITDA growth of about 15% indicated.
Adhesives India: full-year EBITDA guidance of 14-15%; management now expects about 13-14% run rate by year-end and full-year near 13%. Revenue growth guidance to be raised above prior 15-20%.
Adhesives UK: targets 9-10% EBITDA margin; year-end margins to return to normal levels.
Paints: guided positive EBITDA of about 3-4% by year-end and 8-10% next year; no new geographies until EBITDA reaches about 9-10% in existing states; growth run-rate target of 40-50%.

Capex: FY27 capex expected at about INR 400 crore including Nexelon CPVC plant (about INR 40 crore) and goodwill-related items; INR 260 crore spent in H1. Sale of Bengaluru asset from Gem Paints expected to bring about INR 50-52 crore.
capex_capacity: Plastic plumbing capacity stated at 425 KT (press release).
CPVC backward integration plant (Nexelon) construction nearly complete; trials expected in first month of Q4 FY27 and commercial readiness by last month of Q4.
PEX and aluminium PEX machinery installed and stabilised; commercial sales from own plant expected from Q3 FY27.
Management said land and buildings are in place to add about 100 KT in 6-9 months; 60-70% of capex cost is land and building, already in hand.
Kanpur plant opened recently; further capacity possible at Hyderabad and other plants. CPVC ramp-up expected to take up to one quarter.
demand_pricing: October was described as the best month in Astral's history across products, with unprecedented plumbing demand; management expects double-digit momentum in Q3 and Q4.
Industry Q1 was weak with low trade inventory, which drove the Q2 rebound; the industry priced up with a lag.
MIP (minimum import price) implemented; management sees a base price of about INR 85-90/kg protecting the downside, with countervailing duty under consideration.
CPVC price hike of 5% taken in October; PVC price increases since September fully passed through.
Adhesives India: H1 growth is mostly volume-led, with rural, online and overseas expansion; Q3 and Q4 top-line growth expected to match the Q1-Q2 run rate.
Sanitary ware is part of plumbing and estimated at around breakeven plus a small positive EBITDA.
Payable days fell as the company paid dollar liabilities early to avoid forex losses; inventory held on average 55-60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Growth outlook for plumbing in H2 and whether 12-13% is possible given the high base?
qa_highlights.answer: Kairav said October was unprecedented and expects double-digit momentum into Q3 and Q4; full-year volume target is 290,000-300,000 tonnes, with no specific growth figure given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 margins per kg fall versus Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a scheme-driven pipe-heavy mix in September, a PVC-heavy quarter, and lagged price pass-through by the industry were the reasons; CPVC and value-added mix are expected to be better in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Will adhesive India and UK guidance be upgraded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adhesive India growth guidance will be 'much higher' than the earlier 15%, with no exact figure; UK margin is expected to improve gradually to 9-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: why did inventory and payable days move?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days rose from inflation; Sept 30 figures are a point-in-time read, and average holding is 55-60 days. Payables fell due to early payment of dollar liabilities to avoid forex losses, which management says is a current-environment decision.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the paint margin improvement and what is the path to breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 40-50% growth run-rate, overhead absorption and lower manpower, warehousing and delivery costs; collections are now 60 days after legacy Gem Paints issues, and no bad debts are reported.

qa_highlights.question: Overhead cost trend and when it will decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-quarter overhead realisation was about INR 190 (per kg) and expects over INR 200 in the next quarter; OpEx rose 19-20% YoY in H1 against revenue growth of 26%.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude volatility: management attributes margin pressure to high-cost inventory and lagged pass-through; crude moves are the key swing factor.
Full-year plumbing EBITDA of about INR 1,050 crore depends on H2 contributing about 60%, which management says follows a historical pattern.
Adhesives margin gap: India at 11.5% H1 versus 14-15% guidance; UK at 5.6% H1 versus 9-10% target.
Paints remain EBITDA-negative in H1; management has not opened new states until margins reach 9-10%.
CPVC plant commissioning and ramp-up timeline (trials in Q4 FY27) and PEX launch in Q3.
Working capital: lower payable days and rising inventory days, which may reverse once currency stabilises.
Inconsistent reporting of paint growth (39.9% vs 43.9%) and of some figures on the call, which may need verification against the press release.
key_quotes: I think October we saw unprecedented demand and the sale has been very good.
Definitely there will be an upper side, much upper side, I can say, rather than what 15% we have given.

We assure you, and we are very much conscious about bringing this EBITDA margin back to the normal level in this quarter, and by the end of this fiscal year, again, to the margins of 13%, 14%, or up to 15%.
Now, whether we will deliver 10% or 11% or 12%, that still is to be seen.

532832|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 presales hit record INR2,632 crores (+89% QoQ), but FY26 reported PAT was a loss of INR872 crores on revenue-recognition timing and merger accounting.
532832|2026-03.overview: Embassy Developments posted record Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores and FY26 presales of INR4,631 crores (+128% YoY), with 93% of the INR5,000 crore guidance achieved. FY26 collections were INR1,673 crores, slightly below FY25's INR1,852 crores, which management attributed to the lag from H2-weighted presales. Reported FY26 revenue fell to INR1,732 crores and PAT swung to a loss of INR872 crores, which management framed as structural (completion-based revenue recognition and reverse-merger fair value step-up). FY27 guidance is INR6,000 crores own presales (plus INR2,000 crores from DM projects), INR3,000 crores collections and about INR19,400 crores of new launch GDV. Two legal overhangs (CIRP petition and KIADB resumption order) were resolved, and the ASM framework exit took effect 6 May 2026.

Net surplus margin expected close to 50% over the next several years; management declined to give an EBITDA margin range or revenue guidance.

Project progress: Paradiso 100% sold, 80% complete, OC FY27; East Avenue 94% sold, 73% complete, OC FY28; Verde 90% sold, 17% complete, OC FY29; Edge 74% sold, 66% complete, OC FY28; Park Panvel 74% sold, 41% complete, OC FY28-FY30; Greenshore 63% sold, 8% complete, OC FY31.

Launch timing: One North Tower (Bengaluru, INR1,400 crores GDV) in Q1 FY27 after building plan approval; Knowledge Park (INR4,500 crores) end of Q1 or spilling to Q2; Sky Terraces end Q1 or Q2; Juhu in Q2; Springs Front Parcel Q2 or Q3. Whitefield JDA (INR2,000 crores, 68.5% share) and Hebbal Plot A (INR2,100 crores, 91% share) are also in the FY27 pipeline.

Planned pipeline beyond FY27 of 20.4 million sq ft and GDV about INR23,500 crores, plus a 3,250-acre fully paid land bank. Nashik SEZ land is under a stay from MIDC, with next hearing on 12 June; debonding is targeted within FY27.
demand_pricing: Unsold inventory including Worli is about INR12,000 crores GDV, or about INR10,000 crores excluding the commercial asset. Management expects INR2,000 crores of FY27 presales from existing stock (Citadel about INR1,000 crores) and INR4,000 crores from new launches.
Presales over the last quarters: INR198 crores in Q1, INR409 crores in Q2, INR1,392 crores in Q3, INR2,632 crores in Q4. Over 80% of FY26 presales came in H2.
FY26 presales of INR4,058 crores equal 27.5% of unsold inventory value of INR14,728 crores (about 18% of launched and ongoing GDV, per a correction on the call).

Management says it is not yet seeing a market slowdown, and it expects to gain share in a consolidating market. It also expects costs to rise and to pass them on through pricing. Citadel is priced below top Worli developers, and management is not ruling out discounts.
Management said the stock was below fair value and that the promoter and Blackstone shareholder debt of about INR1,100-1,121 crores would be converted to equity later, once the share price recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timelines for the large projects (Knowledge Park, Whitefield, Springs, One North Tower)?
qa_highlights.answer: One North Tower is to launch in Q1 FY27. Knowledge Park is due at the end of Q1 or in Q2. Juhu is Q2, Sky Terraces end-Q1 or Q2, and Springs Front Parcel Q2 or Q3. Most launches fall in H1 or early H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Citadel's RERA completion date moved from 2032 to 2035?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a RERA buffer for a large tower, with the target at FY31-32. It also said this is in line with market norms for 300-metre towers.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt and leverage move given FY27 collections of about INR3,000 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction spend of about INR2,500 crores is planned, so debt will not fall much in FY27. Net debt to equity is to stay at or below 0.5x, with about 0.3x comfortable, and progressive reduction from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give an EBITDA range. It shifted to net surplus margin, which it expects to be close to 50% over several years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was about INR550 crores of interest expensed rather than capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said whatever could be capitalised was. The rest relates to OC-received projects and corporate expenses, and some borrowing funded premium approval charges for Blu.

qa_highlights.question: Interest and promoter pledge: is the pledge being reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pledge rose from about 47% to 68% when the share price fell, with no new debt taken. It expects a return to about 48% and full unpledging over 2 to 3 years.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Named launches are One North Tower (INR1,400 crores GDV, Q1 FY27), Knowledge Park (INR4,500 crores, end-Q1 or Q2), Sky Terraces (Q1 or Q2), Juhu (Q2) and Springs Front Parcel (Q2 or Q3), against FY27 new launch GDV of about INR19,400 crores; a 3,250-acre land bank and 20.4 million sq ft pipeline beyond FY27 back this up, though these are launches of projects rather than completed capacity and OCs

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 own presales guided at INR6,000 crores (about 30% YoY over FY26's INR4,631 crores, or 2.2x the Q4 FY26 run-rate of INR2,632 crores annualised) plus INR2,000 crores DM presales, with INR2,000 crores from existing stock and INR4,000 crores from new launches; risk is that over 80% of FY26 presales came in H2 and the Q1 launch cluster must deliver.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Construction spend in FY26 was INR1,182 crores (about 71% of collections), with FY27 construction spend planned at about INR2,500 crores and Citadel's total project spend of about INR3,000 crores leaving INR5,000-6,000 crores of surplus per management; no utilisation metric is disclosed, so a new capex announcement is not directly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 presales of INR2,632 crores (+89% QoQ) and 93% achievement of the INR5,000 crore FY26 guidance give momentum, but FY27 presales guidance of INR6,000 crores is only 30% above FY26 and collections of INR3,000 crores need 75% growth, so upgrade depends on Q1 launch delivery.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 presales need 2.2x the Q4 run-rate for the full year, the Q1 launch cluster (One North, Knowledge Park, Sky Terraces) must deliver, Nashik SEZ MIDC stay has a hearing on 12 June 2026, and management is not ruling out discounts on Citadel; no revenue guidance was given and FY26 revenue fell to INR1,732 crores from INR2,180 crores.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Named launches in the window are One North Tower (INR1,400 crores GDV, Q1 FY27), Knowledge Park (INR4,500 crores, end-Q1 or Q2), Sky Terraces (end-Q1 or Q2), Juhu ultra-luxury DM project (Q2) and Springs Front Parcel (Q2 or Q3), with 9 to 11 owned projects of INR13,300 crores to INR19,400 crores GDV in FY27.

rows.label: Net debt flat in FY27, reduction from FY28
rows.when: FY27 flat, progressive reduction from FY28
rows.why: Net debt about INR3,000 crores (0.3x net debt to equity) against FY27 collections of about INR3,000 crores and construction spend of about INR2,500 crores; management caps net debt to equity at 0.5x and targets cost of debt falling from about 14.8% to about 10% over 12-18 months.

rows.label: Promoter and Blackstone shareholder debt conversion to equity
rows.why: Shareholder debt of about INR1,100-1,121 crores is to be converted to equity once the share price recovers, which is a dilution overhang; pledge rose from about 47% to 68% and management expects a return to about 48% over 2-3 years.

rows.label: Nashik SEZ debonding and Citadel OC timing
rows.when: next hearing 12 June 2026; debonding within FY27
rows.why: Nashik SEZ land is under a MIDC stay with debonding targeted in FY27, and Citadel RERA completion has moved from 2032 to 2035 (target FY31-32), so the timeline of key project completions remains a risk.

532832|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 presales rose 338% YoY to INR868 crore and collections 54% to INR496 crore, but revenue fell to INR217 crore and net loss widened to INR234 crore.
532832|2026-06.overview: Presales of INR868 crore (up 338% YoY) and collections of INR496 crore (up 54% YoY) led the quarter, while no new projects were launched in Q1 by design. Reported revenue from operations fell to INR217 crore from INR681 crore, EBITDA was negative INR106 crore, and net loss widened to INR234 crore from INR166 crore, as revenue is recognised only on completion and handover. Operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore; management expects collections to pick up from Q2 as launches from H2 FY26 hit milestones. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR6,000 crore owned presales, INR2,000 crore DM presales and about INR3,000 crore collections, and a promoter warrant issue at INR111.51 to repay Embassy Group's INR363 crore shareholder debt.

segments.name: Residential (owned development)
segments.commentary: Presales INR868 crore in Q1; ongoing portfolio of 11 assets about 70% sold by saleable area; OC-received inventory about 98% cumulatively sold. Construction spend INR276 crore, about 56% of collections.

segments.name: Development management (DM)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza (Juhu) received RERA approval just before the call and is slated for Q2 launch; FY27 DM presales guidance INR2,000 crore.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Embassy East Business Park is under excavation and may be held as an annuity asset or sold near completion. Embassy Knowledge Park commercial product is in early planning, with timelines targeted by end-FY27; not included in GDV.

FY27 collections guidance of approximately INR3,000 crore reiterated; management says it could be bettered, with more clarity by Q3.

FY27 launch pipeline: 11 projects, GDV about INR19,400 crore (9 owned, INR13,300 crore; 2 DM, INR6,000-plus crore). Four to launch in Q2 (Embassy One North tower, Embassy Knowledge Park villas and apartments, Juhu DM project); the rest targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.
Management expects a cash-flow inflection around mid-calendar 2027 (April-May) as slab cycles start on Greenshore, Verde and Citadel.
Debt: cost of debt to fall first, with refinancing of the portfolio targeted around March-April 2027; net debt to equity target of 0.3x-0.35x.
Under review: percentage-of-completion accounting, to be assessed over the next couple of quarters.

Embassy Citadel (Mumbai, Worli) has approval for all 81 floors; Leighton appointed as civil contractor; est. INR8,000-9,000 crore of stock to sell over several years.

Cumulative unsold inventory across launched and under-construction residential and commercial projects: INR13,630 crore.
demand_pricing: Bangalore: about 72% of launch inventory sold within 6 months; management cites this as the cleanest read on demand, with Mumbai's 60% figure skewed by Citadel.

Collections-to-presales ratio was about 35% last year; FY27 target implies about 50% (INR3,000 crore vs INR6,000 crore owned presales).
Some Gurgaon landlords have asked about the Indiabulls association; management says the entities are separate and that this is a slow-to-resolve perception issue.

qa_highlights.question: Are Bangalore launch delays (as at Prestige) also affecting Embassy, and can the other 5 Bangalore projects launch within FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the Q1 non-launch to choice, not approvals; Embassy One North was pushed to Q2 after the Four Seasons branding was dropped. Knowledge Park villas and apartments are targeted for Q2, and Bangalore projects are targeted for Q3, possibly spilling into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operating cash flow outlook, given EBITDA of negative INR106 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 operating cash flow was negative INR285 crore because no launches occurred in Q1; collections from Q3-Q4 FY26 launches should accelerate from Q2. Cash balance started FY27 at about INR1,165 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR19,400 crore GDV split between H1 and H2?
qa_highlights.answer: The four Q2 launches (North tower, Knowledge Park, Juhu DM, plus Embassy One already launched) are in H1; the remaining projects are targeted for Q3, possibly Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the average cost of debt and the cost of the Blackstone debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Average cost of debt is about 14%. Blackstone debt accrues at 18%, added to the gross debt rather than paid out; management is in talks to convert the Blackstone portion to equity.

qa_highlights.question: Why the promoter warrant issue if the promoter debt is accruing rather than paid in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it brings no new liquidity; it is a confidence signal, priced at INR111.51 (the earlier pre-merger price), and the Embassy Group debt (growing at over 15%) will be cleared. Warrants will convert within 6 months, versus the 18-month maximum.

qa_highlights.question: Can collections of INR3,000 crore be achieved without new launches, and what is the collection schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Most collections are expected from already-launched projects (Greenshore, Verde, Eden). Launches in Q2 and Q3 are expected to yield 10-20% collected in the quarter; management is confident of the INR3,000 crore.

532832|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales hit a record Rs 3,225 crore, but revenue fell to Rs 292 crore and EBITDA was negative Rs 131 crore.
532832|2026-09.overview: Embassy Developments reported record Q2 FY27 pre-sales of about Rs 3,225 crore, lifting H1 pre-sales to Rs 4,093 crore, and collections rose 10% QoQ to about Rs 546 crore. Reported financials remained weak: revenue from operations was Rs 292 crore (vs Rs 494 crore a year ago), EBITDA was negative Rs 131 crore and loss after tax was Rs 271 crore, which management attributed to legacy projects and the project completion method. Three launches in the quarter carried a combined GDV of Rs 8,397 crore against a pre-launch estimate of Rs 7,500 crore. CEO Sachin Shah announced he will step down on December 31, 2026, with Aditya Virwani becoming MD and CEO from January 1, 2027.

segments.name: Bangalore
segments.commentary: Embassy Riverine (GDV Rs 3,155 crore) and South Reserve (GDV Rs 1,957 crore) at Embassy Origins; combined sales exceeded Rs 1,800 crore within two weeks, with Riverine at Rs 933 crore and South Reserve at Rs 880 crore. Management cited a 93% EOI-to-booking conversion over those two weeks.

segments.name: Mumbai (MMR)
segments.commentary: Embassy Terazza, Juhu (GDV about Rs 3,285 crore) sold Rs 758 crore shortly after launch, including a single Rs 711 crore residence. Embassy Citadel, Worli, crossed Rs 1,350 crore of sales in under nine months; approvals secured for all 81 floors.

segments.name: Projects nearing completion
segments.commentary: Golf City Savroli received OC for remaining towers in Q2 FY27; OC-received portfolio is over 95% sold by area. Embassy Paradiso is fully sold, with OC slated in FY27. Embassy Edge and East Avenue are about 90% sold, targeting FY28 completion.

segments.name: Park Panvel (legacy Indiabulls)
segments.commentary: 17 towers, about 8 million sq ft, with about Rs 500 crore invested so far and Rs 40 crore monthly burn. First two towers expected to get OC around June 2027. Sold receivables plus inventory about Rs 1,800 crore; management estimates a surplus of Rs 300-400 crore after construction and interest.

FY27 pre-sales target of Rs 8,000 crore: Rs 6,000 crore from owned projects and Rs 2,000 crore from DM projects.

Management expects positive operating cash flow by end-March 2027.
Debt expected to start declining around end-Q2 or Q3 FY28 (about this time next year), once collections exceed capex and overheads.
Revenue guidance for next year to be given in Q3 or Q4 FY27 once completion dates are firm; RERA dates have been replaced with completion dates, to be updated every six months.
Launch mix for Q3 and Q4 FY27 to be spread evenly, with Q4 likely to carry a larger share; some launches timed to avoid the mid-December to mid-January market slowdown.
capex_capacity: Owned portfolio: 13 projects with total GDV above Rs 27,422 crore, 55% of area sold (excluding DM projects).
Cumulative sold receivables plus unsold inventory of about Rs 25,536 crore: sold receivables Rs 8,290 crore and unsold inventory Rs 17,246 crore.

Development pipeline beyond FY27 of 20.3 million sq ft with estimated GDV of about Rs 23,470 crore; fully paid land bank of 3,251 acres, including 1,400 acres at Nashik under MIDC resolution and debonding.
Sky Terraces (DM project) targeted for launch in Q4 FY27, delayed by the pending GBA meeting; Sky Terraces sits under the Rs 2,000 crore DM target.
Embassy Citadel, Worli: approvals for all 81 floors; completion in FY33.
Panvel: about 2,000 laborers on site; OC for the first towers from around June 2027, with phased completion after that.
demand_pricing: Pricing: management says Panvel market rate is about Rs 15,000 per sq ft versus its current 12,000-13,000, and it is deliberately pacing sales at Embassy Origins to keep taking prices up.
Eight recent launches (Riverine, South Reserve, Terazza, Verde Phase 2, Greenshore, Eden, Paradiso, Citadel) are over 52% sold by area within six months of launch.
Launches are concentrated in Bangalore, MMR and NCR; Ketan Nanda hired as Business Head for North and Alok Sherry as Head of Business Development for Mumbai.
Management says buyers are mainly end-users in Bangalore; Worli sales were achieved without sample flats or a sales office on site.
Competition and market pricing were not discussed in detail beyond the Panvel and Mumbai commentary.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections reach Rs 3,000 crore in H2, and when will debt fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution is picking up and it is confident of hitting the Rs 3,000 crore collections guidance over the next two quarters. Debt is expected to decline around this time next year, once collections exceed capex and overheads.

qa_highlights.question: Break down the Rs 11,900 crore of launches planned for Q3 and Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Launches will be spread quite evenly, with Q4 likely to have a larger share. Some projects with RERA approval may be formally launched only after mid-January, as the market softens in December.

qa_highlights.question: What has been invested in the Indiabulls revival projects, and what is the Panvel timeline and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 500 crore has gone into Panvel, which consumes about Rs 40 crore a month. Panvel has 17 towers and about 8 million sq ft, with OC starting around June 2027. Realisation is about Rs 1,800 crore with upside, and surplus is estimated at Rs 300-400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kaimal said operating cash flow is expected to turn positive by end-March 2027, as slab-cycle collections from Q3 and Q4 FY26 launches come through.

qa_highlights.question: Why are losses increasing, and when will the balance sheet improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current P&L reflects legacy projects started before the merger. Reverse-merger goodwill is tested for impairment every six months. Cash surplus is about Rs 30,000 crore over the next 3-4 years. Net debt to equity should start improving from next year.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Blackstone Rs 700 crore debt be converted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is still in discussion with Blackstone but will not convert at current prices, calling it extremely dilutive given the stock trades well below book value.

qa_highlights.question: Can a delay in Sky Terraces hit the Rs 8,000 crore pre-sales target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not, citing Juhu over-performance (about Rs 800 crore already) and Rs 25,000-26,000 crore of stock available to sell.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nashik land monetisation status?
qa_highlights.answer: Early stage: the MIDC issues and land debonding must be resolved first. Data-centre use is being explored because a neighbouring 1,350 MW power plant could supply up to 950 MW.

532834|2026-03.headline: Camlin Q4 FY26 revenue about INR424 crores and EBITDA INR21 crores (5% margin), hit by a roughly 20% quarterly sales shortfall from shipping and war-related disruption.
532834|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was weak: management said sales were hit by about 20% from shipment delays, freight shortages and longer transit times linked to the Middle East conflict. Revenue was about INR424 crores in the quarter, with total revenue of INR1,723 crores after moving discontinued operations out. EBITDA was INR21 crores (5%), with vanillin sales largely from channel stock and Blends growth of 17%, short of the 20% target. Management said FY27 guidance is unchanged: revenue INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin 12-14%. The CFS Europe liquidation produced a gain of about INR100 crores and removes ongoing cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year.

Ethyl orders of about 300 tonnes are on hand for Q1, with a 600-tonne ethyl campaign planned. FY27 US volume is guided at 2,200-2,400 tonnes, and Europe at 1,500-1,600 tonnes.

segments.name: Diphenol (hydroquinone and catechol)
segments.commentary: Diphenol production was discontinued on 22 May. Phenol rose from about INR85 to above INR150/kg, and about 3,000 tonnes of catechol stock covers 8-9 months of vanillin output. Hydroquinone will be imported from China.

segments.name: CFS Europe and China
segments.commentary: CFS Europe was liquidated, and its cash burn of about INR50-60 crores a year ends from next quarter. China is still in liquidation, with costs expected at INR7-8 crores next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200-2,400 crores and EBITDA margin at 12-14%; management said guidance is not changing.
FY27 blended vanillin realisation expected at about $13.5-14/kg after tariffs, with US tariff at 15.5% (5.5% base plus 10%).
Q1 FY27 vanillin realisation expected to rise over Q4; gross margin guided to hold at about 48%, give or take 1%.
Q1 FY27 combined US and Europe vanillin sales expected to grow over Q4 FY26; Q1 EBITDA said to be hard to call, with the full diphenol-discontinuation impact in Q2.
Vinpai and Vitafor expected above EBITDA breakeven in FY27; Blends guided to upwards of INR1,400 crores.
Management said a stable 10-15% growth over the next two quarters would be great, citing elevated freight and feedstock costs.
Anticipated US tariff refund of about INR9-10 crores (about 50% cash, 50% duty adjustment, per management) on duties paid until February.
Repayment of about INR60-70 crores in FY27; equity raise described as a last resort, with structured or bank debt being pursued.
capex_capacity: A fire on Saturday (about 23 May) at the Dahej plant was contained, with no spread to the whole plant; insurance cover is adequate, but there will be some loss.
Diphenol plant shut on 22 May; management is evaluating repurposing it into a multipurpose facility to cut raw material costs.
Methyl-to-ethyl vanillin conversion took about 2 months, and ethyl vanillin production has started. Methyl production resumed in April.
FY27 vanillin volume at 70% utilisation implies about 4,000-4,200 tonnes, with the gap of about 1,000 tonnes to be sourced as catechol or guaiacol from China.
Management said the company has increased its authorised capital in March 2026.
demand_pricing: Vanillin: Syensqo is pricing DDP US at about $17-18/kg; Camlin's net realisation is about $13 after holding, tariff and financing costs. Management expects Syensqo to raise prices to $19-20 once its capacity reaches 100%.

Raw materials: phenol rose from about INR85 to above INR150/kg. Total raw material cost was about $7.5/kg before the war and is now about $9/kg; caustic has about doubled and freight to the Americas is about three times the pre-war cost.
Logistics: shipments that were expected in 20 days now take 40-50 days, and management expects it to take about a quarter for normalisation.
Management said demand for 4,000 tonnes of vanillin is achievable; the bigger constraints are working capital, logistics and cash flow.
Management did not expect the EBITDA impact of the conflict to be resolved quickly; it estimated sales were hit by about INR50 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vanillin volumes reach only about 320 tonnes in Q4 when about 650 tonnes was held in the channel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100 tonnes was sold in Q3 and the plan was to hold back a further 200 tonnes. About 300 tonnes of channel stock remains for Q1, so the total is about 600 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA shortfall was due to the Middle East crisis, and is guidance changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales were hit by about INR50 crores and Vinpai had about INR10 crores of EBITDA loss from liquidity issues, so EBITDA would have been about INR30 crores higher. FY27 guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended vanillin realisation for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be about $13.5-14/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt position and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt ended FY26 at about INR670 crores, including INR30 crores in escrow, with repayments of INR60-70 crores in FY27. Management prefers structured or bank debt, and equity is a last resort.

qa_highlights.question: Is the vanillin cost base higher now, and can the company reach INR300-330 crores of EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the vanillin cost is about $10.5/kg against $13.5 realisation, which implies about INR22-23 crores on 800 tonnes in Q1. Group EBITDA guidance is 12-14% on INR2,200-2,400 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US tariff refund cash or duty adjustment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is typically about 50% cash and 50% adjusted against duty, with about INR9-10 crores on a few months of India vanillin turnover.

532834|2026-06.headline: Camlin Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR5,199 million, but EBITDA margin collapsed to about 4% from 45% last quarter on raw material costs and vanillin under-utilisation.
532834|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR5,199 million, up about 28% YoY and about INR1,000 million QoQ, but margins fell sharply on raw material, freight and logistics costs tied to the West Asia conflict. The company reorganised reporting into Specialty Ingredients, Aroma and Performance Chemicals, with Aroma and Performance Chemicals both EBITDA-negative or near zero in the quarter. Ethyl vanillin ramp-up ran at low utilisation, and FY27 vanillin volume guidance was cut to about 3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons. Management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 10-12% while keeping revenue guidance, and debt was flat at about INR640 crore gross.

segments.name: Specialty Ingredients (blends and straights)
segments.commentary: Revenue above INR4,000 million with blends above INR3,000 million; EBITDA margin 6.35%. Management says about 4-5% of gross margin was lost to raw material costs and Brazil air-freight, with Brazil's shortfall of about INR8 crore expected to correct in Q2.

segments.name: Aroma (vanillin)
segments.commentary: Sold about 560 tons (350 t ethyl, 200 t methyl from channel stock) against 6,000-ton capacity; produced ~400 tons. Quarterly EBITDA negative at INR4-4.5 crore on fixed cost absorption; management expects positive EBITDA in Q2.

segments.name: Performance Chemicals
segments.commentary: Gross segment revenue about INR175 crore, of which ~INR130 crore is internal transfer, leaving ~INR40 crore external sales. EBITDA margin 2.5% with diphenol plant shut; management expects positive EBITDA from Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: INR2,200-2,300 crore, versus earlier INR2,000-2,400 crore; management says top line is secure.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 10-12% (10-11% per CFO/MD), implying about INR220-230 crore EBITDA, versus earlier INR250-280 crore.
Analyst read-back: average run rate of about INR70 crore EBITDA per quarter for remaining quarters; management did not dispute this.
Q3 FY27 expected to return to double-digit consolidated EBITDA margin; H2 margin of 13-15% floated by an analyst, not disputed.
FY28 EBITDA margin in the range of 12-14%.
Vanillin FY27 volume about 3,000 tons (earlier 3,600-4,000); 4 campaigns planned, Q2 volume 500-600 tons, Q3 1,000+ tons. Capacity 6,000 tons, achievable 5,000 tons with 3 campaigns.
Blends growth of at least 20% in FY27; budget assumes 25-30%.
capex_capacity: Vanillin capacity 6,000 tons per year; ethyl vanillin campaign of about 750 tons ran through mid-August, with about 350 tons sold and over 300 tons produced; methyl vanillin campaign to follow after roughly two weeks of changeover.
Diphenol plant shut because phenol and raw material prices are high; hydroquinone secured from China for the next two quarters; decision on alternate use or restart by Q3 FY27.
Working capital cycle about 100 days on a consolidated basis; each INR1 crore of revenue growth needs about one-third as working capital support.
CFS Europe in liquidation with no further cash burn beyond legal costs; China subsidiary liquidation expected to cost INR10-20 million in Q1.
demand_pricing: Channel stocks in the US and China described as cleared; management sees demand picking up and is negotiating quarterly, half-yearly and annual contracts with F&F customers.
US and Europe ethyl vanillin realisations stated at about $13-14/kg; methyl vanillin raw material cost $7-8/kg, with conversion cost about INR7 crore/month fixed.
Management sees a supply gap of about 5,000-6,000 tons in US and Europe that must be imported; Syensqo (Solvay) is the market leader; Chinese imports priced around $15 against Solvay's $18.
Pass-through of raw material increases to blends customers is lagging by one quarter; management expects to recover about half of the cost increase in Q2.
Trade financing (dealer finance) on purchase and sales sides costs an estimated 1-1.5% and is hitting gross margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 EBITDA guidance achievable given Q1 EBITDA of about INR9 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management restated guidance as INR2,200-2,300 crore revenue with 10-11% margin, which it said is within reach on the current cost structure; it expects about 10% margin over the next nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Aroma EBITDA negative and what is its normalised economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low utilisation (about 400 tons produced vs 1,500-ton quarterly capacity) left fixed cost unabsorbed. Management said 70-80% utilisation would make the business profitable and gave about 7% EBITDA at $13/kg on 3,000 tons.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt reduction and what external funding is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt is INR640 crore, down from INR670 crore on 31 March. The CFO said INR100-200 crore of working capital lines are expected within 1-1.5 months, and equity or other capital is being considered without a decision yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 vanillin volume cut from 3,600-4,000 tons to about 3,000?
qa_highlights.answer: The ethyl vanillin ramp-up was slower to secure quality, with 95% customer approval. Each campaign switch costs about a month, and four campaigns are planned this year.

qa_highlights.question: What would Q1 EBITDA have been under normal conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4-5% of gross margin was lost, which would have lifted EBITDA to roughly INR37-40 crore, an analyst's figure that management confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Will raw material cost pressure persist into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects elevated raw material prices to persist through Q2 and guidance assumes about three months of elevated costs, not six or nine months.

532834|2026-09.headline: Camlin Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin fell to about 2.5% as liquidity strain hit margins; board approved a ~INR250 crore rights issue.
532834|2026-09.overview: Management said the quarter was weak because liquidity constraints forced reliance on channel financing and stretched payables, which raised costs and cut gross margin from INR2,142 million to INR1,958 million. Aroma revenue fell from INR774 million to INR472 million after the switch from methyl vanillin to ethyl vanillin, and the diphenol plant has been closed since May 2026. The board approved a rights issue of about INR250 crore, backed by promoters, to fund working capital, with money expected by end-calendar 2026 or early 2027. Management guided Q3 only marginally better than Q2 and Q4 to over INR600 crore turnover and EBITDA of INR60 crore-plus.

qa_highlights.question: What would have been the incremental revenue and gross margin had the rights issue been done a quarter earlier?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales would have been about INR100 crore higher and EBITDA margin about INR60 crore better.

qa_highlights.question: Are promoters participating in the rights issue, and what dilution is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters will subscribe to their share (cited as 48%); pricing not yet decided, so total dilution depends on final pricing expected in the next few weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Why return to B2B distributor channel given credit cycles, and why is vanillin realisation only about $12-12.5?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distributors pay in about 30 days versus 90-120 days for large direct customers, saving working capital; muted realisation reflects rerouted Chinese supply and should improve over three to four quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 reach the INR200 crore EBITDA target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, that is correct, given the H1 run-rate; Q4 is the first quarter with liquidity, with turnaround expected.

qa_highlights.question: How do Aroma EBITDA margin of -23% and $2/kg EBITDA reconcile?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said $2/kg is at 70% utilisation before about INR20 crore of quarterly fixed costs; at current selling prices and Q2 volumes EBITDA per ton was zero, and the Aroma loss was about INR11 crore on 300 MT after fixed overheads.

qa_highlights.question: How much further capital is needed after the INR250 crore issue?

532835|2026-03.headline: ICRA Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 28.4% YoY, led by Research & Analytics (+56.8%) with Fintellix consolidated from October 2025.
532835|2026-03.overview: ICRA reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 28.4% YoY, with Research and Analytics up 56.8% on the Fintellix acquisition and Ratings up 10.6%. Q4 consolidated PBT before exceptional items and tax was INR 72.8 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 20.4% and PBT grew 10%, with exceptional charges from the new Labour Code excluded for comparability. Management flagged moderation in the Knowledge Services business and a margin-mix shift toward product-led businesses, and it sees near-term bond market softness offset by bank credit growth. Capital allocation questions (buyback, cash of over INR 700 crores, acquisition IRRs) were largely deflected, with the dividend raised and a special dividend declared.

segments.name: Ratings
segments.commentary: Revenue up 10.6% in Q4 and 14.2% for FY26. Management said the segment is a leverage play on economic activity, and Q4 growth was below some peers, which management attributed to a different base and strategic focus on growth segments.

segments.name: Research and Analytics
segments.commentary: Revenue up 56.8% in Q4 and 29.8% for FY26, driven by Fintellix (consolidated from October 2025, roughly 26% EBITDA margin per notes). Excluding Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly; Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily and turned profitable.

segments.name: Knowledge Services (KnowTech)
segments.commentary: Stable in core areas but growth moderated due to discontinued engagements and automation. Management expects a structural margin shift as non-KnowTech businesses, with different margin profiles, gain mix.

segments.name: Moody's-related non-ratings work
segments.commentary: Growth has been muted over the last couple of years and management expects moderation, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Some periodic in-sourcing by the parent continues.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or margin guidance given; management cited a BankTech product-led EBITDA range of 20% to 35%, depending on geography mix.
Management expects Fintellix to drive reasonable growth over the next 2 to 3 years, partly offsetting Knowledge Services moderation, without quantifying it.
ICRA projects India GDP growth moderating to 6.2% in real terms in FY27, assuming average crude of $95 per barrel.

Management expects bank credit to drive most ratings growth in the near term, with bond market activity subdued due to higher yields; no significant slowdown seen in the first couple of months of FY27.
Bank transition to the expected credit loss framework from 1 April 2027 is expected to sustain demand for risk modelling and compliance solutions.
Management expects roughly INR 180 to 200 crores of cash flow generation in FY27, per an analyst's figure that management did not dispute.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.

Ongoing investment in analytics platforms, compliance capabilities and AI-powered agents; AI layer being integrated into subsidiary analytical tools.
demand_pricing: Ratings demand is tied to bank credit and bond issuance; the first couple of months of FY27 showed no significant slowdown, but geopolitical headwinds persist.
Fintellix competitors cited: Regnology and Nasdaq Technologies (global, PE or public-backed, acquisition-driven), plus system integrators and some Indian CRAs with risk and regulatory solutions.
About USD 18 million of FY26 revenue is dollar-denominated (roughly one-third of about INR 600 crores revenue, per management's figure); dollar-denominated costs are not significant.
Fintellix shift from one-time licence plus smaller recurring fee toward annuity or subscription model is in progress, but not all clients are ready to adopt it.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Ratings growth materially lower than peers, and what is the non-ratings growth ex-Fintellix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICRA is in a similar band to peers, with double-digit growth over the last 4 years, and that growth-segment focus is the strategy. Ex-Fintellix, Knowledge Services grew modestly while Risk Management and Market Data grew healthily.

qa_highlights.question: Is a buyback under consideration given over INR 700 crores of cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to a rising dividend (normal dividend INR 60 to INR 70 per share plus special dividend) and said alternative capital allocation options are being evaluated, subject to Board approval and tax changes.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Ratings outlook for FY27, and what are April-May borrowing trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects bond activity to stay subdued given higher yields, with bank credit driving growth. No significant slowdown was seen in the first couple of months of FY27. No revenue growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: How will R&A margins evolve as the mix shifts, and could Ratings margins exceed 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no margin guidance. It said product-led BankTech-type businesses earn 20% to 35% EBITDA margins, and that double-digit Ratings revenue growth typically brings margin expansion as employee cost growth stays below 10%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Moody's-related work and in-sourcing from the parent?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been muted and is expected to moderate, with no higher double-digit growth expected. Periodic in-sourcing continues, with new project work arriving on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Fintellix segment profit and business description?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give Fintellix-specific contribution, citing parity of disclosure, but referred to notes to accounts showing around 26% EBITDA margin. Fintellix was described as RiskTech and RegTech, covering regulatory reporting and credit analytics for banks, insurers and asset managers.

risks_watch: Elevated energy prices from the West Asia conflict and a possible weak monsoon could weigh on FY27 growth and credit demand.
Knowledge Services growth moderation and automation trends could continue to pressure segment margins during the mix shift.
Limited disclosure of acquisition returns and Fintellix-specific financials, which shareholders have asked about.
Ratings margin gap versus other CRAs; management intends to close it through sales growth.

532835|2026-09.headline: ICRA's Risk & Analytics mix reached 50% of group revenue in FY26, with Ratings growing 15.2% in H1 FY27 while non-Ratings run-rate stayed near INR 80 crore a quarter.
532835|2026-09.overview: Management chose to focus on five strategic pillars rather than the quarter's numbers, which were covered in the investor presentation and press release. Ratings revenue reached INR 336 crore in FY26 (12.4% CAGR since FY21) with operating margin of 37.6%. Risk & Analytics (non-Ratings) revenue rose to INR 313 crore in FY26 from INR 114.9 crore five years earlier, but its quarterly run-rate has been flat at about INR 80 crore for the last few quarters, and margin is compressing as BankTech and CapTech gain mix. Management said D2K and Fintellix are still loss-making, that D2K became 100% owned only about 4-5 months ago, and that no profitability timeline will be guided.

segments.commentary: About 60% of R&A revenue; described as showing muted growth. Anchor client (Moody's) share of KnowTech is about 49%, down from 80% five years ago. Anchor-client margins described as stable.

segments.name: Risk & Analytics: BankTech and CapTech
segments.commentary: About 40% of R&A revenue, with lower margins than KnowTech. BankTech sales moderated in H1; bulk of recurring renewals fall in Q1, so H2 is expected to be better.

segments.name: Group (R&A) structure
segments.commentary: Now run as three divisions across legal entities: KnowTech, BankTech and CapTech. D2K and Fintellix integration described as operationally complete at end-September 2026. Legal-entity simplification is still pending.

guidance_outlook: No numerical guidance given on segment growth, acquisition revenue or profitability; management said it does not provide guidance.
Management expects bank credit growth (21.4% in H1 FY27) to remain buoyant in H2 FY27, while bond issuance grew about 3.7%.

capex_capacity: Technology and AI spend has been expanded significantly; management says ICRA is at a good place, with the platform roadmap now integrated across the three R&A divisions.
Plans for international expansion in Europe, the US and the Middle East, through organic and inorganic routes, with local presence to be built in targeted markets.

Non-Moody's R&A engagements range from INR 10-20 lakh tickets to multi-crore deals; most customers take only one of ICRA's roughly five products.

More than half of R&A revenue is domestic; international work has been served largely through partners or remote engagement. Competitors include global information-service providers, systems integrators, regional players and the Big Four.

qa_highlights.question: Why has non-Ratings profit mix fallen while revenue share rose to 50%, and what does this mean for acquisition IRR, especially Fintellix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin compression is expected as BankTech and CapTech (lower margin) grow, a conscious choice for a more balanced book, and is already in budget. It did not address IRR directly.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the non-Ratings quarterly run-rate stayed near INR 80 crore, and which parts are growing or declining?
qa_highlights.answer: KnowTech shows muted growth; BankTech sales moderated in H1 because renewals cluster in Q1 and H2 is usually better. Other verticals are growing reasonably well, with no guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: How much risk does a bond-yield spike pose to Ratings revenue, given ICRA's bond exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank credit growth (21.4% H1) offsets weak bond issuance (3.7%), that bank credit is expected to stay buoyant in H2, and that ICRA's revenue has been consistent over the last 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is ICRA raising surveillance fees, as a competitor reportedly did?
qa_highlights.answer: Agreements have an enabling clause for surveillance pricing; management is renegotiating with clients and has seen some traction in certain cases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Moody's relationship and headroom for growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is headroom and conversations are ongoing; the engagement is being reshaped with AI and automation, so higher engagement may not show directly in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: When will D2K and Fintellix become profitable and EPS-accretive, and what is the write-off or amortisation glide path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has a clear plan reviewed by the Board, but would not give a year. D2K was 60% owned until recently, which constrained investment; it became 100% owned about 4-5 months ago. R&A segment profit grew about 35% before D&A.
