532843|2026-03.headline: Fortis FY26 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR9,128 crores and EBITDA margin expanded to 22.8%; FY27 guidance is 15%+ hospital revenue growth.
532843|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue reached INR9,128 crores (+17.3%), with hospital revenue up 19.1% to INR7,773 crores and consolidated operating EBITDA up 31.3% to INR2,085 crores (22.8% margin vs 20.4%). Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR2,365 crores (+17.8%) and PAT rose 44.2% to INR271 crores. Management flagged softer Q4 occupancy at several large hospitals, attributed to a drop in international patients and a government price cap on oncology drugs affecting CGHS/ECHS business in Punjab. Net debt rose to INR2,334 crores (1.09x net debt/EBITDA) on acquisitions and investments.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR7,773 crores (+19.1%), operating EBITDA margin 22.2% vs 20.5%; ~85% of consolidated revenue and EBITDA. Q4 revenue INR2,023 crores (+19%), Q4 EBITDA margin 22.1%. Occupancy 68% vs 69%; ARPOB up 3.4% to INR2.51 crores.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: FY26 gross revenue INR1,527 crores (+8.5%), operating EBITDA INR360 crores (23.6% margin vs 17.7%; 23.2% ex one-offs). Q4 gross revenue INR387 crores (+11.1%), EBITDA INR85 crores, margin 22%; Q4 tests ~10 million (+5%). Preventive health 13% of mix vs 11%; B2C:B2B 52:48 for FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital revenue growth guided at 15%+ on an ongoing (organic) basis; acquisitions excluded and additive.
FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 150 bps; long-term target of 25% by FY28 reaffirmed, with management seeing 1.5%-2% annual improvement.
Diagnostics FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 23%-24%; revenue growth targeted at double digits (currently ~8.5%), with ~70% volume and ~30% value mix.
Jaipur expected to grow ~15% in FY27 with 13%-14% EBITDA margin.
Brownfield bed additions of 500+ in FY27 and ~1,800 beds over the next 4 years; capex about INR900 crores annually (about 60% maintenance).
Dividend of INR1 per share (10% of face value), fourth consecutive year, subject to shareholder approval.
IHH reportedly plans to raise stake to 50% and infuse ~INR10,000 crores fresh equity; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR700 crores; ~250 beds added via brownfield (Manesar, Noida, Faridabad) and ~800 beds added in total including acquisitions.

Acquired People Tree Hospital (125 beds, Bengaluru, Jan 2026) with land for 300+ beds; Shrimann Super Specialty Jalandhar (228 beds, Jul 2025) with land for 450+ beds; 200-bed Greater Noida lease (Sep 2025); Adayu 36-bed mental health facility in Gurugram (Nov 2025).
FMRI new tower to be operationalised within about a week, opening ~100 beds in FY27 on a phased basis; FY27 brownfield additions of 400+ beds per earlier statement, with 500+ per later remark.
Shalimar Bagh expansion delayed pending approvals; ~300 beds moved from FY28 to FY29; Mohali, Shalimar Bagh and Amritsar large towers ~2.5-3 years away.
BG Road has ~100 beds of brownfield capacity uncommissioned until occupancy improves; Mulund considering another tower.
demand_pricing: Hospital occupancy 68% in FY26 vs 69%; occupied beds up 15% (management cited 3,270 to 2,838, a figure order inverted in the transcript). FMRI at 85-95% occupancy; BG Road at ~55% vs ~63-64% area norm.
International patient revenue +18.5% to INR639 crores (7.8% of hospital revenue); Q4 international growth ~11%. Management is diversifying to Africa and other markets.
Oncology drug price capping (~30% of MRP) under CGHS/ECHS led Fortis to stop some high-cost drug cases, mainly in Punjab; no timeline for resolution. Management said margin impact is limited.
Focus specialties grew 18.9% and make up 62% of hospital revenue; radiation therapy volumes +19%, robotic surgeries +66%.
Diagnostics: 40.8 million tests in FY26 vs 39.2 million; 50+ new tests added; Illumina NovaSeq X operational at Mumbai reference lab.

qa_highlights.question: Why are occupancies falling at large hospitals such as FMRI and BG Road, and how will this improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal attributed the drop mainly to lower international business (Q4 growth ~11% vs 18-20% for the year) and oncology drug capping in Punjab. He said BG Road is low due to TPA/cash mix, intense competition and a 55% level versus a 63-64% area norm, with a target above 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand given new capacity and doctor cost pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashutosh Raghuvanshi said doctor costs rose slightly but further increases are not expected; the 25% FY28 margin target is intact, with 1.5-2% annual improvement now seen as more confident.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue did the 800 new beds contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Q4 hospital revenue of INR2,000 crores would be INR1,928 crores excluding People Tree, Adayu and Jalandhar, so new-unit contribution is small.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA of Gleneagles?

qa_highlights.question: Is Diagnostics demerger being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the focus is on profitability, this is not the time to lock value, and alternatives may be considered once the business matures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Gleneagles transaction moving forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is under deliberation and evaluation; no timeline, and it would need majority-of-minority approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Manesar run-rate and FMRI ARPOB driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Manesar FY26 revenue was INR140 crores at ~48% occupancy (new beds being added) and reached EBITDA breakeven. FMRI ARPOB rise was attributed to gross-basis international business, MR Linac, Gamma Knife and day-care oncology.

532843|2026-06.headline: Fortis Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.5% to INR 2,545 crore, but hospital EBITDA margin slipped to 21.5% from 22.1% on ESOP, ramp-up and legal costs.
532843|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 17.5% YoY to INR 2,545 crore, with hospital revenue up 19% to INR 2,187 crore and diagnostics gross revenue up 10.2% to INR 407 crore. Consolidated operating EBITDA pre-ESOP rose 15.8% to INR 568 crore, but margin eased to 22.3% from 22.6%, with hospitals at 21.5% versus 22.1%. Management said the margin dip reflects new ramp-up units, higher legal costs, higher doubtful-debt provisions and the new ESOP charge, and it maintained the FY28 target of about 25% margin, now framed as post-ESOP. Net debt rose to INR 2,233 crore (1.01x EBITDA) from INR 1,869 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Hospitals

segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 407 crore (+10.2%) and operating EBITDA INR 97 crore at 23.9% margin versus 23.0%. B2C:B2B mix improved to 53:47 from 51:49; preventive share rose to 14% from 12% and specialised to 35% from 34%. About 10.5 million tests processed and over 200 customer touch points added in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% margin target pre- or post-ESOP?

qa_highlights.question: Why are Manesar and Greater Noida margins below 10%, and when will they reach 20%?

qa_highlights.question: What are diagnostics margin and growth expectations for the rest of the year?

532843|2026-09.headline: Fortis Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.3% to INR 2,735 crore, with operating EBITDA pre-ESOP up 19.2% to INR 663 crore.
532843|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 2,735 crore in Q2 FY27, up 17.3% YoY, driven by the hospital business (up 18.6% to INR 2,340 crore). Operating EBITDA pre-ESOP was INR 663 crore at a 24.2% margin, up from 23.9%. Diagnostics (Agilus) grew more slowly at 12.2% on gross revenue, and management said it expects 12-13% growth for FY27. Management declined to guide FY28 margins, citing drug price capping on 137 oncology drugs, and guided FY27 post-ESOP margin to be flat at around 22%.

segments.name: Hospitals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,340 crore (+18.6%) and H1 INR 4,527 crore (+18.8%). Occupancy 72% (vs 71%), occupied beds 3,616 (+9%), ARPP INR 2.1 lakh (+6.8%). Renal, neuro and orthopaedics grew 27%, 28% and 30%.

segments.name: Diagnostics (Agilus)
segments.commentary: Gross revenue INR 448 crore (+12.2%); H1 INR 855 crore (+11.2%). Tests processed 11.39 million (+7.2%); patient volume +5.8% YoY. B2C:B2B mix 54:46; wellness revenue +28%, specialised testing +14%.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 190 crore (+12.4%), about 8% of Q2 revenue, flat share versus Q2 FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 hospital EBITDA margin expected to be flattish at around 22% post-ESOP, in line with FY26 (management confirmed post-ESOP basis).
No FY28 margin guidance given; management cited drug price capping circular (137 oncology drugs, effective November) as a negative for profitability, with impact not yet quantifiable.
FY29 25% margin guidance still stands if no drug-cap impact, per Vivek Goyal.

Digital revenue +18.6% to 29.5% of hospital revenue; 15 hospitals above 20% EBITDA margin, accounting for 84% of hospital revenue (vs 13 hospitals, 76%).

Gleneagles O&M (Hyderabad, Chennai) operations almost flat in the first year, with improvement expected next year.
Drug-price capping: oncology drugs about one-third of oncology revenue; impact not yet quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Punjab and Mumbai growing slower, and is Fortis lagging listed peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said Punjab is capacity-constrained, with about 500+ beds coming from Amritsar and Mohali expansions; other clusters are growing fast. He declined to compare with competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangalore occupancy low and why buy a small 110-bed hospital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small community hospitals complement larger flagships in a cluster. Bannerghatta Road is about 58% occupied, and TMI Yeshwanthpur is still ramping up. Suguna was bought via direct negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakdown of the 2,000 beds and the committed capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said the 2,000 beds are completed acquisitions and brownfield expansions, excluding Gleneagles and the 400-bed Delhi greenfield. Committed capex is about INR 3,500 crore over 3-3.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What returns hurdle does Fortis apply to acquisitions, and how is capital funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Board-approved benchmark is IRR of at least 15% and payback within 8-10 years, though strategic factors can override. IHH may take its stake above 50%, which could bring about INR 10,000 crore at current prices; management says capital is not a constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins and guidance be revised given drug-price capping?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Goyal said FY27 margin should be flattish at about 22% post-ESOP, with no FY28 guidance until the impact of the drug circular is clear. He reaffirmed that FY29 25% guidance holds if there is no impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for diagnostics growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Vijender Singh said FY27 growth is expected at 12-13%, with mid-teens growth in a few quarters, then industry growth. Brand transition impact is largely behind them.

Forensic audit ordered by court is ongoing; management expects completion within about six months of appointment.

Gleneagles O&M contract flat operationally in year one.

532851|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose about 7% to INR2,140 crores while PAT slipped to INR139 crores on a INR9 crore deferred tax charge; Q4 grew about 19%.
532851|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of resilience, with full-year revenue up about 7% to INR2,140 crores, gross profit up about 5% to INR675 crores, and EBITDA up about 3% to INR227 crores. PAT fell slightly from INR142 crores to INR139 crores, which management attributed to a roughly INR9 crore increase in deferred tax. Q4 revenue grew about 19%, with premium products up about 24%, but May was sluggish and the company is waiting for monsoon rains. Management guided to positive top-line and bottom-line growth in FY27, with the first quarter as the first visible test, while raw material inflation of nearly 10% or more supports pricing.

financial_highlights.change: down from INR142 crores; deferred tax up ~INR9 crores
supported by B2C and B2B; premium products ~24%
per CFO; management also cited FY growth above 7%

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: Contributed 73% of FY26 sales. Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C; management targets 60-70% in four years.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Contributed 22% of FY26 sales. Management says B2B held last year's level in April and expects growth in May and the rest of the year.

segments.name: Exports / International
segments.commentary: Contributed 5% of FY26 sales. Management targets 10% in 2-3 years, with CDMO and technical exports as drivers; CDMO work is at trial stage.

segments.name: Product categories (FY26 vs FY25)
segments.commentary: Patented products INR322 crores (vs ~INR330 crores); combination products INR324 crores (vs INR311 crores); in-licensed INR226 crores (vs INR229 crores); 5 products launched in FY26 INR40 crores; FY25 launches rose from INR23 crores to INR82 crores.

segments.name: Herbicides
segments.commentary: Contributed 39% of last year's sales. Price decline from off-patent competition hit last year; management expects quantities and a good increase this year as prices stabilise.

segments.name: Kaeros (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR110-111 crores; PAT above INR5 crores in its second year after acquisition for under INR6 crores. Management expects revenue to at least double in FY27 and contribute 5-8% of IIL volume.

guidance_outlook: Management expects both top line and bottom line to be positive in FY27, with results visible from Q1; management said the number is flat so far and depends on June monsoon.

Management believes the company is well placed to benefit from raw material inflation of up to about 10% or more, since its inventory of close to INR800 crores was bought before the price rise; management expects a small margin increase, with the size dependent on demand.
Management said EBITDA margins have already crossed double digits and it wishes to improve them further, without giving a number.
Working capital cycle target: management called a reduction from 140-150 days to 120 days achievable, with the timing dependent on the season.
Finance cost target: management internally targets a reduction of at least 25-30% in FY27.
Capex for FY27 is largely maintenance, in the range of INR25-30 crores after current projects are completed.
capex_capacity: Dahej: a new building (L&T) has begun manufacturing; management expects it to break even and be profitable by Diwali.
Technical plants at all sites have reached breakeven.
Sotanala: formulation start targeted around Diwali; whether it is billed depends on a CFO investment decision.
Sotanala technical plant: first of two buildings targeted for March-April 2027 for early kharif start; second building to follow based on market yield.
Management says Sotanala and Dahej provide sufficient capacity headroom for growth. About INR94 crores was invested in new products from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Industry: geopolitical tension has created supply constraints; raw material prices rose by nearly 10% and more for crude-linked products, shifting the market to a supplier-driven environment.
Two price increases were taken in April; the first was well received, but the second needed discounts in May. A June price increase is under consideration.
May was sluggish due to heat, and farmers are waiting for monsoon rains; El Nino and crop-mix changes in dry crops are key risks.
Herbicides are gaining traction as manual labour costs rise, but specialty herbicides from competitors are lowering prices.
Management says it sets no write-offs; unsold stock is taken back from the channel at season end and reformulated or moved between regions.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company benefit from its approximately INR800 crore inventory as raw material prices rise, given smaller competitors may lack stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed, saying the company plans from Diwali to Holi and bought stock before the price rise; the benefit depends on converting that stock into sales as the kharif season starts in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the breakup of volume and value growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volume grew 5% and value 14%; FY26 volume grew 5% and value 2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target for the working capital cycle and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle target is 120 days from 140-150 days, which management called achievable. Management internally targets a 25-30% cut in finance cost; the FY26 consolidated finance cost was INR16.87 crores against INR6.86 crores in FY25, driven by higher inventory, bank limit use and INR94 crores of new-product investment.

qa_highlights.question: How is Kaeros positioned against the Tractor/IIL brand and the partner products?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros will run a parallel distribution network with its own brand and a sales-only team. It is positioned as a follower to IIL, which gets first access to partnership products from Corteva, Nissan and OAT. Kaeros is not positioned as a cheaper brand; it will sell at a 2-3% initial discount.

qa_highlights.question: What is the share of premium products and can it reach 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are 60-63% of B2C. Management targets 60-70% in four years, so 70% will take three to four years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the R&D success rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said success rates vary: about 9,000-10,000 molecules screened a year, with a dozen trial teams testing 500-600 products to yield roughly 10-15 launches. Reverse engineering has higher success rates. The first Indian patent filing is pending IUPAC name approval.

Kaeros channel conflict risk, as Kaeros is distributed alongside IIL partner products; management says the policy of no common distributors avoids conflict.

532851|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12% YoY to INR612 crore as volume dropped about 13% on a delayed monsoon; gross margin rose to 31.6%.
532851|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined 12% YoY to INR612 crore from INR691 crore, with management attributing the drop to a delayed and uneven monsoon and high temperatures that pushed back crop protection demand. Gross profit fell 4% to INR193.16 crore, but gross margin widened from 29% to 31.6%, which management linked to premium mix and inventory effects amid volatile raw material prices. EBITDA margin fell from 12.2% to 11.1% and PAT margin from 8.4% to 7.2%. Management said the season was deferred rather than lost and expects stronger execution over the remaining three quarters, but declined to give revised FY27 targets until after H1.

from INR97 crore YoY (lower Hachiman sales)

Management expects to tighten power and steam costs through solar, wind and solid fuel, with benefits from end-Q2 onwards.
demand_pricing: Monsoon: delayed and uneven, with channel activity starting early in March. Management said August rains were good, but rice sowing lagged in South India (about 40% pending in Karnataka, Andhra and Tamil Nadu) and MP and some eastern states were dry.

Management said inventory was slightly elevated in June and is expected to decline sharply in Q2 quarter.
Management said gross margin bands by product type: generics about 10-15% (up to 20-25% in some cases), Maharatna about 30% (20-25% in some), FM 35%+ (up to 40%+).

qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about 2% price rise, specialty product mix, and some benefit from older inventory, while noting volatile input prices. It said the net effect was mixed.

532851|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 8% YoY to INR686 crore on value growth, with volumes down 6-7% and PAT at INR56.17 crore.
532851|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR686 crore, up 8% YoY from INR637 crore, driven by premium mix and price rather than volume. Management said volumes fell about 6-7% due to weak rains and El Nino, with value growth of 4-5%. Gross margin was 33.7% (vs 34.5%), EBITDA INR92.44 crore (13.5% margin) and PAT INR56.17 crore. H1 revenue declined about 2% YoY, with H1 EBITDA at INR161 crore (12.3% margin) and PAT near INR100 crore. Working capital days rose to 158 from 151, and management guided to a volume decline for the full year with H2 improvement in value.

segments.commentary: Premium Maharatna and Focused Maharatna products are now above 60% of B2C mix, with a target of 70%. Gold products fell as farmers shifted to new-generation products; management said they are not pushed.

segments.commentary: Exports are about 5% of revenue, mainly white-label formulations in more than 25 countries. Technical exports are starting, with more than 10 technicals registered and about 15 AIs in work. Long-term target is INR500 crore by five years out.

segments.commentary: B2B sales are above INR400 crore. Domestic portfolio has 28 technicals.

Gross margin expected to hold around 33% this year; management aims to match best-in-industry over time, with a typical gain of about 1% a year.
Q3 and Q4 returns expected to be normal; H1 PAT loss not expected to be fully recovered, but H2 expected positive.
Dahej project to be fully capitalised by December 2026 (Q3). Sotanala formulation start targeted April 2027, possibly May; technical manufacturing and full formulation unit next fiscal.

Four R&D centres, including Chopanki and Dahej (both NABL), plus a discovery centre in a JV with a Japanese company (Japanese partner funds 80%).
demand_pricing: Volume fell about 6-7% in Q2, with value up 4-5%, as the company sold more premium products; weak rains hit herbicides and granules.
Inflation is visible in agri commodity prices; farmers are moving to premium products and fewer sprays, and farmer profitability is largely intact despite low yields.
Field activity in H1: more than 18,000 farmer meetings, more than 9,000 demonstrations and more than 2.5 lakh farmers met. Around 70 ICS crop-solution plots this year, up from about 30.
Third-party field team ranges from 750 to 1,300-1,400 by season; H2 expected near 750. Kaeros adds about 150 people (70-80 on roll).
Crude oil spiked to about $125 and freight costs rose, pressuring the business; management said the impact is still to be seen in the festive season.
Channel returns were high but lower than last year. Most returns were taken in Q2; Q3 expected to be normal. Secondary visibility is partial (DMS and QR coverage of 15-20%).

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth by B2B, B2C and export, and how did Maharatna products perform?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume was negative, down about 6-7%; value grew 4-5%. Gold products fell while Focused Maharatna and Maharatna grew, with Maharatna showing a decent rise in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will volumes decline for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said this is not a volume-growth year, but value growth is expected, with H2 improvements from a mix of premium products and price pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kaeros outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Kaeros brand turnover is about INR75 crore in H1. The target is above INR125 crore this year, with standalone Kaeros around INR200 crore and a planned doubling next year. The national network is to be complete in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the OAT Agrio launch and the 9(3) registrations?
qa_highlights.answer: No immediate launch this calendar year. The schedule inclusion application is pending CIB inquiry, so the launch could slip a few months. Nissan's new product is due in kharif, followed by 9(3) mixtures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export strategy and cost competitiveness versus China?
qa_highlights.answer: Shifting from white-label brand exports to technicals, with more than 10 registrations and about 15 AIs in work. CDMO deals are early-stage, mostly with Japanese players. Exports are about 5% of revenue, with a target of INR500 crore in five years.

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D is spent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the R&D expense shown is about INR12 crore, with some trial costs booked under marketing. More than 100 registrations are involved, with about 200 people across IIL and the OIL JV.

532853|2026-03.headline: Asahi Songwon Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 30.2% YoY to Rs 23 crore, with margin at 15.6% on price pass-through in Blue pigments.
532853|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 144 crore, up 19.4% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 23 crore (15.6% margin vs 8.58% in Q3 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25) and PAT of Rs 10.82 crore. For FY26, revenue fell 4.78% to Rs 535.48 crore while PAT rose 5.48% to Rs 17.78 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to raw-material price pass-through and operational efficiencies in Blue pigments, with a small inventory gain, and said the API price decline of the prior three years has reversed. Gokul Jaykrishna handed day-to-day CEO duties to his son Arjun Jaykrishna, while remaining Managing Director.

segments.name: Blue pigment (standalone, ATC Dahej)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability improved QoQ on stronger realisation with modest volume growth. Gross margin rose to about 34% from about 29% QoQ; management cited price pass-through, operating efficiencies and a marginal inventory gain. Management said utilisation is about 80-85% and no capex is planned for capacity.

segments.name: AZO pigments (subsidiary ATC)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive and cash break-even reached. FY26 revenue Rs 78 crore with PBT loss of Rs 2.42 crore; management expects PBT break-even in FY27. Capacity is 2,400 tpa, utilisation about 65% per management, with a planned Rs 10-15 crore brownfield expansion to about 1.5x once utilisation reaches 75-85%.

segments.name: API (subsidiary Atlas, Chattral plant)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive. Volumes grew about 18% CAGR over three years, but realisations fell 40-45% since acquisition; Pregabalin prices are about 15% above the bottom. Pregabalin is 60-70% of API business. Chattral intermediates run at about 60-70% and finished APIs at about 30%. Q4 API revenue was reported as about Rs 30 crore with EBIT of about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA across all three segments to at least maintain Q4 FY26 margins, with an aim to improve.

Blue standalone: management said peak EBITDA of about Rs 50-55 crore is the goal for FY27 if prices hold, on about Rs 400 crore revenue at 13-14% margin (analyst's framing, accepted as a goal, not a formal guide).

Long-term margin targets: about 13% EBITDA for AZO and 15-16% for API; Mitesh Patel said Chattral and Atlas could reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex, at 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.
CEP certification for Pregabalin expected by end of FY27 (current financial year), seen as a driver of volume and export access.
Management aims for Rs 1,000 crore group revenue within the next few years, with priority on sustaining revenue first.
capex_capacity: AZO capacity 2,400 tpa; brownfield expansion of about Rs 10-15 crore (plant and machinery only) to lift capacity to about 1.5x, triggered at 75-85% utilisation, expected within 3-4 quarters and funded by internal accruals.
Blue: no capex planned for capacity; incremental gains expected from debottlenecking and efficiency projects.
Chattral: intermediates about 60-70% utilised; finished API utilisation about 30%, which management sees as the key lever for fixed-asset turnover.
Peak debt was Rs 220 crore after the completed four-year capex cycle; debt is falling faster than internal estimates.
demand_pricing: Blue pricing is set quarterly with MNC customers; Q4 benefit was partly locked in, so further benefit expected in Q1 and Q2. Mitesh Patel put the price increase at about 20%, and management said prices across pigments and crude rose meaningfully on raw-material tightness.
Management said China raised prices about 30-40% due to lower export incentives and VAT rebates, roughly doubled ocean freight and higher crude-linked raw material costs.

US tariffs hit AZO and Blue exports, including via India-made value-added products; US business has revived since tariffs eased but has not returned to normal. AZO export customers have restarted testing.
Management said Europe remains in a structural slowdown; India remains the main AZO growth market.
Management says the cyclical slowdown appears to be bottoming, and no new pigment capacity is expected in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA gain came from raw-material price pass-through, and does it reverse if raw material prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jaykrishna said the strategy was to pass through as much raw-material inflation as possible via long-term supplier and customer relationships. He did not quantify the split and said revenue was under pressure while the bottom line held.

qa_highlights.question: Blue gross margin rose from about 29% to 34% QoQ. Is there inventory gain, and how do margins return to 35-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said margins reflect internal strategy, some inventory addition, and operating efficiencies. Gokul Jaykrishna later put the inventory gain as marginal, since the company held finished goods bought before the war.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Blue power and fuel cost fall to under 5% of sales in Q4 because of a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said a one-time receipt of renewable-energy billing rebate, pending for two years, drove the drop. Management expects power and fuel as a percentage of sales to be lower than before but not at Q4 levels every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is AZO FY26 revenue and PBT, and will it break even in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Nupur (company) said FY26 AZO revenue was Rs 78 crore and PBT was Rs (-2.42) crore. Management said it expects PBT break-even in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone Blue utilisation and possible FY27 EBITDA of Rs 50-55 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Gokul Jaykrishna corrected the analyst's 60% figure, saying Blue runs at about 80-85%. He called Rs 50-55 crore peak potential and the goal for FY27. Mitesh Patel put Blue price increases at about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiaries: peak revenue and EBITDA potential at Atlas and Chattral?
qa_highlights.answer: Mitesh Patel said the two facilities can reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex and 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years. Arjun said API EBITDA depends on pricing, and management said the subsidiaries could reach about Rs 50 crore EBITDA at peak.

risks_watch: Q4 margin gains were partly one-off: a renewable-energy rebate lowered Blue power and fuel costs, and an inventory gain contributed. Q1 FY27 is the test.
Pricing is volatile: management says there is no stability in prices or the business environment; a reversal of raw-material inflation could compress margins.
API utilisation at Chattral finished products is about 30%, and the company has not yet hired senior business development or marketing leadership; a senior hire is expected in the next quarter.
FY26 consolidated revenue fell 4.78% and EBITDA 6.12%; FY26 net margin about 3.3%. AZO and API are still loss-making or marginal, so consolidation depends on Blue.

rows.why: Pune RMC plant (60 cum/hour) started in Sep 2026 and Hoskote and Kalyan followed; wind indigenous plant is expected operational in 12-14 months, and the ash target of 90,000 t in Q4 FY27 is up from 35,000-40,000 t in Q2.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ash & coal guided at 20-25% YoY growth for FY27 and FY28 (midpoint 22.5%) against a ~INR1,700 crore order book; wind FY27 execution of INR1,300-1,400 crore is backed by an INR1,100-1,200 crore order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says RMC rollout is asset-light with no capex, and the wind plant is already under setup, so no new capex programme was signalled; utilisation was not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Ash growth held at 20-25%, EBITDA margin held at 15-18%, and wind execution guided at INR1,300-1,400 crore against an order book of INR1,100-1,200 crore, with Q2 volumes weak on monsoon, so no basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 ash volume of 35,000-40,000 t is far below the 90,000 t Q4 target and H2 growth was not quantified, while the brief's guidance table flags the FY27 wind execution figure as a cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: RMC rollout planned across Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Chennai after Pune, Hoskote and Kalyan, with Pune expected at 4,000-4,500 cum/month; RMC contribution expected meaningfully from FY28.

rows.label: Large-volume wind order closure
rows.why: Final price negotiation expected to close in 30-45 days with quantum described as substantial; existing wind order book about INR1,100 crore.

rows.label: Green mobility demerger
rows.why: Completion guided in 2-3 months subject to NCLT and regulatory approvals; NCLT adjourned to 11 November 2026.

rows.label: Receivables cycle to about 130 days
rows.why: Receivables INR1,251 crore on a 120-130 day cycle; management targets holding about 130 days, with billing delays of up to 70 days, and promoter pledge release of INR400-450 crore expected in 3-5 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on the ash business, wind order closure and RMC outlook but cautious on the weak Q2 volumes from monsoon; analysts pressed on receivables of INR1,251 crore, finance cost rise, promoter pledge and the unquantified H2 growth.

532885|2026-03.headline: Central Bank of India Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR724 crore on a one-time INR632 crore DTA charge; FY26 net profit rose 15.43% to INR4,369 crore.
532885|2026-03.overview: FY26 business grew 15.60% to INR812,439 crore, with gross advances up 18.76% to INR344,516 crore and deposits up 13.38% to INR467,923 crore. Q4 net profit fell to INR724 crore from INR1,034 crore a year earlier, mainly due to a one-time INR632 crore hit from recognising deferred tax assets at 25% instead of 35%. Q4 operating profit rose 4.64% YoY to INR2,096 crore, but fell QoQ as treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore) and recoveries from written-off accounts (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore) dropped. Asset quality improved on a full-year basis: gross NPA 2.67% (down 51 bps YoY), net NPA 0.49%, slippage ratio 1.16% vs 1.45%.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1,034 crore Q4 FY25 (after INR632 crore one-time DTA charge)
marginal decline; Q4 about 2.9% excluding INR431 crore tax refund interest
GNPA -51 bps YoY; NNPA +6 bps per call (analyst noted rise)
includes 2% quarterly interim dividends for three quarters

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances INR103,533 crore, up 25.67% YoY; management called retail, agriculture and MSME (RAM) the main growth engine.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances INR61,687 crore, up 17.60% YoY.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances INR69,351 crore, up 17.06% YoY; Q4 slippages partly linked to MSME branch audits and MUDRA/PMEGP accounts up to INR10 lakh.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book INR109,945 crore, up 14.50% YoY; bank is selective, targeting good-rated borrowers only. RAM/corporate split is 58:32 per call, with a 65:35 +/-5 target.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book around INR28,000 crore, growth 8.6%; LTV and yield not disclosed on the call.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: business growth 14% to 15%, deposit growth 10% to 12%, advances growth 14% to 16%.
FY27 slippage ratio guided below 1%.
NIM to be maintained above 3%, supported by deposit repricing expected to complete next quarter.

ECL migration effective 1 April 2027; INR1,525 crore already provided. Management says it can absorb full day-one impact through reserves at 17.91% CRAR. Ongoing ECL-related provisions estimated at INR600 crore to INR650 crore a year, offset by roughly INR600 crore to INR800 crore of tax-rate benefit (25% vs 35%).
FY27 capex budget INR1,442 crore and revenue budget INR1,276 crore for digital spend.
Expects to recover INR2,200 crore to INR2,500 crore from technically written-off accounts in FY27 (INR2,270 crore recovered in FY26 from over INR32,000 crore pool). Dividend to be maintained.
capex_capacity: FY27 capital budget for digital spend INR1,442 crore; revenue budget INR1,276 crore.
Sales and marketing team being set up, 50% through IBPS recruitment, expected within 1 to 2 months.
Around 900 officers from training to be deployed in October; 1,000 credit officers being trained.
Outreach programme held in more than 100 locations since November; 225 MSME and more than 300 agriculture branches identified for focus.
Wealth management division, credit card business and centralised forex set up or being established.
demand_pricing: Yield on advances 7.78% in Q4 vs 8.21% a year earlier (down 57 bps); cost of deposits 4.82% (down 2 bps). About 61% of advances are external-benchmark linked, so repricing hit yields faster than deposits.
CD ratio 73.80% in March 2026 (66% in September 2025), roughly 74%; LCR 210% in FY26.
Term deposit growth above 14% to 15%; saving bank deposits crossed INR2 lakh crore for the first time, growing 10.05%.
Government business cell MoUs with state governments, railways and police/paramilitary forces are driving salary accounts.
No stress signals from the Middle East situation so far; no requests for overdue PCs or post-shipment facilities. Daily slippage of about INR250 crore recorded around 20 April.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating profit and net profit fall QoQ, and is there stress from geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lower treasury income (INR9 crore vs more than INR300 crore in Q3) and lower written-off recoveries (INR352 crore vs INR1,062 crore). Net profit was hit by the INR632 crore DTA charge. No stress signals have appeared so far from the Middle East situation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fresh slippages rise QoQ to INR1,301 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mukul Dandige attributed part of the rise to MSME accounts flagged in branch audits where credit submissions did not match business projections, and to some agriculture accounts. Government-scheme (MUDRA, PMEGP) accounts up to INR10 lakh also slipped; the normal run-rate is about INR800 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL impact on the one-time charge and recurring credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management's back-of-envelope estimate of the ECL impact is around INR4,000 crore, of which INR1,525 crore is already provided. Ongoing ECL-related provisions are estimated at INR600 crore to INR650 crore a year, offset by a tax benefit of roughly INR600 crore to INR800 crore. The full simulation is not complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM rise about 30 bps QoQ when yields and funding costs were flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Dandige said a INR431 crore income-tax interest refund booked in Q4 added to NIM. Excluding it, NIM was about 2.89% to 2.9% in Q4 vs 2.96% in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What are standard asset provisions and gold loan details?
qa_highlights.answer: Standard asset provisions are about 0.7% to 0.8% of standard assets, around INR2,800 crore to INR2,900 crore in total, including the INR1,525 crore ECL provision and RBI restructuring provisions. Gold loans are about INR28,000 crore, growing 8.6%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for NIM and recovery from written-off accounts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM will stay above 3% in FY27 given CASA strength and RAM mix. It expects INR2,200 crore to INR2,500 crore of recoveries from written-off accounts in FY27.

risks_watch: Q4 one-time DTA charge of INR632 crore; the tax refund (INR431 crore) inflated Q4 NIM and profit, so underlying quarterly profit is lower than reported.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027: the simulation is not finished and no final impact number has been given.
Q4 slippage rose to INR1,301 crore vs about INR800 crore average; FY27 slippage target is below 1%.
Yield pressure from external-benchmark-linked loans (about 61%) versus slower deposit repricing; NIM guidance of above 3% depends on repricing finishing next quarter.
Treasury income dropped to INR9 crore in Q4; the lumpy airline account recovery process is ongoing (INR515 crore guarantee received previously).
532885|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, capital and asset quality, but evasive on specifics: ECL impact, the pipeline, and offline-only items (technology, sanctions) were deferred. Management framed the Q4 profit fall as largely one-time and downplayed the slippage increase.
key_quotes: And here, I want to mention as per the New Finance Bill, bank has taken a onetime impact of INR632 crores due to recognition of deferred tax asset at the rate of 25% as against 35%.
So bank being sufficiently capitalized at 17.91%, I can easily take the impact on day 1.
We have given direction that we are going to remain above 3%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided above 3% for FY27 with deposit repricing expected to complete next quarter, but Q4 NIM ex the INR431 crore tax refund was about 2.9% vs 2.96% in Q3, and 61% of advances are external-benchmark linked with yield down 57 bps YoY to 7.78%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guided FY27 advances growth of 14% to 16% and business growth of 14% to 15% after FY26 advances grew 18.76% to INR344,516 crore, with retail up 25.67% and MSME up 17.06%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation and capacity are not discussed; the only capex is an FY27 digital budget of INR1,442 crore capital and INR1,276 crore revenue, which is not new physical capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance was newly set at 14-15% business growth and above 3% NIM, with no sign of running ahead; Q4 net profit fell to INR724 crore from INR1,034 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 slippage rose to INR1,301 crore vs about INR800 crore run-rate against an FY27 target below 1%, the ECL simulation is unfinished (estimated about INR4,000 crore total impact), and NIM above 3% depends on deposit repricing finishing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Wealth management division, credit card business and centralised forex are set up or being established, and a sales and marketing team (50% via IBPS recruitment) is expected within 1 to 2 months.

rows.label: Recoveries from written-off accounts of INR2,200-2,500 crore in FY27
rows.why: FY26 recoveries were INR2,270 crore from a pool of over INR32,000 crore, and management guides INR2,200-2,500 crore for FY27, though Q4 recoveries fell to INR352 crore from INR1,062 crore in Q3.

rows.label: ECL migration effective 1 April 2027
rows.why: INR1,525 crore already provided against an estimated about INR4,000 crore total impact, with ongoing ECL provisions of INR600-650 crore a year offset by a tax benefit of INR600-800 crore; management says it can absorb day-one impact through reserves at 17.91% CRAR.

rows.label: Tax refund and treasury income normalisation
rows.why: The INR431 crore tax refund interest inflated Q4 NIM and profit, and treasury income fell to INR9 crore from more than INR300 crore in Q3, so underlying quarterly earnings are below the reported figure.

tone.note: Management was confident on RAM-led growth, capital (CRAR 17.91%) and FY27 NIM above 3%, but deferred specifics on ECL impact, the pipeline and tech/sanctions; analysts pushed on the QoQ profit fall, the slippage jump to INR1,301 crore and the NIM uplift from the INR431 crore tax refund.

532885|2026-06.headline: Central Bank of India Q1 FY27 net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, with advances up 28.58% YoY and gross NPA at 2.60%.
532885|2026-06.overview: Central Bank of India reported Q1 FY27 global business of ₹833,320 crore (up 18.29% YoY), with deposits up 11.68% to ₹478,972 crore and gross advances up 28.58% to ₹354,348 crore. Net profit rose 13.26% to ₹1,324 crore, NIM was 3.06%, and ROE improved to 14.92% from 14.17%. Asset quality improved, with gross NPA at 2.60% (down 53 bps YoY), net NPA at 0.49%, and slippage ratio at 0.29%. Management said the quarter's advances growth was driven partly by a low base in corporate loans, and quarter-on-quarter advances growth was only about 2.85%. Liquidity coverage ratio fell sharply from 235% to 156%, as the bank deployed liquidity into loans.

financial_highlights.value: ₹276 crore (per Q&A); ₹621 crore vs ₹353 crore in segment comments

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 23.92% to ₹1,05,523 crore. Segment profit was reported at ₹1,377 crore vs ₹633 crore a year earlier in an analyst's reading of segment data.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 21.14% to ₹64,274 crore. Gold loan book is ₹36,000 crore; gold loans under agriculture are MCLR-linked, retail gold loans are not.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.03% to ₹71,308 crore.

segments.name: Corporate credit
segments.commentary: Corporate credit rose 46.52% to ₹1,12,770 crore from ₹76,966 crore, on a low base. Growth is concentrated in renewable energy, data centres, HAM projects and CRE. RAM-to-corporate mix is 68:32 against a 65:35 guidance (±5%).

segments.name: Wholesale and unallocated
segments.commentary: An analyst cited wholesale segment at minus ₹139 crore (vs ₹284 crore) and unallocated at minus ₹75 crore (vs ₹322 crore). Management said provisioning had not risen and did not clearly explain the change.

segments.name: Insurance associates
segments.commentary: Bank holds about 26% in Generali Central Life and Generali Central Non-Life, with ₹627 crore invested in total. Management expects higher income from both this year after the establishment phase.

guidance_outlook: Deposit growth guidance of 11% to 12% and advances growth guidance of 14% to 16% for FY27, which management said it will align with in the current quarter.
Quarter-on-quarter advances growth of about 3% expected to continue.
NIM guided at 3% and above; ROA guided at 1% and above.
Cost-to-income ratio to fall by 1.5% to 1.6% in the coming year, against a target below 56%.
Yield on advances expected to rise from 7.89% to about 8% by March 2027, led by gold loan and SHG yields of 8%+.

ECL transition planned from 1 April 2027; management estimated about 80 bps CRAR impact if provisioning is spread over five years or taken at once. Total ECL requirement estimated at ₹4,500-5,000 crore, with ₹1,525 crore already provided for Stage 1 and 2.
Technical write-off recoveries targeted at ₹2,200-2,500 crore for FY27; 600-700 property sales targeted against 460 last year.
FCNR(B) mobilisation target of USD400 million by September 2026 (USD8.4 million mobilised so far).
GIFT City targets: deposits of USD200 million and trade book of USD500 million over the next few years.
capex_capacity: Network of 4,605 branches (65% rural and semi-urban), 3,820 ATMs, 13,890 BC outlets, 30 BC MaXX centres and 1 IFSC Banking Unit; 22,346 total touch points.
New branch opened at GIFT City, Gandhinagar on 29 June 2026.
Plans to open more corporate finance and mid-corporate branches.
Around 1,000 credit officers in specialised training to join in the first week of October 2026 for deployment at credit centres.
300 marketing officers hired and posted; 35 customer acquisition centres and 9 government business centres opened.
Board has approved establishing wealth management, credit card, NRI and marketing verticals; credit card entry is being initiated.
demand_pricing: Retail, agriculture and MSME growth of about 24%, 21% and 18% respectively; management expects similar rates ahead.
Growth engines named as gold loans and SHG, with dedicated divisions reporting to an Executive Director; South India cited as a gold-loan opportunity.
Deposit products: Cent Queen mobilised ₹1,457 crore and Salary Cent Prestige ₹787 crore.
Term deposits grew about 12%; around 85% of deposits are under ₹3 crore.
Undisbursed advances about ₹5,000 crore.
ECLGS 5.0: 34,824 applications sanctioned for ₹4,646 crore; guarantees issued in 30,561 accounts for ₹4,353 crore; disbursed in 27,567 accounts for ₹3,693 crore.
Business per branch ₹185 crore; business per employee ₹24 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is capital raising planned, given the Board's approval of up to about ₹7,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% are sufficient for guidance, so no capital raise is planned currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why did LCR fall from 235% to 156% and NSFR from 147% to 128%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said excess liquidity carries a cost and has been deployed; CD ratio rose from 64% to 74%. It said LCR remains above the regulatory threshold.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments drive the 28.6% advances growth, and what protects underwriting?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate grew 46.52% from a low base. Management cited a 0.29% slippage ratio, or 0.19% excluding agriculture KCC slippage of ₹200 crore, and better post-disbursement monitoring.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for deposit repricing and FCNR mobilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Term deposits are largely repriced at a 4.60% cost of deposits. FCNR(B) mobilisation is USD8.4 million so far, with a USD400 million target by September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Average yield on the corporate book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have corporate yield data; overall yield on advances is 7.89%, up from 7.78%, and is expected to reach about 8% by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost-to-income fall below 56%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited income steps (forex and BG cells, exporter meets, insurance and LC/BG business) and cost cuts (cash retention, ATM and currency chest use, utilities), targeting a 1.5-1.6% reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for credit cards and GIFT City?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit card and wealth management verticals were approved by the Board. GIFT City targets USD200 million deposits and USD500 million trade book over several years; about ₹470 crore has been disbursed there.

risks_watch: Liquidity coverage ratio fell to 156% from 235%, and NSFR to 128% from 147%; watch for further decline as the CD ratio rises.
ECL transition from 1 April 2027 needs about ₹4,500-5,000 crore in provisioning, with about ₹1,525 crore already provided.
Corporate book concentration: corporate loans up 46.52% in a single year, so underwriting quality needs testing.
Treasury income of ₹276 crore is lower YoY on market conditions.
Segment profit data conflicts with management's explanation; the wholesale and unallocated swing was not clearly explained.
Recovery targets depend on technical write-off recoveries of ₹2,200-2,500 crore and property sales.
532885|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and assertive on growth, capital and asset quality. Management was less precise on specific figures such as corporate yield and segment profit changes, and on the segment question it deflected to “provisioning has come down.”
key_quotes: Growth is not a challenge for Central Bank of India now. We have enough capital. We have enough resources and the momentum and credit underwriting quality, post disbursement monitoring part, all these things we have taken care of.

So, comfort of having 215% and having CD ratio of 66% or 64% for any vibrant organization and growing organization, it is liability because those high-quality liquid assets and all those things comes with a cost.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Yield on advances is guided to rise from 7.89% to about 8% by March 2027, and cost of deposits fell 33 bps to 4.60%, but cost-to-income is 55.40% and treasury income fell to ₹276 crore, so NIM only holds at 3.06%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network is 4,605 branches and 13,890 BC outlets; a GIFT City branch opened 29 June 2026 and more corporate and mid-corporate branches are planned, but no count or timing was given, so the capacity add is small and unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Advances grew 28.58% YoY to ₹354,348 crore and deposits grew 11.68%; retail +23.92%, agri +21.14%, MSME +18.03%, and management expects similar rates ahead, but QoQ growth was only ~2.85%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex was discussed and management said CRAR of 18.28% and CET1 of 16.24% are sufficient, so no capital raise is planned despite the ~₹7,000 crore board approval.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held all FY27 guidance (advances 14-16%, deposits 11-12%, NIM 3%+, ROA 1%+) rather than raising it, and LCR fell to 156% from 235%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: QoQ advances growth was ~2.85% against the ~3% guided pace, and the 14-16% FY27 advances guide needs faster sequential growth; the ECL transition from 1 April 2027 needs ₹4,500-5,000 crore with ₹1,525 crore already provided.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Board approved wealth management, credit card, NRI and marketing verticals, and credit card entry is being initiated; FCNR(B) target is USD400 million by September 2026 against only USD8.4 million mobilised so far.

rows.label: Liquidity deployment and LCR decline
rows.why: LCR fell to 156% from 235% and NSFR to 128% from 147% as CD ratio rose to 74.10% from 64%; management says it will keep deploying excess liquidity, so further drop is a watch item.

rows.label: Technical write-off recoveries of ₹2,200-2,500 crore in FY27
rows.why: Recovery target is new and depends on technical write-off recoveries plus 600-700 property sales against 460 last year, so the outcome is conditional.

rows.label: Cost-to-income down 1.5-1.6% next year
rows.why: Cost-to-income is 55.40% against a target below 56%; management cites forex/BG income steps and cash, ATM and utility cost cuts, but the ratio rose slightly YoY from 55.30%.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, capital (CRAR 18.28%, no raise planned) and asset quality (GNPA 2.60%, slippage 0.29%), but less precise on corporate yield and the wholesale/unallocated segment swing; analysts pressed on the corporate book's 46.52% growth and LCR decline.

532885|2026-09.headline: Central Bank of India Q2 FY27 net profit rose 21% YoY to Rs1,469 Crore, with NIM at 3.01% and gross NPA at 2.39%.
532885|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs1,469 Crore (up 21% YoY, 11% QoQ), with operating profit of Rs2,268 Crore and NII of Rs4,146 Crore (up 26.28% YoY). Global advances grew 29.83% to Rs3,81,032 Crore and domestic deposits grew 14.41%, with CASA at 44.65%, below the 48% plus or minus 1% guidance. Asset quality improved on net NPA (0.31%) and slippage (0.24%), but credit cost rose to 0.53% as provisions were built for standard assets and ahead of ECL. Cost-to-income at 58.95% missed the sub-56% guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +21% YoY; +11% QoQ (from Rs1,213 Crore YoY base)
vs 62.42% in Q2 FY26; guidance was below 56%
guidance was above 3%; down about 5bps QoQ per analyst
+9.23% YoY; below 48% plus or minus 1% guidance

financial_highlights.metric: Yield on advances / cost of deposits

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM book Rs2,54,273 Crore, up 21%; retail Rs1,12,299 Crore (+24.49%), agriculture Rs67,778 Crore (+19.92%), MSME Rs74,196 Crore (+17.36%). RAM:corporate mix 68:32 against 65:35 plus or minus 5% guidance.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate book Rs1,18,666 Crore, up about 42-44% YoY from Rs83,000 Crore; focus on roads, infrastructure, data centres, renewables. Pipeline: Rs7,000 Crore undisbursed sanctions, Rs5,200 Crore under process, Rs11,000 Crore under consideration.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book Rs41,000 Crore at average yield above 8.5%; plan to open or customise 116 gold loan branches with TAT up to 30 minutes.

segments.name: Overseas / GIFT City
segments.commentary: GIFT City branch opened June 29, 2026, contributing overseas advances of Rs8,093 Crore. FCNR(B) raised USD 926.74 million across 731 accounts; overseas loans against it USD 794.60 million.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Yield rose to 7.19% at September 30, 2026 and was reported higher at 7.25-7.40% since; AFS book Rs1,023 Crore (from Rs843 Crore). Treasury earned Rs56 Crore from IPO participation; management sees treasury outlook as challenged.

guidance_outlook: Management says ECL requires Rs5,000-5,500 Crore in total, with Rs1,525 Crore already provided; ECL applies from April 1, 2027. Whether to take a one-time hit or stagger it is undecided.
Credit cost guided at up to 0.75% for next year as well (0.53% this quarter).
ROA expected to stay above 1%, supported by rising repo rates on 61% external-benchmark-linked book; management declined to guide beyond next year.
NIM expected to rise in a rising-rate scenario; management says margin increase is likely.
Recoveries from written-off pool (Rs31,301 Crore) targeted at Rs2,500 Crore-plus this year; aviation account expected to yield Rs700 Crore via SARFAESI in the current or next quarter.
Cost-to-income: management says efficiency numbers will improve in coming quarters, but Q2 missed the sub-56% guidance.
Business growth guidance of 14-15%, deposit growth 10-12% and advances growth 14-16% were all exceeded in Q2.
capex_capacity: GIFT City branch opened June 29, 2026.
116 gold loan branches to be opened or customised with TAT up to 30 minutes.
300 marketing officers recruited; 32 places identified for MSME credit teams; CPAC revamped for higher ticket loans.
Credit card franchise to launch around June; cash management services with two modules live and more in coming months.
New banking emerging department (NBET) set up to lead digital user experience; 45 digital journeys launched and under revision.
demand_pricing: Management said yield on advances was 7.87% and cost of deposits 4.60%; the 125bp reference rate cut in the prior year hit the book.
Gold loans, SHG linkages (26 states NRLM tie-ups) and housing (over 50% of retail advances) named as growth engines; car loans via dealer and builder tie-ups.
Average ticket size is rising for housing and car loans, per management; a Rs22 Crore green home loan was cited.
Corporate growth focus on renewable energy, roads, data centres, real estate, hospitality, NBFC and agri-food processing.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provisioning is needed and is the bank prepared?
qa_highlights.answer: Total requirement Rs5,000-5,500 Crore, with Rs1,525 Crore already provided; management is confident profits can cover the gap before April 1, 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will the one-time ECL hit go to net worth on April 1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference over Rs1,525 Crore is the remaining need; it has not decided between a one-time hit and staggering it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did provisions rise even as NPA and slippage improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited building a higher provision coverage ratio in good times and standard-asset provisions rising to Rs399 Crore from Rs37 Crore (prior year); credit cost 0.53%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROA of about 1% sustainable into FY28 and FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ROA should stay above 1% but declined to guide beyond next year given fast-changing conditions, citing El Nino and global factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why is yield on advances low versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed the 125bp reference rate cut on the 61% external-benchmark book; repo pass-through lags and yields should rise as rates increase; gold loans yield above 8.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Any stress in rural collections from El Nino or drought?
qa_highlights.answer: Management saw no distress signals this quarter, except some agri slippage in Pune; it will assess the drought impact with future data.

532891|2026-03.headline: Puravankara Q4 FY26 presales rose 190% YoY to INR3,547 crore; FY27 presales guidance set at INR11,200 crore and debt reduction target of INR750 crore.
532891|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter on sales and handovers, with presales of INR3,547 crore (up 190% YoY and 151% QoQ) and total income of INR1,541 crore (up 173% YoY) driven by 1,301 handovers. FY26 presales hit a record INR7,407 crore (up 55%) and collections a record INR4,258 crore (up 15%). Net debt was INR2,321 crore at March 31, 2026, down INR160 crore in the quarter, and cost of debt fell to 11.05%. Management guided FY27 presales of INR11,200 crore and a gross debt reduction of about INR750 crore, excluding new borrowing for business development. Collections, interest cost and FY27 delivery guidance drew the most pointed questions and several were deferred to offline follow-up.

segments.name: Residential sales
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales volume was 3.01 million sq ft (vs 1.42 million sq ft in Q4 FY25) at average realisation of INR11,787 per sq ft (up 37% YoY). FY26 volume was 7.25 million sq ft at INR10,213 per sq ft (up 21%).

segments.name: Handovers
segments.commentary: Handed over 1,301 homes (1.67 million sq ft) in Q4 FY26 and 3,747 homes (4.25 million sq ft) in FY26.

segments.name: Launches
segments.commentary: Launched three new projects (Purva SilverSky, Purva Northern Lights, Purva Estrella) and seven new phases in FY26, totalling 6.39 million sq ft. Northern Lights realisation is about INR10,700 per sq ft and it contributed INR1,100-1,200 crore to Q4 presales. Lokhandwala contributed slightly over INR800 crore in Q4.

segments.name: Commercial assets
segments.commentary: Aerocity has received OC and leasing has started; Zentech OC is expected within the month and is about 40-45% leased or sold. FY26 commercial sales and leasing was about 2.6 lakh sq ft.

segments.name: Starworth
segments.commentary: Not a reporting segment; order book is above INR2,000 crore and FY25 financials are on the website, with FY26 to follow.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales target of about INR11,200 crore, of which about 48% from sustained sales and 52% from new launches; about INR7,000 crore expected from the South and the rest from West and Commercial.
Gross debt reduction target of about INR750 crore for FY27, excluding incremental borrowing for business development; scheduled repayment is INR836 crore this year.

Collections expected to grow in double digits in FY27; management suggested 45-50% of the INR7,400 crore sales from the big launches could be collected in the first year (exact figure to be shared offline).
Estimated surplus cash flow of INR19,290 crore: INR8,816 crore from ongoing projects, INR2,131 crore from exiting commercial assets, and INR8,343 crore from the launch pipeline.
Launch pipeline of 14.85 million sq ft with GDV of INR22,547 crore; Bandra launch expected between Dussehra and Diwali after members vacate by end-June.
capex_capacity: Land bank of about 56.48 million sq ft, of which about 21 million sq ft is earmarked for the launch guidance, leaving about 35 million sq ft.

FY26 business development added over 12 million sq ft and about INR15,200 crore GDV across six projects, including Chembur (INR2,100 crore GDV), Malabar Hills (INR2,700 crore), Hennur Road JD (INR1,300 crore), Baglagere JD (INR1,000 crore), Attibele 53.5 acres (INR4,800 crore) and Northern Bengaluru JD (INR3,300 crore).
Malabar Hills: development agreement complete, registration in about 45 days, approvals expected in 9-12 months, pricing INR115,000-120,000 per sq ft on carpet area.
Two under-construction assets delivered, totalling about 2 million sq ft; FY27 residential delivery guidance to be shared offline.
Commercial: planning new verticals including data centres, warehousing and retail (about 3 lakh sq ft retail in Thane), with NCR (Delhi, Noida, Gurugram) as the expansion focus; no timelines given.
demand_pricing: Management says the Bengaluru market is steady rather than frenzied, with about 30% of the last launch sold; AI and GCC demand is seen as supportive.
NRI demand held up after the strong launch quarter; management says rupee depreciation may attract outside money but is watching global uncertainty.
Construction costs are rising about 6-7% due to diesel prices; management says margins and contingencies absorb this for now.
Project margins: new launches target above 20% gross margin (Northern Lights about 20-21%, Purva Estrella slightly above 20%); plotted development 30-40% gross margin.
Housing sales in top 8 cities were about 84,800 units, with homes above INR10 million at about 53% of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timing and confidence in the launch pipeline, including Bandra?
qa_highlights.answer: Bandra launch targeted between Dussehra and Diwali, with a GDV of about INR2,700 crore for the saleable portion. Management says most of the pipeline (INR22,547 crore) should launch despite past delays from Bengaluru approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Collection outlook for FY27 given weak YoY growth and flat Western collections?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections will grow in double digits, with about 45-50% of the FY26 sales expected to be collected in the first year; the exact figure will be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense rise to about INR600-650 crore, and how does the NCD accounting work?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the increase reflects debt raised for business development, and that fair-value accounting for some instruments adds to P&L cost. Cost on that instrument is above 11.05%. Detailed working to follow offline.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR750 crore debt reduction apply to gross or net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it refers to gross debt, with scheduled repayment of INR836 crore this year; excess collections and project-level sweeps may add to that.

qa_highlights.question: Commercial leasing traction at Zentech and Aerocity?
qa_highlights.answer: Zentech is about 40-45% leased or sold before OC; Aerocity has many GCC RFPs of over 2 million sq ft and large deals are expected in the next couple of quarters.

risks_watch: Collections: FY26 collections grew only 15% against 55% presales growth, and the company has not given a collection number for FY27.
Interest cost of about INR600-650 crore on roughly INR3,900-4,000 crore gross debt; management is to provide reconciliation offline.
Launch execution risk in Bengaluru amid approval changes (e-Khata, Greater Bengaluru Authority) and the Bandra vacation timeline.
Cost inflation of 6-7% from diesel prices and geopolitical impact on the RBI's FY27 growth outlook (6.9%).
Delivery guidance for FY27 residential and the timing of Zentech OC and Aerocity leasing remain unquantified.
532891|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on sales, launches and the FY27 presales target, but cautious on macro and cost risks. Management deferred several numerical questions (collections, interest reconciliation, FY27 delivery) to offline follow-up.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a landmark year for the company.
We are targeting a presales value of approximately INR 11,200 crores for FY26-27

On the balance sheet front, we are targeting a debt reduction of approximately INR 750 crores for FY26-27, excluding any incremental borrowing undertaken for strategic business development opportunities.

So whether it is AI, I would actually look at it as a positive thing for any place which is technology centric simply because AI also requires work and implementation and everything else that goes along with that.

down INR160 crore in the quarter; net debt-to-equity 1.31x

rows.why: Launch pipeline of 14.85 million sq ft (GDV INR22,547 crore) targets FY27 presales of INR11,200 crore, with Bandra launch between Dussehra and Diwali and Malabar Hills approvals expected in 9-12 months; land bank of 56.48 million sq ft, about 35 million sq ft unallocated after launch guidance.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 presales target of INR11,200 crore vs INR7,407 crore in FY26 (about 51% up), with 52% from new launches; FY26 sales volume was 7.25 million sq ft (up 21%) and Q4 volume was 3.01 million sq ft vs 1.42 million a year earlier.

rows.why: Land bank has about 35 million sq ft left after launch guidance and FY26 added over 12 million sq ft and INR15,200 crore GDV, but no new capex or land spend is firmly guided and commercial verticals have no timelines.

rows.why: FY27 presales target of INR11,200 crore is new and management cites 30% sold on last Bengaluru launch and strong Q4 presales of INR3,547 crore (up 190% YoY), but the call did not signal a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bengaluru approval changes (e-Khata, Greater Bengaluru Authority) could delay launches that carry most of the INR22,547 crore pipeline, and collections grew only 15% in FY26 against 55% presales growth with no FY27 collection number given.

rows.when: Q2 FY27 (Bandra between Dussehra and Diwali)
rows.why: Launch pipeline of 14.85 million sq ft and Bandra GDV of about INR2,700 crore for the saleable portion, with management saying most of the INR22,547 crore pipeline should launch despite past delays.

rows.label: Gross debt reduction of about INR750 crore in FY27
rows.why: Scheduled repayment of INR836 crore this year plus excess collections and project sweeps support the target, but FY26 collections grew only 15% and cost of debt is 11.05% on about INR3,900-4,000 crore gross debt.

rows.label: Aerocity GCC leasing deals
rows.why: Aerocity has GCC RFPs of over 2 million sq ft and management expects large deals in the next couple of quarters; Zentech is 40-45% leased or sold before OC, but FY26 commercial leasing was only about 2.6 lakh sq ft.

rows.label: Malabar Hills pricing at INR115,000-120,000 per sq ft
rows.why: Pricing guided at INR115,000-120,000 per sq ft on carpet area for a INR2,700 crore GDV project, but approvals are 9-12 months away so it sits beyond the first two to three quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on record presales, the INR11,200 crore FY27 target and the launch pipeline, but cautious on diesel-driven cost inflation and deferred collections, interest reconciliation and FY27 delivery numbers to offline follow-up, which analysts pressed on.

532891|2026-06.headline: Puravankara Q1 FY27 presales rose 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores and PAT turned positive at INR25 crores; FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated.
532891|2026-06.overview: Presales grew 28% YoY to INR1,439 crores on 9% higher volume (1.36 million sq ft) and 18% higher realisation (INR10,589/sq ft). Collections rose 40% to INR1,199 crores and 745 homes (0.94 million sq ft) were handed over. Total income rose 63% YoY to INR877 crores, EBITDA margin expanded to 25% from 15%, and PAT was INR25 crores versus a loss of INR69 crores a year earlier. Management kept FY27 presales guidance and the INR700 crores debt-reduction target, while adding four Bengaluru land opportunities (GDV ~INR5,200 crores) and signing a sale of Purva Zentech to ICICI Prudential AMC at ~INR625 crores EV.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR69 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: Reduced by INR74 crores in the quarter

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: Contributed INR1,046 crores of presales in Q1 FY27 per management. Projects cited include Northern Light and Provident Equinox.

segments.name: West & Commercial
segments.commentary: Contributed INR393 crores of presales in Q1 FY27, including ~INR200 crores from Purva Estrella (per Rajat Rastogi's estimate). Aerocity received OC for 1.3 million sq ft; Miami has RERA and is on sale.

qa_highlights.question: Why did land payment reach INR574 crores in cash flow, and what is the outlook for land spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the amount paid for the four Bengaluru acquisitions from cash on hand; no land cost is unpaid, but future development spend will be booked as construction cost, and new land purchases would add land payments.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt will come off with the ICICI Prudential AMC Purva Zentech deal, and how will proceeds be used?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR250 crores of debt on that asset will be repaid from proceeds; the rest will be evaluated for debt reduction, business development or working capital, with closing expected this month.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q2 launches (Westend, Hennur Road, Cityspire, Winworth) on track, and any approval issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Westend has RERA and is launched with good EOIs; Hennur Road delayed by Karnataka government change, clarity expected this week; Cityspire and Winworth only await RERA, expected this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR11,200 crores presales guidance and INR700 crores debt reduction still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Both held; launches slipping from Q1 moved to Q2 for one or two projects, and management said opportunity spend versus debt reduction will be reviewed from time to time.

qa_highlights.question: What margin is targeted over the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin guidance of 25-30% at portfolio level held, with product mix (plotted, JDA, outright, redevelopment) causing project-level variation.

qa_highlights.question: How much did Purva Estrella contribute to Q1 sales and how does it compare with the top projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Estrella contributed about INR200 crores in Q1 and about INR800 crores since launch; management could not confirm a separate top-three ranking, citing South's Northern Light and Provident Equinox and West's Estrella.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no zero-debt target; free cash flow will be split between new opportunities and debt, and debt is an important part of the business as the portfolio (about INR58,500 crores) grows.

qa_highlights.question: What is the leasing status and rate expectation for Purva Aerocity, and when is Phase 2?
qa_highlights.answer: OC for 1.3 million sq ft; about 2.5 million sq ft of RFPs filed with no lease signed yet; LOIs expected at INR60-65 per sq ft. Phase 2 (0.9 million sq ft) to start after 70-80% of Phase 1 is leased, possibly in the next few quarters; monetisation possible later.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales guidance of INR11,200 crores reiterated; management said it holds the number despite Q1 presales of INR1,439 crores, with 1-2 projects slipped from Q1 to Q2.
Project-wise launch guidance totals about INR27,300 crores of launches, plus about INR10,000 crores of sustenance projects; management expects some Q2 launches to slip to Q3 and Q3 to Q4.
Debt reduction target of INR700 crores for FY27 retained; gross debt fell INR74 crores in Q1 despite four new Bengaluru acquisitions.
EBITDA margin guidance of 25% to 30% at portfolio level held; Q1 printed 25%.
About INR250 crores of debt sits on Purva Zentech and will be repaid from the ICICI Prudential AMC proceeds; closing expected in August 2026.

Launch timing: Westend RERA received and launched; Cityspire, Winworth and Winworth 3 awaiting final RERA approval, expected this quarter; Hennur Road delayed by Karnataka government change; Pali Hill launch planned Oct-Nov 2026; Apna Ghar 3 and Deonar Baug in Q4.
capex_capacity: Four Bengaluru acquisitions in Q1 (about 41.93 acres, 4.23 million sq ft development potential, GDV about INR5,200 crores): JDAs at Sarjapur and Doddagubbi, land at Sanna Amanikere and Mandur; land cost fully paid, with INR574 crores land payment in cash flow funded from cash on hand.

Purva Aerocity (commercial, about 2.2 million sq ft): OC received for 1.3 million sq ft; balance 0.9 million sq ft not started, to be built in phases once 70-80% of Phase 1 is leased. RFPs filed for about 2.5 million sq ft.
New commercial project at recently acquired Hebbal land (about 1.3 million sq ft) planned to start construction by end of Q4 FY27.

Pali Hill (Mumbai) to apply for RERA by end-September 2026; launch targeted October-November. Miami RERA received in June and on sale; Apna Ghar 3 and Deonar Baug submitted for approvals, Q4 launch targeted.
Mumbai landscape of about INR25,000 crores GDV across South Bombay, Thane and Dombivli, per Rajat Rastogi; NCR (Noida) being evaluated for first land development.
demand_pricing: Q1 presales INR1,439 crores (+28% YoY): South INR1,046 crores; West & Commercial INR393 crores, including about INR200 crores from Purva Estrella. Estrella cumulative sales about INR800 crores since launch.
Volume 1.36 million sq ft (+9% YoY) and realisation INR10,589 per sq ft (+18% YoY); management says growth was not reliant on one lever.
South demand described as steady with no slowdown; growth expected to be lower than 2024-25 levels, with well-priced, well-designed branded products doing well.
Mumbai and Pune: branded players gaining share; Purva Miami in Breach Candy drew encouraging ultra-luxury response; demand expected to build into festive season.
Aerocity lease rate expected around INR60-65 per sq ft via LOIs; GCC and large-company RFP interest reported.
risks_watch: Launch slippage: Hennur Road delayed by Karnataka government change; several RERA approvals still pending for Q2 launches, and the guidance relies on about INR27,300 crores of project launches.
Presales guidance of INR11,200 crores needs about INR9,761 crores in Q2-Q4 (implied by Q1 INR1,439 crores); requires sustained launch cadence.

Debt: net debt INR2,836 crores, net debt to equity 1.57x, average cost of debt 11.12%; management has not committed to a timeline beyond the INR700 crores FY27 reduction target and says new opportunities may take priority.
Aerocity leasing: no signed leases yet on 2.2 million sq ft asset; Phase 2 timing depends on 70-80% pre-leasing.

Cash flow: Q1 land spend of INR574 crores and capital deployed into new Bengaluru and Mumbai pipeline; watch whether Purva Zentech proceeds (about INR625 crores EV, INR250 crores debt repayment) close in August 2026.
Q1 profitability: PAT of INR25 crores is linked to handover-driven revenue recognition; management itself cautioned against reading a single quarter as a trend.
key_quotes: Puravankara has entered FY27 with a stronger operating rhythm.
One quarter does not define an earnings trajectory, particularly in a business where revenue recognition depends on completion, handovers and project mix.
We are giving guidance as a project-wise.
So we do not have any such guidance towards saying that we are going to become 0 debt in the next 2 years or 3 years, and we think that the debt is an important part of the business.

532891|2026-09.headline: Puravankara Q2 FY27 presales rose 109% YoY to INR2,762 crores, with net debt cut by INR470 crores to INR2,366 crores.

Customer collections grew 24% to INR1,301 crores, and net debt fell to INR2,366 crores, with net debt-to-equity at 1.26x. Management says collections from the large new launches will follow as construction milestones are hit, and that the launch pipeline remains on track for FY27 guidance of INR11,200 crores, with some South and West launches possibly slipping into FY28.
