532892|2026-03.headline: MOFSL FY26 operating PAT rose 16% YoY to ₹2,360 crores; Q4 operating PAT up 25% with a ₹661 crore exit run rate.
532892|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 operating PAT of ₹2,360 crores (+16% YoY), with Q4 operating PAT up 25% and the strongest of the four quarters. Asset and Private Wealth businesses grew profit 33% and now contribute about 50% of operating PAT, with Asset Management at 33% of group operating PAT versus 26% in FY25. Reported PAT including OCI was hit by notional MTM losses of about ₹1,000 crores on a ~₹9,000 crore investment book, which management said were largely recouped in April 2026. Long-term credit rating was upgraded to AA+ (stable). Q&A focused on SIP and MF flow share, yield compression from product mix, MTF and broking trajectory, digital broker competition, and treasury MTM.

532892|2026-09.headline: Motilal Oswal Q2FY27 operating PAT rose 29% YoY to ₹718 crore, led by Asset & Private Wealth, which grew 43% YoY.
532892|2026-09.overview: Operating PAT grew 29% YoY to ₹718 crore, with Asset & Private Wealth Management up 43% and now contributing about 58% of operating PAT. AUM for Asset Management plus MO Alternates reached ₹2.23 lakh crore, and PWM AUM reached ₹2.96 lakh crore (up 58% YoY). Management said broking headwinds from regulation and flat markets are in the base and that H2FY27 growth should be higher. The company received a SEBI custodian licence in Q2 and plans to launch the custody business in Q4FY27, with no material contribution expected in FY28.

532893|2026-03.headline: VTM Ltd FY26 PAT fell about 75% to Rs 11 crore on US tariff discounts (~Rs 20 crore), with FY27 turnover guided up 12-14% and EBITDA margin targeted at 10-11%.
532893|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue growth of about 8% (base ~Rs 372 crore) but PAT of about Rs 11 crore, down roughly 75% YoY. The drop was attributed to an ~18% US tariff-related discount (~Rs 20 crore), chargeback discounts (~Rs 8 crore), a Rs 2.3 crore forex MTM loss on PCFC borrowings, a gratuity provision under the new Labour Code, and ~15% higher raw material costs. FY26 EBITDA margin was 7.43%, and management said the 18% discount to the US customer Quince is still in place, with negotiations ongoing and the current price point at about 10%. Management guided to 12-14% FY27 top-line growth, a 10-11% EBITDA margin, and a 6.5 million-unit order backlog as of 31 May.

New customers in the UK, Europe, Middle East, Japan and Australia; onboarding takes about one year, with results expected in 2-3 quarters.

Home textiles outsourcing is increasing; commodity items may be outsourced to cut costs and expand volume.

US tariff rose to ~50-60% at one point and then settled at 18%; the company shared ~10% of the tariff burden with the customer through a discount of 18% that is still in place, against a current tariff of 10%.

Customer price sensitivity is elevated post-tariff; management cited the tariff, the war and oil price shocks as exogenous hits.
Input costs: raw material up ~15% due to the war and cotton futures moving to 78 cents from ~69-70 cents; bleaching, job work and freight costs also rose.
Working capital: payables held to 45-60 days; the company says it pays vendors within 45 days to comply with MSME rules.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 operating margin return to FY25 levels of ~19% EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: uncertain. FY26 was 7.43%; target is 10-11%. CMD said 19% is pre-tariff and may be a stretch in the post-tariff era.

qa_highlights.question: What is peak revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said greige runs at 80-83% utilisation so ~80% is the practical ceiling. Management said the top line would reach ~Rs 420 crore at peak, with a Rs 500-600 crore run-rate possible with the right mix and outsourcing.

qa_highlights.question: How is the margin split between greige and home textiles?
qa_highlights.answer: Greige fabric earns a traditional 7-9% margin. The EBITDA drop is mainly from home textiles, where the ~Rs 20 crore tariff-linked price cut was the main hit, plus gratuity (Rs 41 lakh) and PF settlement (Rs 32 lakh) costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 18% discount still in place when US tariffs have fallen to 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount is still in place, the customer is more price sensitive post-tariff, and negotiations are ongoing; pipeline sales carry the earlier tariff.

qa_highlights.question: Why are payables so low compared with group companies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CMD said both companies are cash-rich and pay vendors within 30-45 days, so terms are not favourable to group entities. Pacific Cotton is a separate US entity selling basic lower-value Amazon-brand items.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 discounting fall from Rs 13.7 crore to Rs 2.3 crore, yet gross margin is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: gross margin is unchanged; Q4 PBT Rs 4.1 crore vs Rs 4.87 crore in Q3, with the gap from strategy consultant costs, the PF settlement and a Rs 62 lakh Canadian liability.

532898|2026-03.headline: POWERGRID delivered ₹28,206 crore capitalisation and ~₹40,000 crore capex in FY26, guiding FY27 capex to ₹37,000 crore and capitalisation to ₹30,000 crore.
532898|2026-03.overview: Management said FY26 capex (close to ₹40,000 crore against an initial ₹28,000 crore guide) and capitalisation (₹28,206 crore against a ₹25,000 crore commitment) both beat guidance. Standalone PAT rose 4% to about ₹15,921 crore and consolidated PAT rose 3% to about ₹15,928 crore, with total income of ₹47,684 crore versus ₹47,459 crore. Management flagged a natural RTM revenue decline as assets reach 12 years, offset by FY26 capitalisation that it expects to flow into FY27 revenue. The pipeline was described as ₹1.7 lakh crore of works in hand and ₹1.1 lakh crore under bidding, with new avenues in BESS, integrated storage under Section 62, and the first international PPP in Kenya.

segments.name: TBCB (tariff-based competitive bidding)
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 81% of the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand (₹1.37 lakh crore). Management said FY26 saw 9 TBCB wins out of 28 projects floated, at a total tariff of about 44% share.

segments.name: RTM (regulated tariff mechanism)
segments.commentary: Works in hand of about ₹28,000 crore. Revenue is on a natural downward trajectory after assets complete 12 years, offset in FY26 by ~₹1,700 crore of depreciation-related gaps covered by other income items.

segments.name: Telecom
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,195 crore; first 400G interface in India, first international long-distance link to Bhutan, and a 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible in the next quarter.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Revenue of ₹1,755 crore versus ₹799 crore in FY25, with 39 domestic orders and 62 ongoing projects, and 8 international orders across 25 countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 capex expected above ₹40,000 crore, with management indicating a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range.
FY27 capitalisation guidance of up to ₹30,000 crore initially; FY28 capitalisation expected to move to about ₹35,000 crore.
FY27 expected to show full revenue benefit of FY26 capitalisation, which came mainly in the later part of FY26.
Management said FY27-FY28 earnings growth is likely to be better than the last three years when asked directly; it did not quantify this.
Integrated storage (BESS) capacity target not yet given; management said numbers would follow once Section 62 regulatory clarity emerges.
Pang-Kaithal HVDC project excluded from the ₹1.7 lakh crore works in hand pending Government of India review.
capex_capacity: Capitalisation of 4,765 ckm of transmission lines and 72,055 MVA of substation capacity added in FY26; 9 new substations taking the total to 291, and total transmission lines at 1.84 lakh ckm and 624 GVA transformation capacity at 31 March 2026.

Transformer and reactor manufacturing capacity in India is about 300 GVA against demand of 400+ GVA a year; the company is moving to bulk procurement and project timelines were extended to 26-30+ months from 18 months.
Gross fixed assets crossed ₹3 lakh crore; 11 HVDC projects are running with about 101 GW of the 120 GW inter-regional capacity.
New substations commissioned include Bhadla, Ramgarh/Dausa (8 months from foundation), Bikaner-3, KPS-2, KPS-3, Narela and Ananthapuram.
Pilot 1,000-rack data centre at Manesar expected to be visible within the next quarter; 220 kV mobile GIS in place, with 132 kV and 400 kV mobile GIS expected within this calendar year.
demand_pricing: Works in hand ₹1.7 lakh crore (TBCB ₹1.37 lakh crore, RTM ₹28,000 crore, others ₹4,200 crore), excluding Pang-Kaithal HVDC.

Under-bidding pipeline of ₹1.1 lakh crore, including ₹5,270 crore of intra-State; major projects include Barmer Phase 4, Vizag Green Hydrogen, Jam Khambhaliya, Krishnagiri, Lakadia, ERWR and Nawada-Durgapur.
Management cited a ₹7.9 lakh crore opportunity under the 900+ GW by 2036 anchor programme and ₹6.4 lakh crore from Brahmaputra basin hydro; 22 HVDC schemes (127 GW) are in planning or bidding.
Intra-State TBCB thresholds are ₹150-250 crore by state; the smallest project POWERGRID has bid was about ₹60 crore.
Management said electricity share in the energy basket is about 22% and is expected to rise, supporting transmission demand.

On competition, management said it bids on risk-return framework and declined to quantify changes in TBCB tariff or IRR; equity IRR guidance of 11-13% was described as possibly better, with change-in-law as a cost pass-through.

qa_highlights.question: Reason for the Q4 FY26 EBITDA decline and whether new TBCB projects use service concession accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to the natural RTM tariff dip after 12 years of asset life; new BOOT-method TBCB projects are accounted for using the financial lease model.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and commissioning expectations for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex initial guidance of about ₹37,000 crore; FY28 expected beyond ₹40,000 crore, in a ₹40,000-45,000 crore range. Capitalisation guided at ₹30,000 crore for FY27 and about ₹35,000 crore for FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Gross block versus NCT cost variance on projects and inflation indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: No project-level variance was given; management said costs are factored into bids and surprises such as force majeure and change in law are addressed under the Transmission Service Agreement.

qa_highlights.question: Market share and whether competitive intensity in TBCB is rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has bid TBCB for about 14 years and selects projects by risk-return framework rather than volume; it did not indicate a change in intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Equity IRR on TBCB projects given cost inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said returns could be better than the 11-13% range, as cost-plus RTM rewards cost but TBCB rewards efficiency, and change-in-law provisions protect against surprises.

qa_highlights.question: Phasing of capex and capitalisation in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing depends on individual project completions, expects an even spread across quarters, and noted that the Q4-heavy FY26 was incidental.

qa_highlights.question: Regulated equity on standalone and consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Regulated equity exists only in standalone; TBCB projects have no regulated equity.

risks_watch: Revenue dip as RTM assets reach 12 years of life, with management noting FY26 ~₹1,700 crore gap covered by other items; FY27 revenue depends on capitalisation flow-through.
Equipment supply constraints: transformer and reactor capacity of ~300 GVA against 400+ GVA demand; project delays from procurement and labour shortages.
Right-of-way and compensation: market-rate determination via three valuers introduced; resolution timelines unclear.
Cost inflation on TBCB projects where bids may not fully reflect rising conductor, transformer, land and interest costs; reliance on change-in-law recovery.
Intra-State payment security and right-of-way risk versus ISTS; PRAAPTI portal extension to intra-State is pending.
Monitor SPV consolidation (28 SPVs in process) and the timing of the ₹1.1 lakh crore bidding pipeline, which management said could slip by a couple of months.

532898|2026-06.headline: POWERGRID Q1 FY27 PAT flat at Rs 3,598 crore (vs Rs 3,631 crore QoQ) as regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore offset Rs 790 crore transmission-charge growth.
532898|2026-06.overview: Consolidated transmission charges rose 3% QoQ to Rs 10,905 crore and total income to Rs 11,697 crore, but PAT was Rs 3,598 crore against Rs 3,631 crore in the prior quarter. Management attributed the flat profit to a ~Rs 560 crore regulatory drag: Rs 330 crore lower depreciation/interest recovery and Rs 230 crore of interest on provisional-vs-final tariff differential that is no longer available, plus a Rs 33 crore one-off write-back (KSK Mahanadi) in the base quarter. Capitalisation of Rs 5,277 crore in Q1 was about 3.1x the prior-year Q1 figure of Rs 1,683 crore, against a FY27 guidance of Rs 30,000 crore. Receivable days fell to about 12 from 19.41, with Rs 11,404 crore realised against Rs 10,963 crore billed.

segments.name: Transmission (regulated RTM and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Transmission charges up Rs 790 crore from new assets, offset by regulatory drag of ~Rs 560 crore; TBCB operational equity investment rose to Rs 9,965 crore from Rs 4,671 crore a year earlier, funded through internal accruals.

segments.name: Consultancy
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 252 crore; 16 domestic and 3 international orders, footprint in about 25 countries.

segments.name: Telecom (PowerTel)
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 391 crore; connectivity extended to Andaman and Nicobar and first international link to Nepal; 100% backbone availability claimed.

FY27 capitalisation guidance Rs 30,000 crore; Q1 at Rs 5,277 crore, with Koppal, Gadag and Bidar-Maheshwaram projects expected to be commissioned later.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the regulatory drag in depreciation and revenue this quarter, and how will it evolve as 2014-16 assets age?
qa_highlights.answer: Management quantified the drag at about Rs 560 crore for Q1: Rs 330 crore depreciation/interest and Rs 230 crore interest on the CERC differential. It said assets capitalised about 12 years ago will continue to weigh, and framed this as part of the regulatory characteristic.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PAT flat if the change is profit-neutral, and what is the adjusted base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs 230 crore interest on the provisional-vs-final differential is no longer available and a Rs 33 crore write-back (KSK Mahanadi) in the prior quarter does not recur. It said the regulatory differential is the major factor, with a small depreciation/interest mismatch versus notional figures.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Rs 13,000 crore TBCB equity funded, and what is the Rs 7.9 lakh crore transmission capex timeline and land cost treatment?
qa_highlights.answer: All TBCB equity is funded from internal accruals with no parent-level debt. Management said the Rs 7.9 lakh crore to 2035-36 would be bid over the next 3-4 years and excludes land compensation under new MoP guidelines, which Delhi, Haryana and Gujarat have adopted.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Barmer HVDC award and BESS opportunity under the regulated route?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bids for the Rajasthan Phase IV Barmer Complex HVDC are submitted and under evaluation by the bid process coordinator, with no award date yet. On BESS, it said petitions have been filed before the regulator after NR and WR RPC consent, with timing dependent on regulator and stakeholder positions.

qa_highlights.question: Can TBCB consolidated revenue, EBITDA and PAT be disclosed separately, and what returns are earned on operational TBCB equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a separate TBCB P&L or return figure. It said returns are calibrated across multiple projects and that it will examine better disclosures, while noting regulatory disclosures are already made.

532899|2026-03.headline: Kaveri Seed FY26 revenue rose 16.25% to INR 1,303.77 crore, but PAT grew only 6.8% to INR 283.26 crore; management guides FY27 revenue growth of 15-20%.
532899|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations rose 6.84% YoY to INR 82.21 crore and the net loss narrowed to INR 25.65 crore from INR 29.25 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 16.25% to INR 1,303.77 crore, EBITDA rose 8.34% to INR 349.75 crore, and PAT rose 6.8% to INR 283.26 crore. Growth came from maize, hybrid rice, selection rice, exports and new cotton hybrids. Management said inventory is elevated by design, with higher yields and a deliberate buffer, and that FY27 growth will be volume-led because price increases are unlikely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about 17% when sales grew about 16%, and will the buffer persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was raised on purpose to hold buffer stock amid last year's competition for production areas; yields of 5-7% higher also added to inventory. Management said inventory is not a concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other current liabilities and customer advances fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Advances were INR 75-80 crore lower YoY because farmer cash flows are tight and the company has not pushed advances, which would require higher incentives, as margins have shrunk.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be driven by volume or price, and what margin is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth will be volume-led with no price hikes; revenue guided at 15-20%, cotton above 20%. Lower production costs and stable other costs should lift margins; management did not give a specific margin figure.

qa_highlights.question: Are write-offs a risk on older cotton seed inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most inventory is new production with about 1.3-1.5 years of age against a 3-year cotton seed life, so write-off risk is low and any leftover stock will be used next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for maize in kharif, given high channel inventory and El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Kharif sentiment is weak, with sideways trend tied to El Nino uncertainty and fertiliser shortage; rabi is positive, and the company expects to grow in kharif by targeting new pockets.

qa_highlights.question: How are the Kaveri and Aditya brands positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya and Genomix are wholly owned subsidiaries that market B2B hybrids from R&D; Kaveri focuses on its main product line, and the subsidiaries sell different products but may compete among themselves.

532899|2026-06.headline: Kaveri Seed Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 815 crore from Rs 945 crore (about -14%) on a weak El Nino monsoon, with EBITDA margin held near 35%.
532899|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 815 crore against Rs 945 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA at Rs 285 crore (vs Rs 332 crore) and net profit at Rs 271.3 crore (vs Rs 316 crore) as stated on the call. Management attributed the decline to a delayed, deficient monsoon that shortened the sowing window, cutting maize sales in Karnataka and weakening demand in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Cotton was flat YoY at Rs 213.43 crore while non-cotton was Rs 601.57 crore, and new products gained share in cotton and maize. Management said the quarter's margin was helped by lower production cost (down 4-5%) and that inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY, prompting lower production next year.

financial_highlights.change: same as last year, management said slightly above
about Rs 265-270 crore as of 30 June

segments.name: Cotton
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 213.43 crore, flat YoY. New cotton products were 37% of cotton sales vs 22% last year; North India (Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) roughly doubled from a small base, while Gujarat and Maharashtra were hit by low rain and illegal Bt seed.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Sales fell sharply (about 40% decline per analyst question, not disputed by management); Karnataka sowing was about one-fifth done by mid-June. New single-cross hybrids are over 20% of maize sales.

segments.name: Hybrid rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 247.07 crore, the largest non-cotton segment. Two new hybrids KRH7344 and KRH7227 launched this season contributed 62% of new-product sales in rice.

segments.name: Selection rice
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 159.07 crore, marginal YoY growth despite poor rain in rice sowing areas.

segments.name: Bajra
segments.commentary: New hybrids are 65% of Bajra volumes, up from 61%.

segments.name: Vegetables
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 15.08 crore; management called it a small segment with some spillover possible in Q2 if rain improves.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the rest of FY27 quarters to be higher than the prior year's comparable quarters, with Karnataka recovery and Rabi maize supporting H2; the Q1 revenue gap is expected to narrow but no full recovery was committed.
Management said Q2 margins would be lower than Q1 margins, and that the YoY revenue gap would narrow, not turn positive, within FY27.
Karnataka Kharif recovery: about 1,500 tonnes sold this year vs about 2,600 tonnes last year, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore (figures given inconsistently on the call).
Export target of Rs 100 crore in vegetables and other crops within about 3 years; export margin expected at 25-30%, in line with current levels.
Management reiterated a long-term growth target of 15-18% (earlier referenced as 18-20%) over the next 2-3 years, with growth expected to return to last year's level.
Cash expected to rise only by about Rs 20-30 crore by Q2 to close to Rs 300 crore; any buyback is subject to a Board decision, with no amount decided.
capex_capacity: Inventory is up about Rs 200 crore YoY because production was taken up on expectations of a good El Nino-era season; management said production will be reduced next year.
Cost of production is down 4-5% YoY while dealer-level realisations are down 2-3%; management said FY28 production will be minimal and cost per unit should stay at last year's level.
Product pipeline described as among the best in 10 years, with Madhya Pradesh hybrids newer and not yet at scale.
demand_pricing: Monsoon deficit to June 15 shortened the Kharif sowing window and farmers bought fewer premium products; Karnataka tanks now filling after July rains, which management expects to support maize in Q2-Q3.
Maize price rose to about Rs 27-28 from Rs 16-17 at the start of the season, which management expects to support Rabi demand.
Cotton MRP is government-capped; management said Kaveri realises higher prices than many peers in the top three cotton segments.
Competition: illegal Bt cotton and smaller players have grown; management said no new hybrids from peers have taken share in the last 3-4 years, and that Kaveri has lost cotton share over 7-8 years.
Management said subsidiaries (sales of about 10-12 lakh cotton packets this year) operate as separate competitors, and that their revenue is booked independently.

qa_highlights.question: Why has profit not crossed the ~Rs 300 crore peak of 2014-15 despite non-cotton growth, and what can be achieved in 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cotton was about 90% of mix in 2014-15 at high margins versus about 20% now, with cotton margins shrunk; FY27 was a one-off weather year and should not be a benchmark.

qa_highlights.question: Is Kaveri losing focus on cotton given illegal seed, price caps and no new cotton hybrids; what about the inventory build of about Rs 1,200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted cotton share was lost over 7-8 years, said new hybrids were developed in the last 3-4 years, and said inventory is about Rs 200 crore higher YoY due to over-anticipated El Nino season; production will be reduced next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins not fall with lower sales, and is any crop's margin lower than last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin slightly expanded; gross margin up 2-3%, with higher employee and other costs as people were deployed ahead of an expected good season.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiaries selling seeds alongside Kaveri, and what is the new-product definition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said subsidiaries are independent competitors that take discarded me-too hybrids; about 10-12 lakh cotton packets sold through subsidiaries this year. New products are those launched within the last 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did maize fall about 40% when peers grew, and what about Karnataka recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak rain in Karnataka, Andhra and Telangana (25-30% of last year's Kharif sales came from Karnataka) and no Madhya Pradesh or Maharashtra presence; Karnataka sales were about 1,500 tonnes vs 2,600 tonnes, a gap of 1,100-1,200 tonnes worth about Rs 40-60 crore.

532899|2026-09.headline: Kaveri Seed Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 29.84% to Rs 1,040 crore (Rs 1,040.44 cr) with EBITDA margin 30.48%, net profit Rs 96.61 cr...
532899|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 1,040.44 crore, up 29.84% YoY, with EBITDA of Rs 315.88 crore at a 30.48% margin and net profit of Rs 96.61 crore (versus a Rs 6.47 crore loss a year earlier for net loss narrowing reference in the call). Standalone Q2 revenue was Rs 286.68 crore (about 13.32% decline) per the call's segment figures, with cotton revenue down 12.12% and non-cotton revenue up 29%; the transcript's figures are internally inconsistent in places and should be verified against the filing. Maize was the largest drag: revenue fell about 36.3% in the first half, partly due to a monsoon-related sowing shortfall and delayed onset, while non-cotton products grew with new hybrids in vegetables and rice. Management said cotton volume pressure is tied to illegal Bt cotton seed sales and that the company is shifting toward new hybrid cotton products, with 85-90% of the cotton portfolio expected to come from new hybrids over 3-4 years. Management flagged elevated maize and rice inventory (Rs 150 crore plus higher than last year) and higher cash-to-payables timing effects, and said export expansion into Bangladesh, Philippines, Indonesia, Tanzania and others is aimed at building its own brand.

532900|2026-03.headline: Paisalo posted record Q4 FY26 PAT of Rs.722 million, up 56% YoY, with AUM up 17% to Rs.61,009 million.
532900|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 35% YoY to Rs.2,609 million and net interest income rose 61% YoY to Rs.1,733 million, driving a record quarterly PAT. FY26 PAT was Rs.2,372 million, with total income up 22% and NII up 29%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 0.76% and NNPA at 0.61%, and cost of borrowing eased to 10.22%. Management reaffirmed a three-year guidance to double AUM, income and net profit, and said co-lending is excluded from that base.

segments.commentary: Food and hospitality 24%, Agri and allied agri 14%, street vendors 14%, heavy industries 11%, technology 8%, health and education 5%, textiles 4%, vehicles 3%, others 17%. MSME/SME 71%, income generation 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Can NIM be sustained at current levels given higher loan yields and lower borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 NIM was 6.83%, above prior guidance, and it targets about 6.5% in FY27 while hoping to overachieve.

qa_highlights.question: What trends are seen in SME and overall book in April and May amid the war situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Stress is concentrated in large SMEs and mid-corporates with export exposure, hit by insurance, freight and Strait of Hormuz flow issues (about 5% capacity). Paisalo has no large concentrated exposure; LCC segment may see difficulty this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Update on co-lending expansion with State Bank of India?
qa_highlights.answer: Paisalo has completed its RBI-circular compliance on both methods; one is expected live within Q1 FY27 and the other awaits the bank's compliance confirmation, expected by end of Q1 or early Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How are NPAs recognised and what is recovery on collateral?
qa_highlights.answer: NPAs are recognised under RBI IRAC norms on both secured and unsecured books. Secured lending uses 50-60% LTV, with recovery typically covering principal plus cost of funds; only NIM is lost, not principal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the three-year doubling guidance still intact given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management reaffirmed doubling AUM income and net profit over the next three fiscal years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters increase their stake this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoters raised stake by about 4.7% last fiscal year after warrants of Rs.180 crore and 5% creeping acquisition earlier; management declined to comment on FY27 plans.

qa_highlights.question: How is collection efficiency at 98.5% achieved despite industry MFI stress, and is inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited a 'lend right, collect tight' philosophy with credit processes designed for elimination rather than servicing. It confirmed active scouting for inorganic opportunities and partners.

qa_highlights.question: Which new products will drive FY27 revenue, and why was QoQ disbursement growth low?
qa_highlights.answer: Six new segments have about 18-20 partnerships, to be scaled in FY27 with roughly three sub-products per category over time. Reported QoQ disbursement growth was 3%, with Q3 to Q4 growth of about 27% and FY26 growth about 15%.

532900|2026-06.headline: Paisalo Q1 FY27: record disbursement of Rs.17,309 million (+128% YoY), PAT up 30% to Rs.613 million, gross NPA 0.70%.
532900|2026-06.overview: Management, represented solely by Deputy MD Santanu Agarwal (CFO unavailable), reported AUM of Rs.67,074 million (+28% YoY) and a record quarterly disbursement of Rs.17,309 million. Total income rose 19% YoY to Rs.2,603 million and PAT rose 30% YoY to Rs.613 million, with gross NPA at 0.70% and net NPA at 0.49%. Management set a three-year ambition to roughly double AUM, income and profitability, and launched a Rs.300 crore NCD tranche under a Rs.900 crore shelf. Sequential metrics were weaker in several places: interest expense rose and opex fell sharply QoQ, and loan-loss provisions jumped, which management attributed to timing and settlement effects.

segments.commentary: Touch points rose to 5,995 across 23 states from 5,299 a quarter earlier (+696 over four quarters per management). BC franchise crossed USD 1 billion gross transaction value.

532923|2026-06.headline: Renaissance Global Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR690 crores and PAT jumped 288% to INR26 crores, but management guided revenue down as low-return customers are exited.

Owned-brand revenue grew 29% to INR89 crores and owned-brand EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 10%. Working capital days fell to 220 from 253 YoY. Management said it will exit low-return customer businesses in the customer brands segment, which lowers revenue run-rate by INR400 crores by year-end, while it targets bottom-line growth above 30% for FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management rationalised a wide licence portfolio, exiting NFL, Netflix, Harry Potter and others, with exit costs taken. It expects growth and margin recovery to 14-15% from focusing on Disney.
